verses.1:1: In the beginning God created the heavens and the earth.
verses.1:2: Now the earth was formless and empty, and darkness was over the face of the deep, and the Spirit of God was hovering over the face of the waters.
verses.1:3: Then God said, "Let there be light," and light came to be.
verses.1:4: God saw the light, that it was good, and God made a division between the light and the darkness.
verses.1:5: God named the light "day," and the darkness He named "night." And there was evening, and there was morning: one day.
verses.1:6: Then God said, "Let there be an expanse in the middle of the waters, and let it make a division between waters and waters."
verses.1:7: So God made the expanse, and He made a division between the waters that were below the expanse and the waters that were above the expanse; and it was so.
verses.1:8: God named the expanse "heavens." And there was evening, and there was morning: a second day.
verses.1:9: Then God said, "Let the waters below the heavens be gathered into one place, and let the dry land appear"; and it was so.
verses.1:10: God named the dry land "earth," and the collection of the waters He named "seas"; and God saw that it was good.
verses.1:11: Then God said, "Let the earth sprout vegetation: plants yielding seed, and fruit trees producing fruit according to their kind, whose seed is in them, on the earth"; and it was so.
verses.1:12: The earth brought forth vegetation: plants yielding seed according to their kind, and trees producing fruit whose seed is in them, according to their kind. And God saw that it was good.
verses.1:13: And there was evening, and there was morning: a third day.
verses.1:14: Then God said, "Let there be lights in the expanse of the heavens to make a division between the day and the night, and let them serve as signs and for appointed times, and for days and years;
verses.1:15: and let them serve as lights in the expanse of the heavens to shine light on the earth"; and it was so.
verses.1:16: God made the two great lights, the greater light to govern the day and the smaller light to govern the night, and also the stars.
verses.1:17: And God set them in the expanse of the heavens to shine light on the earth,
verses.1:18: and to govern the day and the night, and to make a division between the light and the darkness. And God saw that it was good.
verses.1:19: And there was evening, and there was morning: a fourth day.
verses.1:20: Then God said, "Let the waters teem with teeming living creatures, and let birds fly above the earth across the face of the expanse of the heavens."
verses.1:21: God created the great sea creatures and every moving living creature with which the waters teemed, according to their kinds, and every bird of wing according to its kind; and God saw that it was good.
verses.1:22: And God blessed them, saying, "Bear fruit and increase, and fill the waters in the seas, and let the birds increase on the earth."
verses.1:23: And there was evening, and there was morning: a fifth day.
verses.1:24: Then God said, "Let the earth bring forth living creatures according to their kind: livestock, crawling creatures, and wild animals of the earth according to their kind"; and it was so.
verses.1:25: God made the wild animals of the earth according to their kind, and the livestock according to their kind, and every crawling creature of the ground according to its kind. And God saw that it was good.
verses.1:26: Then God said, "Let Us make humanity in Our image, after Our likeness, and let them have dominion over the fish of the sea and over the birds of the heavens and over the livestock and over all the earth and over every crawling creature that crawls on the earth."
verses.1:27: So God created humanity in His image; in the image of God He created him; male and female He created them.
verses.1:28: And God blessed them, and God said to them, "Bear fruit and increase, and fill the earth and subdue it; and have dominion over the fish of the sea and over the birds of the heavens and over every living creature that crawls on the earth."
verses.1:29: Then God said, "Look, I have given you every plant yielding seed that is on the face of all the earth, and every tree that has in it the fruit of a tree yielding seed; they will be food for you.
verses.1:30: And to every wild animal of the earth and to every bird of the heavens and to everything that crawls on the earth, everything that has a living soul in it, I have given every green plant for food"; and it was so.
verses.1:31: God saw all that He had made, and look, it was very good. And there was evening, and there was morning: the sixth day.
verses.2:1: So the heavens and the earth were completed, and all their array.
verses.2:2: On the seventh day God completed His work that He had done, and on the seventh day He ceased from all His work that He had done.
verses.2:3: Then God blessed the seventh day and made it holy, because on it He ceased from all His work that God had created and made.
verses.2:4: These are the generations of the heavens and the earth when they were created, in the day that the LORD God made earth and heavens.
verses.2:5: Now no shrub of the field was yet on the earth, and no plant of the field had yet sprung up, for the LORD God had not sent rain on the earth, and there was no man to work the ground.
verses.2:6: But a mist would rise from the earth and water the whole face of the ground.
verses.2:7: Then the LORD God formed the man, dust from the ground, and blew into his nostrils the breath of life, and the man became a living creature.
verses.2:8: And the LORD God planted a garden in Eden, toward the east, and He set there the man whom He had formed.
verses.2:9: Out of the ground the LORD God made every tree grow that is pleasing to the sight and good for food, with the tree of life in the middle of the garden, and the tree of the knowledge of good and evil.
verses.2:10: A river was flowing out of Eden to water the garden, and from there it divided and became four headstreams.
verses.2:11: The name of the first is Pishon; it is the one that encircles the whole land of Havilah, where there is gold.
verses.2:12: The gold of that land is good; bdellium and onyx stone are there.
verses.2:13: The name of the second river is Gihon; it is the one that encircles the whole land of Cush.
verses.2:14: The name of the third river is Tigris; it is the one that flows east of Assyria. And the fourth river is the Euphrates.
verses.2:15: Then the LORD God took the man and settled him in the garden of Eden to work it and to guard it.
verses.2:16: And the LORD God commanded the man, saying, "From every tree of the garden you may freely eat,
verses.2:17: but from the tree of the knowledge of good and evil you must not eat, for on the day that you eat from it you will certainly die."
verses.2:18: Then the LORD God said, "It is not good for the man to be alone; I will make for him a helper corresponding to him."
verses.2:19: So out of the ground the LORD God formed every animal of the field and every bird of the heavens, and He brought them to the man to see what he would call each one; and whatever the man called each living creature, that was its name.
verses.2:20: The man gave names to all the livestock, and to the birds of the heavens, and to every animal of the field; but for Adam there was not found a helper corresponding to him.
verses.2:21: So the LORD God brought a deep sleep over the man, and he fell asleep; then He took one of his ribs and closed up flesh in its place.
verses.2:22: The LORD God built the rib that He had taken from the man into a woman, and He brought her to the man.
verses.2:23: Then the man said, "This time this one is bone from my bones and flesh from my flesh; this one will be called 'woman,' because this one was taken out of man."
verses.2:24: Therefore a man will leave his father and his mother and cling to his wife, and they will become one flesh.
verses.2:25: And the two of them were naked, the man and his wife, and they felt no shame.
verses.3:1: Now the serpent was more shrewd than any animal of the field that the LORD God had made. He said to the woman, "Is it really so that God said, 'You must not eat from any tree of the garden'?"
verses.3:2: The woman said to the serpent, "We may eat from the fruit of the trees of the garden,
verses.3:3: but from the fruit of the tree that is in the middle of the garden, God has said, 'You must not eat from it, and you must not touch it, or you will die.'"
verses.3:4: The serpent said to the woman, "You certainly will not die!
verses.3:5: Because God knows that on the day you eat from it, your eyes will open, and you will become like God, knowing good and evil."
verses.3:6: When the woman saw that the tree was good for food, and that it was a delight to the eyes, and that the tree was desirable for gaining insight, she took from its fruit and ate; and she also gave some to her husband with her, and he ate.
verses.3:7: Then the eyes of both of them were opened, and they knew that they were naked; so they sewed fig leaves together and made coverings for themselves.
verses.3:8: Then they heard the sound of the LORD God walking about in the garden at the breeze of the day, and the man and his wife hid from the LORD God's presence among the trees of the garden.
verses.3:9: And the LORD God called out to the man and said to him, "Where are you?"
verses.3:10: He said, "I heard Your sound in the garden, and I was afraid because I was naked; so I hid."
verses.3:11: And He said, "Who told you that you were naked? Have you eaten from the tree that I commanded you not to eat from?"
verses.3:12: The man answered, "The woman You gave to be with me—she herself gave me from the tree, and I ate."
verses.3:13: The LORD God said to the woman, "What is this that you have done?" And the woman replied, "The serpent misled me, and I ate."
verses.3:14: The LORD God said to the serpent, "Because you have done this, cursed are you more than all the livestock and more than every animal of the field; on your belly you will go, and dust you will eat all the days of your life.
verses.3:15: And I will put hostility between you and the woman, and between your offspring and her offspring; he will strike your head, and you will strike his heel."
verses.3:16: To the woman He said, "I will greatly multiply your pain and your conception; with pain you will give birth to children; yet your desire will be for your husband, and he will rule over you."
verses.3:17: Then to Adam He said, "Because you listened to the voice of your wife and ate from the tree about which I commanded you, saying, 'You must not eat from it,' cursed is the ground because of you; with pain you will eat from it all the days of your life.
verses.3:18: Thorns and thistles it will sprout for you, and you will eat the plants of the field.
verses.3:19: By the sweat of your face you will eat bread until you return to the ground, since from it you were taken; for dust you are, and to dust you will return."
verses.3:20: The man called his wife's name Eve, because she became the mother of all the living.
verses.3:21: And the LORD God made tunics of skin for Adam and for his wife, and He clothed them.
verses.3:22: Then the LORD God said, "See, the man has become like one of Us, knowing good and evil; and now, he might reach out his hand and take also from the tree of life, and eat, and live forever—"
verses.3:23: So the LORD God sent him out from the garden of Eden to work the ground from which he had been taken.
verses.3:24: He drove the man out; and east of the garden of Eden He stationed the cherubim and the flame of the sword that turned this way and that, to guard the way to the tree of life.
verses.4:1: Now the man knew Eve, his wife, and she conceived and gave birth to Cain, and said, "I have acquired a man with the LORD."
verses.4:2: Then she went on to give birth to his brother Abel. Abel became a shepherd of flocks, while Cain was a worker of the ground.
verses.4:3: And it happened at the end of some days that Cain brought from the fruit of the ground an offering to the LORD.
verses.4:4: And Abel too brought from the firstborn of his flock and from their fat portions, and the LORD showed regard for Abel and for his offering,
verses.4:5: but for Cain and for his offering He showed no regard. And Cain burned with great anger, and his face fell.
verses.4:6: Then the LORD said to Cain, "Why are you burning with anger, and why has your face fallen?
verses.4:7: If you do well, will there not be a lifting up? And if you do not do well, at the doorway sin is crouching; its desire is toward you, yet you are to rule over it."
verses.4:8: And Cain spoke to his brother Abel. Now it happened while they were in the field that Cain rose against his brother Abel and killed him.
verses.4:9: And the LORD said to Cain, "Where is Abel, your brother?" And he said, "I do not know. Am I my brother's guardian?"
verses.4:10: And He said, "What have you done? The voice of your brother's blood cries out to Me from the ground.
verses.4:11: And now, cursed are you from the ground, which opened wide its mouth to take your brother's blood from your hand.
verses.4:12: When you work the ground, it will no longer give its strength to you; you will be restless and wandering on the earth."
verses.4:13: Then Cain said to the LORD, "Too great is my punishment to bear!
verses.4:14: Look, today You have driven me out from the face of the ground, and I will be hidden from Your face; I will be restless and wandering on the earth, and it will be that anyone who finds me will kill me."
verses.4:15: And the LORD said to him, "Therefore, vengeance will be exacted sevenfold on anyone who kills Cain." And the LORD set a sign for Cain, so that no one who found him would strike him down.
verses.4:16: So Cain went out from before the LORD and lived in the land of Nod, east of Eden.
verses.4:17: And Cain knew his wife, and she conceived and gave birth to Enoch. He was building a city, and he called the name of the city after the name of his son Enoch.
verses.4:18: And Irad was born to Enoch. Irad fathered Mehujael, Mehujael fathered Methushael, and Methushael fathered Lamech.
verses.4:19: And Lamech took for himself two wives; the name of the one was Adah, and the name of the second was Zillah.
verses.4:20: And Adah gave birth to Jabal; he was the father of those who live in tents and own livestock.
verses.4:21: And the name of his brother was Jubal; he was the father of all who play the lyre and flute.
verses.4:22: And Zillah too gave birth to Tubal-cain, a forger of every cutting tool of bronze and iron; and Tubal-cain's sister was Naamah.
verses.4:23: And Lamech said to his wives, "Adah and Zillah, listen to my voice; wives of Lamech, give ear to my speech: for I have killed a man for wounding me, and a youth for bruising me.
verses.4:24: If Cain will be avenged sevenfold, then Lamech seventy-sevenfold!"
verses.4:25: And Adam knew his wife again, and she gave birth to a son and called his name Seth, "For God has appointed another offspring for me in place of Abel, since Cain killed him."
verses.4:26: And to Seth as well a son was born, and he called his name Enosh. Then people began to call on the name of the LORD.
verses.5:1: This is the book of Adam's generations. On the day God created man, in the likeness of God He made him.
verses.5:2: Male and female He created them, and He blessed them and called their name Man on the day they were created.
verses.5:3: And Adam lived one hundred thirty years, and he fathered a son in his likeness, according to his image, and he called his name Seth.
verses.5:4: And the days of Adam after fathering Seth were eight hundred years, and he fathered sons and daughters.
verses.5:5: And all of Adam's days that he lived were nine hundred thirty years, and he died.
verses.5:6: And Seth lived one hundred five years, and he fathered Enosh.
verses.5:7: And Seth lived eight hundred seven years after fathering Enosh, and he fathered sons and daughters.
verses.5:8: And all of Seth's days were nine hundred twelve years, and he died.
verses.5:9: And Enosh lived ninety years, and he fathered Kenan.
verses.5:10: And Enosh lived eight hundred fifteen years after fathering Kenan, and he fathered sons and daughters.
verses.5:11: And all of Enosh's days were nine hundred five years, and he died.
verses.5:12: And Kenan lived seventy years, and he fathered Mahalalel.
verses.5:13: And Kenan lived eight hundred forty years after fathering Mahalalel, and he fathered sons and daughters.
verses.5:14: And all of Kenan's days were nine hundred ten years, and he died.
verses.5:15: And Mahalalel lived sixty-five years, and he fathered Jared.
verses.5:16: And Mahalalel lived eight hundred thirty years after fathering Jared, and he fathered sons and daughters.
verses.5:17: And all of Mahalalel's days were eight hundred ninety-five years, and he died.
verses.5:18: And Jared lived one hundred sixty-two years, and he fathered Enoch.
verses.5:19: And Jared lived eight hundred years after fathering Enoch, and he fathered sons and daughters.
verses.5:20: And all of Jared's days were nine hundred sixty-two years, and he died.
verses.5:21: And Enoch lived sixty-five years, and he fathered Methuselah.
verses.5:22: And Enoch walked with God three hundred years after fathering Methuselah, and he fathered sons and daughters.
verses.5:23: And all of Enoch's days were three hundred sixty-five years.
verses.5:24: And Enoch walked with God, and he was gone, for God had taken him.
verses.5:25: And Methuselah lived one hundred eighty-seven years, and he fathered Lamech.
verses.5:26: And Methuselah lived seven hundred eighty-two years after fathering Lamech, and he fathered sons and daughters.
verses.5:27: And all of Methuselah's days were nine hundred sixty-nine years, and he died.
verses.5:28: And Lamech lived one hundred eighty-two years, and he fathered a son.
verses.5:29: And he called his name Noah, saying, "This one will comfort us from our work and from the painful labor of our hands, from the ground that the LORD has cursed."
verses.5:30: And Lamech lived five hundred ninety-five years after fathering Noah, and he fathered sons and daughters.
verses.5:31: And all of Lamech's days were seven hundred seventy-seven years, and he died.
verses.5:32: And Noah was five hundred years old, and Noah fathered Shem, Ham, and Japheth.
verses.6:1: Now it happened, when man began to grow numerous on the surface of the ground and daughters were born to them,
verses.6:2: that the sons of God saw the daughters of man, that they were lovely, and they took for themselves wives from all whom they chose.
verses.6:3: Then the LORD said, "My Spirit will not remain in man forever, since he too is flesh, and his days will be one hundred and twenty years."
verses.6:4: The Nephilim were on the earth in those days, and after that as well, when the sons of God would go in to the daughters of man and they bore offspring to them. They were the mighty warriors who were from ancient times, the men of renown.
verses.6:5: And the LORD saw that the evil of man was great on the earth, and that every inclination of the thoughts of his heart was only evil all day long.
verses.6:6: So the LORD regretted that He had made man on the earth, and He was pained to His heart.
verses.6:7: And the LORD said, "I will wipe out man whom I created from the surface of the ground, from man to animals, to creeping things, and to the birds of the sky, for I regret that I made them."
verses.6:8: Noah, however, found favor in the eyes of the LORD.
verses.6:9: These are the generations of Noah: Noah was a righteous man, blameless among his generations; with God Noah walked.
verses.6:10: And Noah fathered three sons: Shem, Ham, and Japheth.
verses.6:11: And the earth became corrupt before God, and the earth became filled with violence.
verses.6:12: And God looked at the earth, and look, it was corrupt, for all flesh had corrupted its way on the earth.
verses.6:13: Then God said to Noah, "The end of all flesh has come before Me, for the earth is full of violence on account of them; and look, I am about to destroy them along with the earth.
verses.6:14: Make for yourself an ark of gopher wood; make the ark with compartments, and coat it inside and outside with pitch.
verses.6:15: And this is how you are to make it: the length of the ark is to be three hundred cubits, its width fifty cubits, and its height thirty cubits.
verses.6:16: You shall make an opening for light for the ark, and finish it to a cubit from the top, and place the doorway of the ark in its side; make it with lower, second, and third stories.
verses.6:17: And as for Me, look, I am bringing the flood of waters upon the earth to destroy all flesh in which is the spirit of life from beneath the heavens; everything that is on the earth will perish.
verses.6:18: Yet I will establish My covenant with you, and you shall go into the ark, you and your sons and your wife and the wives of your sons with you.
verses.6:19: And of every living thing, of all flesh, you shall bring two of each into the ark to keep them alive with you; they shall be male and female.
verses.6:20: Of the birds according to their kind, and of the animals according to their kind, of every creeping thing of the ground according to its kind, two of each will come to you to keep them alive.
verses.6:21: And as for you, take for yourself of every kind of food that is eaten, and gather it to yourself, and it shall be food for you and for them."
verses.6:22: So Noah did this; according to all that God commanded him, just so he did.
verses.7:1: And the LORD said to Noah, "Enter the ark, you and your entire household, for I have seen you to be righteous before Me in this generation.
verses.7:2: From every clean animal you shall take for yourself by sevens, a male and its mate, and from the animals that are not clean, two, a male and its mate;
verses.7:3: also from the birds of the sky by sevens, male and female, to keep offspring alive on the surface of the entire earth.
verses.7:4: For in seven more days I will cause it to rain upon the earth forty days and forty nights, and I will wipe out every existing thing that I have made from the surface of the ground."
verses.7:5: So Noah did according to everything that the LORD had commanded him.
verses.7:6: Noah was six hundred years old when the flood of waters arrived on the earth.
verses.7:7: So Noah went into the ark, and his sons, his wife, and the wives of his sons with him, because of the waters of the flood.
verses.7:8: Of the clean animals and of the animals that are not clean, and of the birds and everything that creeps on the ground,
verses.7:9: two by two they came to Noah into the ark, male and female, just as God had commanded Noah.
verses.7:10: And it happened after the seven days that the waters of the flood came upon the earth.
verses.7:11: In the six hundredth year of the life of Noah, in the second month, on the seventeenth day of the month, on that day all the springs of the great deep split open, and the windows of the heavens were opened.
verses.7:12: And the rain was upon the earth forty days and forty nights.
verses.7:13: On that very day Noah, and Shem, Ham, and Japheth, the sons of Noah, and the wife of Noah and the three wives of his sons with them, went into the ark,
verses.7:14: they and every wild animal according to its kind, and all the livestock according to its kind, and every creeping thing that creeps on the earth according to its kind, and all the birds according to their kind, every bird, everything with wings.
verses.7:15: And they came to Noah into the ark, two by two from all flesh in which was the spirit of life.
verses.7:16: And those that came in, male and female from all flesh, came in just as God had commanded him; and the LORD shut him inside.
verses.7:17: Now the flood lasted forty days on the earth, and the waters increased and lifted the ark, and it rose up above the earth.
verses.7:18: And the waters prevailed and increased greatly upon the earth, and the ark moved over the surface of the waters.
verses.7:19: And the waters prevailed exceedingly upon the earth, and all the high mountains that were beneath the entire heavens were covered.
verses.7:20: Fifteen cubits upward the waters prevailed, and the mountains were covered.
verses.7:21: And all flesh that moved on the earth perished: birds, livestock, wild animals, and every swarming thing that swarms on the earth, and all mankind.
verses.7:22: Everything in whose nostrils was the breath of the spirit of life, of all that was on the dry land, died.
verses.7:23: So He wiped out every existing thing that was on the surface of the ground, from man to animals, to creeping things, and to the birds of the sky, and they were wiped out from the earth; and only Noah remained, and those who were with him in the ark.
verses.7:24: And the waters prevailed over the earth for one hundred and fifty days.
verses.8:1: Then God remembered Noah and every wild animal and all the livestock that were with him in the ark, and God made a wind pass over the earth, and the waters subsided.
verses.8:2: And the springs of the deep and the windows of the heavens were shut off, and the rain from the heavens was held back.
verses.8:3: And the waters steadily receded from the earth, and the waters diminished at the end of one hundred and fifty days.
verses.8:4: And the ark came to rest in the seventh month, on the seventeenth day of the month, upon the mountains of Ararat.
verses.8:5: And the waters kept diminishing until the tenth month; in the tenth month, on the first day of the month, the tops of the mountains appeared.
verses.8:6: And it happened at the end of forty days that Noah opened the window of the ark that he had made.
verses.8:7: And he sent out the raven, and it went out, going back and forth until the waters dried up from the earth.
verses.8:8: Then he sent out the dove from him to see whether the waters had abated from the surface of the ground.
verses.8:9: But the dove found no resting place for the sole of its foot, and it returned to him into the ark, for water was on the surface of the entire earth; so he reached out his hand and took it, and brought it to himself into the ark.
verses.8:10: And he waited yet another seven days, and again he sent out the dove from the ark.
verses.8:11: And the dove came to him at evening time, and look, a freshly plucked olive leaf was in its beak; so Noah knew that the waters had abated from the earth.
verses.8:12: Then he waited yet another seven days and sent out the dove, and it did not return to him again.
verses.8:13: And it happened in the six hundred and first year, in the first month, on the first day of the month, that the waters had dried off the earth; and Noah removed the covering of the ark and looked, and see, the surface of the ground had dried.
verses.8:14: And in the second month, on the twenty-seventh day of the month, the earth had become dry.
verses.8:15: And God spoke to Noah, saying,
verses.8:16: "Go out from the ark, you, and your wife, and your sons, and the wives of your sons with you.
verses.8:17: Bring out with you every living creature that is with you from all flesh, birds and animals and every creeping thing that creeps on the earth, so that they may swarm on the earth and be fruitful and multiply upon the earth."
verses.8:18: Then Noah came out, and his sons and his wife and the wives of his sons with him.
verses.8:19: Every living creature, every creeping thing, and every bird, everything that moves upon the earth, came out from the ark according to their families.
verses.8:20: And Noah built an altar to the LORD, and he took from every clean animal and from every clean bird and offered up burnt offerings on the altar.
verses.8:21: And the LORD smelled the soothing aroma, and the LORD said to His heart, "I will not again curse the ground on account of man, for the inclination of man's heart is evil from his youth, nor will I again strike down every living thing as I have done.
verses.8:22: Throughout all the remaining days of the earth, sowing and harvest, and cold and heat, and summer and winter, and day and night will not cease."
verses.9:1: Then God blessed Noah and his sons and said to them, "Be fruitful and grow numerous, and fill the earth.
verses.9:2: And the dread of you and the terror of you will be upon every beast of the earth and upon every bird of the sky; along with everything that moves on the ground and all the fish of the sea, they have been given into your hand.
verses.9:3: Every moving creature that is alive will be food for you; just as with the green vegetation, I have given everything to you.
verses.9:4: However, you must not eat flesh with its life—its blood.
verses.9:5: And indeed, I will demand your own lifeblood; from the hand of every beast I will demand it, and from the hand of man—from the hand of each person's brother—I will demand the life of man.
verses.9:6: One who sheds the blood of man, by man his blood will be shed, because in God's image He made man.
verses.9:7: As for you, be fruitful and grow numerous; teem on the earth and grow numerous in it."
verses.9:8: Then God spoke to Noah and to his sons with him, saying,
verses.9:9: "As for Me, look, I am establishing My covenant with you and with your offspring after you,
verses.9:10: and with every living creature that is with you—among the birds, the livestock, and every beast of the earth with you—from all that came out of the ark to every beast of the earth.
verses.9:11: And I will establish My covenant with you: all flesh will never again be cut off by the waters of the flood, and there will never again be a flood to destroy the earth."
verses.9:12: Then God said, "This is the sign of the covenant that I am giving between Me and you and every living creature that is with you, for generations forever:
verses.9:13: I have placed My bow in the cloud, and it will be a sign of a covenant between Me and the earth.
verses.9:14: And it will happen, when I gather a cloud over the earth, that the bow will appear in the cloud,
verses.9:15: and I will remember My covenant that is between Me and you and every living creature among all flesh; and the waters will never again become a flood to destroy all flesh.
verses.9:16: The bow will be in the cloud, and I will see it to remember an everlasting covenant between God and every living creature among all flesh that is on the earth."
verses.9:17: Then God said to Noah, "This is the sign of the covenant I have established between Me and all flesh that is on the earth."
verses.9:18: The sons of Noah who came out of the ark were Shem, Ham, and Japheth; and Ham was the father of Canaan.
verses.9:19: These three were Noah's sons, and from these the whole earth was dispersed.
verses.9:20: And Noah began as a man of the soil, and he planted a vineyard.
verses.9:21: He drank from the wine and grew drunk, and he uncovered himself in the middle of his tent.
verses.9:22: Ham, Canaan's father, saw his father's nakedness, and he told his two brothers outside.
verses.9:23: Then Shem and Japheth took the cloak, placed it across the shoulders of both of them, walked backward, and covered their father's nakedness. With their faces turned backward, they did not see their father's nakedness.
verses.9:24: Then Noah woke from his wine and learned what his youngest son had done to him.
verses.9:25: He said, "Cursed be Canaan; a slave of slaves he will be to his brothers."
verses.9:26: And he said, "Blessed be the LORD, the God of Shem, and let Canaan be a slave to him.
verses.9:27: May God grant wide space to Japheth, and may he dwell in the tents of Shem, and let Canaan be a slave to him."
verses.9:28: And Noah lived after the flood three hundred fifty years.
verses.9:29: Thus all the days of Noah came to nine hundred fifty years, and he died.
verses.10:1: Now these are the generations of Noah's sons—Shem, Ham, and Japheth—and sons were born to them after the flood.
verses.10:2: Japheth's sons were Gomer, Magog, Madai, Javan, Tubal, Meshech, and Tiras.
verses.10:3: And Gomer's sons were Ashkenaz, Riphath, and Togarmah.
verses.10:4: And Javan's sons were Elishah, Tarshish, Kittim, and Dodanim.
verses.10:5: From these the coastlands of the nations separated in their lands, each according to his language, by their clans, in their nations.
verses.10:6: And Ham's sons were Cush, Mizraim, Put, and Canaan.
verses.10:7: And Cush's sons were Seba, Havilah, Sabtah, Raamah, and Sabteca; and Raamah's sons were Sheba and Dedan.
verses.10:8: Now Cush fathered Nimrod; he began to be a mighty one on the earth.
verses.10:9: He was a mighty hunter in the sight of the LORD; for this reason it is said, "Like Nimrod, a mighty hunter in the sight of the LORD."
verses.10:10: And the beginning of his realm was Babel, Erech, Accad, and Calneh in the land of Shinar.
verses.10:11: Out of that land he went into Assyria, and he built Nineveh, Rehoboth-Ir, Calah,
verses.10:12: and Resen, between Nineveh and Calah—that is the great city.
verses.10:13: And Mizraim fathered Ludim, Anamim, Lehabim, Naphtuhim,
verses.10:14: Pathrusim, Casluhim—from whom the Philistines came out—and Caphtorim.
verses.10:15: And Canaan fathered Sidon his firstborn, Heth,
verses.10:16: the Jebusite, the Amorite, the Girgashite,
verses.10:17: the Hivite, the Arkite, the Sinite,
verses.10:18: the Arvadite, the Zemarite, and the Hamathite; and afterward the clans of the Canaanite were dispersed.
verses.10:19: And the border of the Canaanite extended from Sidon, going toward Gerar as far as Gaza; going toward Sodom, Gomorrah, Admah, and Zeboiim as far as Lasha.
verses.10:20: These are Ham's sons, by their clans, by their languages, in their lands, in their nations.
verses.10:21: And to Shem—the father of all the sons of Eber, the brother of Japheth the elder—children were born as well.
verses.10:22: Shem's sons were Elam, Asshur, Arpachshad, Lud, and Aram.
verses.10:23: And Aram's sons were Uz, Hul, Gether, and Mash.
verses.10:24: Now Arpachshad fathered Shelah, and Shelah fathered Eber.
verses.10:25: And two sons were born to Eber: the name of the first was Peleg, because in his days the earth was divided, and the name of his brother was Joktan.
verses.10:26: And Joktan fathered Almodad, Sheleph, Hazarmaveth, Jerah,
verses.10:29: Ophir, Havilah, and Jobab; all of these were Joktan's sons.
verses.10:30: And their dwelling place extended from Mesha, going toward Sephar, the mountain of the east.
verses.10:31: These are Shem's sons, by their clans, by their languages, in their lands, by their nations.
verses.10:32: These are the clans of Noah's sons, according to their generations, in their nations; and from these the nations separated on the earth after the flood.
verses.11:1: Now all the earth had one language and one set of words.
verses.11:2: And it happened, as they journeyed from the east, that they found a valley plain in the land of Shinar and settled there.
verses.11:3: They said, each to his neighbor, "Come, let us make bricks and fire them thoroughly." So brick served them for stone, and bitumen served them for mortar.
verses.11:4: And they said, "Come, let us build a city for ourselves and a tower whose top is in the heavens, and let us make a name for ourselves, or else we will be scattered across the face of all the earth."
verses.11:5: Then the LORD went down to see the city and the tower that the sons of mankind had built.
verses.11:6: And the LORD said, "Look, they are one people, and all of them have one language; this is what they have started to do, and now nothing that they devise to do will be withheld from them.
verses.11:7: Come, let Us go down and confuse their language there, so that each will not understand his neighbor's language."
verses.11:8: So the LORD scattered them from there across the face of all the earth, and they ceased building the city.
verses.11:9: For this reason its name was called Babel, for there the LORD confused the language of all the earth, and from there the LORD scattered them across the face of all the earth.
verses.11:10: These are the generations of Shem: Shem was one hundred years old, and he fathered Arpachshad two years after the flood.
verses.11:11: And Shem lived five hundred years after fathering Arpachshad, and he fathered sons and daughters.
verses.11:12: Now Arpachshad lived thirty-five years, and he fathered Shelah.
verses.11:13: And Arpachshad lived four hundred three years after fathering Shelah, and he fathered sons and daughters.
verses.11:14: Now Shelah lived thirty years, and he fathered Eber.
verses.11:15: And Shelah lived four hundred three years after fathering Eber, and he fathered sons and daughters.
verses.11:16: And Eber lived thirty-four years, and he fathered Peleg.
verses.11:17: And Eber lived four hundred thirty years after fathering Peleg, and he fathered sons and daughters.
verses.11:18: And Peleg lived thirty years, and he fathered Reu.
verses.11:19: And Peleg lived two hundred nine years after fathering Reu, and he fathered sons and daughters.
verses.11:20: And Reu lived thirty-two years, and he fathered Serug.
verses.11:21: And Reu lived two hundred seven years after fathering Serug, and he fathered sons and daughters.
verses.11:22: And Serug lived thirty years, and he fathered Nahor.
verses.11:23: And Serug lived two hundred years after fathering Nahor, and he fathered sons and daughters.
verses.11:24: And Nahor lived twenty-nine years, and he fathered Terah.
verses.11:25: And Nahor lived one hundred nineteen years after fathering Terah, and he fathered sons and daughters.
verses.11:26: And Terah lived seventy years, and he fathered Abram, Nahor, and Haran.
verses.11:27: And these are the generations of Terah: Terah fathered Abram, Nahor, and Haran, while Haran fathered Lot.
verses.11:28: And Haran died during the lifetime of Terah his father, in the land of his birth, in Ur of the Chaldeans.
verses.11:29: And Abram and Nahor took wives for themselves; Abram's wife was named Sarai, and Nahor's wife was named Milcah, the daughter of Haran, the father of Milcah and the father of Iscah.
verses.11:30: And Sarai was barren, having no child.
verses.11:31: And Terah took his son Abram, and Lot son of Haran, his grandson, and his daughter-in-law Sarai, the wife of his son Abram, and they went out together from Ur of the Chaldeans to go to the land of Canaan; but they came as far as Haran and settled there.
verses.11:32: And the days of Terah amounted to two hundred five years, and Terah died in Haran.
verses.12:1: Then the LORD said to Abram, "Go out from your land, from your relatives, and from your father's house, to the land that I will show you.
verses.12:2: And I will make you into a great nation, I will bless you, and I will make your name great; and be a blessing.
verses.12:3: And I will bless those who bless you, and the one who reviles you I will curse; and all the families of the earth will be blessed in you."
verses.12:4: So Abram went just as the LORD had spoken to him, and Lot went with him; Abram was seventy-five years old when he went out from Haran.
verses.12:5: And Abram took his wife Sarai, his brother's son Lot, all the possessions that they had amassed, and the persons whom they had acquired in Haran; and they went out to go to the land of Canaan, and they came into the land of Canaan.
verses.12:6: And Abram passed through the land as far as the place of Shechem, as far as the oak of Moreh; now the Canaanites were in the land at that time.
verses.12:7: And the LORD appeared to Abram and said, "I will give this land to your offspring." And there he built an altar to the LORD, who had appeared to him.
verses.12:8: Then he relocated from there to the hill country east of Bethel and set up his tent with Bethel to the west and Ai to the east; he built an altar to the LORD there and called on the name of the LORD.
verses.12:9: Then Abram journeyed on, going steadily toward the Negev.
verses.12:10: And there was a famine in the land, and Abram went down into Egypt to stay there as a foreigner, because the famine in the land was severe.
verses.12:11: And as he drew near to enter Egypt, he said to his wife Sarai, "Look now, I know that you are a woman of beautiful appearance.
verses.12:12: And it will happen that when the Egyptians see you, they will say, 'This is his wife,' and they will kill me, but they will keep you alive.
verses.12:13: Say, please, that you are my sister, so that it may go well for me on your account and that my soul may live because of you."
verses.12:14: Now when Abram entered Egypt, the Egyptians saw the woman, that she was very beautiful.
verses.12:15: And the officials of Pharaoh saw her, and they praised her to Pharaoh; so the woman was taken into the house of Pharaoh.
verses.12:16: And he dealt well with Abram on her account, and he came to have flocks and herds, male donkeys, male servants and female servants, female donkeys, and camels.
verses.12:17: But the LORD plagued Pharaoh and his house with great plagues because of Sarai, the wife of Abram.
verses.12:18: Then Pharaoh summoned Abram and said, "What is this that you have done to me? Why did you not inform me that she is your wife?
verses.12:19: Why did you say, 'She is my sister,' so that I took her to myself as a wife? And now, here is your wife—take her and go!"
verses.12:20: Then Pharaoh commanded men concerning him, and they sent him away, along with his wife and all that was his.
verses.13:1: Then Abram went up out of Egypt, he and his wife and all that belonged to him, and Lot with him, into the Negev.
verses.13:2: Now Abram was very wealthy in livestock, in silver, and in gold.
verses.13:3: And he went by stages from the Negev as far as Bethel, to the place where his tent had been at the start, between Bethel and Ai,
verses.13:4: to the place of the altar that he had made there previously, and Abram called on the name of the LORD there.
verses.13:5: Lot as well, who was going along with Abram, had flocks and herds and tents.
verses.13:6: And the land could not support them living together, because their possessions were great, and they were unable to live together.
verses.13:7: Then a dispute arose between the herders of Abram's livestock and the herders of Lot's livestock; now the Canaanites and the Perizzites were living in the land at that time.
verses.13:8: So Abram said to Lot, "Please let there be no dispute between me and you, and between my herders and your herders, because we are brothers.
verses.13:9: Is not all the land before you? Separate yourself from me, please. If you take the left, I will go to the right; and if you take the right, I will go to the left."
verses.13:10: So Lot lifted up his eyes and saw the entire plain of the Jordan, that all of it was well watered—before the LORD destroyed Sodom and Gomorrah—like the garden of the LORD, like the land of Egypt, as one goes toward Zoar.
verses.13:11: Then Lot chose for himself the entire plain of the Jordan, and Lot journeyed eastward; and they separated, each from his brother.
verses.13:12: Abram lived in the land of Canaan, while Lot lived in the cities of the plain and moved his tent as far as Sodom.
verses.13:13: Now the men of Sodom were very wicked and sinful against the LORD.
verses.13:14: And after Lot had separated from him, the LORD said to Abram, "Lift up your eyes, please, and look from the place where you are—to the north and to the south, to the east and to the west;
verses.13:15: for all the land that you see, to you I will give it, and to your offspring forever.
verses.13:16: And I will make your offspring like the dust of the earth, so that if a man is able to count the dust of the earth, your offspring too could be counted.
verses.13:17: Rise, walk about in the land, along its length and its breadth, for to you I will give it."
verses.13:18: Then Abram moved his tent, and he came and settled among the oaks of Mamre, which are in Hebron; and he built an altar to the LORD there.
verses.14:1: Now it happened in the days of Amraphel king of Shinar, Arioch king of Ellasar, Chedorlaomer king of Elam, and Tidal king of Goiim,
verses.14:2: that they waged war against Bera king of Sodom, Birsha king of Gomorrah, Shinab king of Admah, Shemeber king of Zeboiim, and the king of Bela—that is, Zoar.
verses.14:3: All of these united at the Valley of Siddim—that is, the Salt Sea.
verses.14:4: For twelve years they served Chedorlaomer, yet in the thirteenth year they rebelled.
verses.14:5: In the fourteenth year, Chedorlaomer and the kings who were with him arrived and struck down the Rephaim in Ashteroth-karnaim, the Zuzim in Ham, the Emim in Shaveh-kiriathaim,
verses.14:6: and the Horites in their mountain country of Seir, as far as El-paran, which is beside the wilderness.
verses.14:7: Then they turned back and came to En-mishpat—that is, Kadesh—and struck all the territory of the Amalekites, as well as the Amorites living in Hazazon-tamar.
verses.14:8: Then the king of Sodom, the king of Gomorrah, the king of Admah, the king of Zeboiim, and the king of Bela—that is, Zoar—marched out, and they lined up for battle against them in the Valley of Siddim,
verses.14:9: against Chedorlaomer king of Elam, Tidal king of Goiim, Amraphel king of Shinar, and Arioch king of Ellasar—four kings against the five.
verses.14:10: Now the Valley of Siddim had pit after pit of bitumen, and the kings of Sodom and Gomorrah fled and fell into them, while those who remained fled to the hill country.
verses.14:11: Then they took all the possessions of Sodom and Gomorrah and all their food, and went away.
verses.14:12: They also took Lot, Abram's brother's son, and his possessions, and went away; for he was living in Sodom.
verses.14:13: Then an escapee came and told Abram the Hebrew. Now he was dwelling by the oaks of Mamre the Amorite, brother of Eshcol and brother of Aner, and they were covenant allies of Abram.
verses.14:14: When Abram heard that his relative had been captured, he mustered his trained men, born in his household—three hundred and eighteen—and pursued as far as Dan.
verses.14:15: He split up against them at night—he and his servants—and struck them down, pursuing them as far as Hobah, which is north of Damascus.
verses.14:16: He brought back all the possessions; he also brought back Lot his relative and his possessions, as well as the women and the people.
verses.14:17: After his return from striking down Chedorlaomer and the kings who were with him, the king of Sodom came out to meet him at the Valley of Shaveh—that is, the King's Valley.
verses.14:18: Melchizedek king of Salem brought out bread and wine, and he was priest of God Most High.
verses.14:19: He blessed him and said, "Blessed be Abram by God Most High, Creator of heaven and earth,
verses.14:20: and blessed be God Most High, who has delivered your adversaries into your hand." And he gave him a tenth of everything.
verses.14:21: Then the king of Sodom said to Abram, "Give me the people, and take the possessions for yourself."
verses.14:22: And Abram said to the king of Sodom, "I have raised my hand to the LORD, God Most High, Creator of heaven and earth,
verses.14:23: that I will take nothing—not from a thread to a sandal strap—out of all that belongs to you, so that you will not say, 'I have made Abram rich.'
verses.14:24: Nothing for me, only what the young men have eaten, and the portion of the men who went with me. Aner, Eshcol, and Mamre—let them take their portion."
verses.15:1: After these events, the word of the LORD came to Abram in a vision, saying, "Do not be afraid, Abram. I am a shield for you; your reward will be exceedingly great."
verses.15:2: Abram said, "Lord GOD, what will You give me, since I go on childless, and the heir of my household is Eliezer of Damascus?"
verses.15:3: And Abram said, "See, to me You have given no offspring, and look, one born in my household is to be my heir."
verses.15:4: Now the word of the LORD came to him, saying, "This one will not be your heir; rather, one who comes out from your own body—he will be your heir."
verses.15:5: He brought him outside and said, "Look up now to the heavens and count the stars, if you can count them." Then He said to him, "So will your offspring be."
verses.15:6: And he trusted in the LORD, and He counted it as righteousness for him.
verses.15:7: Then He said to him, "I am the LORD, who brought you out from Ur of the Chaldeans to give this land to you to possess it."
verses.15:8: And he said, "Lord GOD, how can I know that I will possess it?"
verses.15:9: Then He said to him, "Bring for Me a three-year-old heifer, a three-year-old female goat, a three-year-old ram, a turtledove, and a young pigeon."
verses.15:10: So he brought all of these to Him, cut them in two down the middle, and placed each half opposite the other; but he did not cut the birds in two.
verses.15:11: Then birds of prey descended onto the carcasses, and Abram drove them off.
verses.15:12: Now as the sun was about to go down, a deep sleep fell on Abram; and look, a dread, a great darkness, was falling on him.
verses.15:13: Then He said to Abram, "Know for certain that your offspring will be sojourners in a land that is not theirs, and they will be enslaved and afflicted for four hundred years.
verses.15:14: Yet I will also judge the nation they will serve, and after that they will come out with great possessions.
verses.15:15: But you will go to your fathers in peace; you will be buried at a good old age.
verses.15:16: And in the fourth generation they will return here, because the iniquity of the Amorites is not yet full."
verses.15:17: When the sun had gone down and thick darkness had set in, look—there was a smoking firepot and a torch of fire that passed between these pieces.
verses.15:18: On that day the LORD made a covenant with Abram, saying, "To your offspring I have given this land, from the river of Egypt to the great river, the Euphrates River:
verses.15:19: the Kenites, the Kenizzites, and the Kadmonites,
verses.15:20: the Hittites, the Perizzites, and the Rephaim,
verses.15:21: the Amorites, the Canaanites, the Girgashites, and the Jebusites."
verses.16:1: Now Sarai, the wife of Abram, had borne no children to him; she had an Egyptian maidservant, and her name was Hagar.
verses.16:2: Then Sarai said to Abram, "See now, the LORD has kept me from giving birth. Please go in to my maidservant; perhaps I will be built up through her." And Abram heeded the voice of Sarai.
verses.16:3: So Sarai, Abram's wife, took Hagar the Egyptian, her maidservant—at the end of ten years of Abram living in the land of Canaan—and gave her to Abram her husband as a wife for him.
verses.16:4: He went in to Hagar, and she conceived. When she saw that she had conceived, her mistress became despised in her eyes.
verses.16:5: Then Sarai said to Abram, "The wrong done to me is on you! I myself gave my maidservant into your embrace, and when she saw that she had conceived, I became despised in her eyes. May the LORD judge between me and you!"
verses.16:6: Abram said to Sarai, "Look, your maidservant is in your hand; do to her what is good in your eyes." Then Sarai afflicted her, and she fled from her presence.
verses.16:7: Then the angel of the LORD found her beside a spring of water in the wilderness—beside the spring along the road to Shur.
verses.16:8: He said, "Hagar, maidservant of Sarai, where have you come from, and where are you going?" She said, "From the presence of Sarai my mistress I am fleeing."
verses.16:9: Then the angel of the LORD said to her, "Return to your mistress and submit yourself under her hands."
verses.16:10: And the angel of the LORD said to her, "I will greatly multiply your offspring, so that they cannot be counted for their abundance."
verses.16:11: And the angel of the LORD said to her, "Look, you are pregnant and about to bear a son; you will call his name Ishmael, for the LORD has heard your affliction.
verses.16:12: He will be a wild donkey of a man—his hand against everyone, and the hand of everyone against him—and he will dwell opposite all his brothers."
verses.16:13: So she called the name of the LORD who was speaking to her, "You are a God of Seeing," for she said, "Have I really even here seen after Him who sees me?"
verses.16:14: Therefore the well was called Beer-lahai-roi; see, it lies between Kadesh and Bered.
verses.16:15: Then Hagar gave birth to a son for Abram, and Abram called the name of his son, whom Hagar had borne, Ishmael.
verses.16:16: Now Abram was eighty-six years old when Hagar gave birth to Ishmael for Abram.
verses.17:1: Abram was ninety-nine years old when the LORD appeared to Abram and said to him, "I am God Almighty. Walk continually in My presence and be blameless,
verses.17:2: and I will set My covenant between Me and you, and I will multiply you very greatly."
verses.17:3: Then Abram fell upon his face, and God spoke with him, saying,
verses.17:4: "As for Me, look, My covenant is with you, and you shall become the father of a multitude of nations.
verses.17:5: Your name shall no longer be called Abram; rather, your name shall be Abraham, for I have appointed you father of a multitude of nations.
verses.17:6: And I will make you very fruitful indeed; I will make you into nations, and kings will come out from you.
verses.17:7: And I will establish My covenant between Me and you, and your offspring after you through their generations, as a perpetual covenant, to be God for you and for your offspring after you.
verses.17:8: And I will give to you and to your offspring after you the land of your sojournings, all the land of Canaan, as a perpetual possession, and I will be God for them."
verses.17:9: Then God said to Abraham, "And as for you, you must keep My covenant—you and your offspring after you through their generations.
verses.17:10: This is My covenant that you must keep between Me and you and your offspring after you: every male among you is to be circumcised.
verses.17:11: And you shall circumcise the flesh of your foreskin, and it shall serve as a sign of the covenant between Me and you.
verses.17:12: At eight days old, every male among you shall be circumcised through your generations—whether born in the house or purchased with silver from any foreigner who is not from your offspring.
verses.17:13: Both the one born in your house and the one purchased with your silver must certainly be circumcised, and My covenant in your flesh shall be a perpetual covenant.
verses.17:14: And as for any uncircumcised male who has not been circumcised in the flesh of his foreskin, that person shall be cut off from his people; he has violated My covenant."
verses.17:15: God also said to Abraham, "Regarding Sarai your wife, you are not to call her name Sarai; instead, her name shall be Sarah.
verses.17:16: I will bless her, and I will also give you a son by her; yes, I will bless her so that she becomes nations, and kings of peoples will come from her."
verses.17:17: Then Abraham fell upon his face and laughed, and he said in his heart, "To a man a hundred years old, will a child be born? And Sarah, at ninety years old—will she give birth?"
verses.17:18: And Abraham said to God, "If only Ishmael might live in Your presence!"
verses.17:19: But God said, "No; Sarah your wife is going to bear you a son, and you shall call his name Isaac. And I will establish My covenant with him as a perpetual covenant for his offspring after him.
verses.17:20: As for Ishmael, I have heard you: see, I have blessed him, and I will make him fruitful and multiply him very greatly. Twelve princes he will father, and I will make him into a great nation.
verses.17:21: Yet My covenant I will establish with Isaac, whom Sarah will bear to you at this set time in the next year."
verses.17:22: And when He had finished speaking with him, God ascended from Abraham.
verses.17:23: Then Abraham took his son Ishmael, along with all those born in his house and all those purchased with his silver—every male among the men of Abraham's household—and he circumcised the flesh of their foreskin on that very day, just as God had spoken with him.
verses.17:24: Abraham was ninety-nine years old at the time he was circumcised in the flesh of his foreskin.
verses.17:25: And his son Ishmael was thirteen years old at the time he was circumcised in the flesh of his foreskin.
verses.17:26: On that very day Abraham was circumcised, together with his son Ishmael.
verses.17:27: And all the men of his household, both those born in the house and those purchased with silver from a foreigner, were circumcised with him.
verses.18:1: Then the LORD appeared to him at the oaks of Mamre while he was sitting at the entrance of the tent during the heat of the day.
verses.18:2: He raised his eyes and looked, and see, three men were standing near him. When he saw them, he ran to meet them from the entrance of the tent and bowed down to the ground.
verses.18:3: And he said, "Lord, if now I have found favor in Your eyes, please do not go on past Your servant.
verses.18:4: Let a little water please be fetched, and wash your feet, and recline beneath the tree.
verses.18:5: And let me fetch a morsel of bread, and sustain your hearts; afterward you may pass on, since you have passed by your servant." And they said, "Do so, just as you have spoken."
verses.18:6: Abraham then hurried into the tent to Sarah and said, "Hurry! Three seahs of choice flour—knead it and make bread cakes."
verses.18:7: And to the herd Abraham ran; he took a calf that was tender and fine, and gave it to the young attendant, and he hurried to prepare it.
verses.18:8: Then he brought curds and milk, along with the calf that he had prepared, and set them before them; and he was standing beside them beneath the tree while they ate.
verses.18:9: Then they said to him, "Where is your wife Sarah?" And he said, "Right there in the tent."
verses.18:10: And He said, "I will certainly return to you when the season returns, and look, your wife Sarah will have a son." Now Sarah was listening at the entrance of the tent, which was behind Him.
verses.18:11: Abraham and Sarah were old, advanced in days, and the way of women had ceased for Sarah.
verses.18:12: So Sarah laughed within herself, saying, "After I have grown worn out, am I to have pleasure, when my lord is old?"
verses.18:13: Then the LORD said to Abraham, "Why is it that Sarah laughed, saying, 'Will I truly give birth, when I have grown old?'
verses.18:14: Is any matter too extraordinary for the LORD? At the set time I will return to you, when the season returns, and Sarah will have a son."
verses.18:15: Then Sarah denied it, saying, "I did not laugh," because she was afraid. Yet He said, "No, indeed, you did laugh."
verses.18:16: Then the men got up from there and looked down over Sodom, while Abraham was walking with them to see them off.
verses.18:17: And the LORD said, "Am I to conceal from Abraham what I am about to do,
verses.18:18: since Abraham is certain to become a great and powerful nation, and all the nations of the earth will be blessed in him?
verses.18:19: For I have known him so that he may charge his children and his household after him, and they will keep the way of the LORD by practicing righteousness and justice, in order that the LORD may bring upon Abraham what He has spoken concerning him."
verses.18:20: Then the LORD said, "The outcry concerning Sodom and Gomorrah is truly great, and their sin is truly very grave.
verses.18:21: Let Me go down now and see whether they have acted altogether according to its outcry that has come to Me; and if not, I will know."
verses.18:22: And the men turned from there and walked toward Sodom, while Abraham remained standing before the LORD.
verses.18:23: Then Abraham approached and said, "Will You truly sweep away the righteous along with the wicked?
verses.18:24: Perhaps there are fifty righteous people within the city; will You truly sweep it away and not spare the place on account of the fifty righteous who are in its midst?
verses.18:25: Far be it from You to do a thing like this—to put the righteous to death along with the wicked, so that the righteous becomes like the wicked! Far be it from You! Will the Judge of the whole earth not do justice?"
verses.18:26: And the LORD said, "If I find fifty righteous people in Sodom, within the city, then I will spare the entire place for their sake."
verses.18:27: Abraham answered and said, "Look now, I have taken it upon myself to speak to the Lord, even though I am dust and ashes.
verses.18:28: Perhaps the fifty righteous fall short by five; will You destroy the entire city on account of the five?" And He said, "If I find forty-five there, I will not destroy it."
verses.18:29: He spoke to Him yet once more and said, "Perhaps forty will be found there." And He said, "I will not do it for the sake of the forty."
verses.18:30: Then he said, "Please may the Lord not grow angry, and let me speak: perhaps thirty will be found there." And He said, "If I find thirty there, I will not do it."
verses.18:31: And he said, "Look now, I have taken it upon myself to speak to the Lord: perhaps twenty will be found there." And He said, "I will not destroy it for the sake of the twenty."
verses.18:32: Then he said, "Please may the Lord not grow angry, and let me speak just this once: perhaps ten will be found there." And He said, "I will not destroy it for the sake of the ten."
verses.18:33: Then the LORD departed after He had finished speaking to Abraham, while Abraham returned to his place.
verses.19:1: The two angels reached Sodom in the evening, while Lot was sitting in the gate of Sodom. Lot saw them, got up to meet them, and bowed down, his face to the ground.
verses.19:2: He said, "Now look, my lords, please turn aside to your servant's house, spend the night, and wash your feet; then you may rise early and go on your way." They replied, "No, instead we will spend the night in the open square."
verses.19:3: Yet he pressed them very strongly, so they turned aside to him and entered his house. He prepared a feast for them and baked unleavened bread, and they ate.
verses.19:4: Before they lay down, the men of the city, the men of Sodom, encircled the house, from youth to old man, all the people from every quarter.
verses.19:5: They called out to Lot and said to him, "Where are the men who came to you tonight? Bring them out to us so that we may know them."
verses.19:6: Lot went out to them into the doorway, and he closed the door behind him.
verses.19:7: He said, "Please, my brothers, do not act wickedly.
verses.19:8: Look now, I have two daughters who have not known a man. Please let me bring them out to you, and do to them according to what is good in your eyes. Only do not do anything to these men, since they have come under the shadow of my roof."
verses.19:9: But they said, "Step back!" And they said, "This one came to reside as a foreigner, yet he keeps acting as judge! Now we will do worse to you than to them." So they pressed very hard against the man, against Lot, and stepped forward to break down the door.
verses.19:10: Then the men stretched out their hands, brought Lot to themselves inside the house, and closed the door.
verses.19:11: And they struck the men who were at the doorway of the house with blindness, from small to great, so that they grew weary trying to find the doorway.
verses.19:12: Then the men said to Lot, "Who else do you have here? A son-in-law, and your sons, and your daughters, and all that you have in the city, bring them out of the place,
verses.19:13: for we are going to destroy this place, because the outcry against them has grown great before the LORD, and the LORD has sent us to destroy it."
verses.19:14: So Lot went out and spoke to his sons-in-law, who were marrying his daughters, and said, "Get up, go out from this place, for the LORD is going to destroy the city." Yet he seemed like someone joking in the eyes of his sons-in-law.
verses.19:15: As dawn rose, the angels hurried Lot, saying, "Get up! Take your wife and your two daughters who are here, or else you will be swept away in the city's punishment."
verses.19:16: Yet he lingered; so the men took hold of his hand, his wife's hand, and the hands of his two daughters, because of the LORD's compassion on him, and they brought him out and placed him outside the city.
verses.19:17: When they had brought them outside, he said, "Escape for your life! Do not look behind you, and do not stop anywhere in the plain. Escape to the hill country, or else you will be swept away."
verses.19:18: But Lot said to them, "No, please, my lord!
verses.19:19: Look now, your servant has found favor in your eyes, and you have magnified your kindness that you have shown to me in preserving my life; yet I cannot escape to the hill country, or else the disaster will overtake me and I will die.
verses.19:20: See now, this city is near enough to flee there, and it is a small one. Please let me escape there! Is it not a small one? Then my soul will live."
verses.19:21: He said to him, "Look, I grant you favor in this matter as well, so that I will not overthrow the city of which you have spoken.
verses.19:22: Hurry, escape there, because I cannot do a thing until you get there." For that reason, the name of the city was called Zoar.
verses.19:23: The sun had come up over the land as Lot entered Zoar.
verses.19:24: Then the LORD rained down sulfur and fire on Sodom and on Gomorrah, from the LORD out of the heavens.
verses.19:25: He overthrew those cities, the entire plain, all the inhabitants of the cities, and the vegetation of the ground.
verses.19:26: His wife, however, looked back from behind him, and she became a pillar of salt.
verses.19:27: Abraham rose early in the morning and went to the place where he had stood before the LORD.
verses.19:28: He gazed down toward Sodom and Gomorrah and over the entire face of the land of the plain, and he looked, and there the smoke of the land was going up like the smoke of a furnace.
verses.19:29: So when God destroyed the cities of the plain, God remembered Abraham and sent Lot out from the middle of the overthrow when He overthrew the cities where Lot had lived.
verses.19:30: Then Lot went up from Zoar and lived in the hill country, and his two daughters were with him, because he was afraid to live in Zoar. So he lived in a cave, he and his two daughters.
verses.19:31: The firstborn said to the younger, "Our father is old, and there is no man on the earth to come in to us according to the way of all the earth.
verses.19:32: Come, let us give our father wine to drink and let us lie with him, so that we may preserve offspring from our father."
verses.19:33: So they gave their father wine to drink that night, and the firstborn came in and lay with her father, and he did not know when she lay down or when she got up.
verses.19:34: The next day the firstborn said to the younger, "Look, I lay with my father last night; let us give him wine to drink tonight as well, and you go in and lie with him, so that we may preserve offspring from our father."
verses.19:35: So they gave their father wine to drink that night as well, and the younger rose and lay with him; and he did not know when she lay down or when she got up.
verses.19:36: So the two daughters of Lot conceived by their father.
verses.19:37: The firstborn gave birth to a son and called his name Moab; he is the father of Moab to this day.
verses.19:38: And the younger, she also gave birth to a son and called his name Ben-ammi; he is the father of the sons of Ammon to this day.
verses.20:1: Then Abraham traveled on from there to the land of the Negev and settled between Kadesh and Shur, and he resided as a foreigner in Gerar.
verses.20:2: Abraham said concerning Sarah his wife, "She is my sister." So Abimelech, the king of Gerar, sent and took Sarah.
verses.20:3: Yet God came to Abimelech in a dream at night and said to him, "Look, you are a dead man because of the woman whom you have taken, since she is married to a husband."
verses.20:4: Now Abimelech had not come near her, so he said, "Lord, will You kill even a righteous nation?
verses.20:5: Did he not say to me himself, 'She is my sister'? And she, she herself also said, 'He is my brother.' In the integrity of my heart and in the cleanness of my hands I did this."
verses.20:6: Then God said to him in the dream, "I too know that you did this in the integrity of your heart, and I Myself also kept you from sinning against Me; therefore I did not allow you to touch her.
verses.20:7: So now, return the man's wife, because he is a prophet, and he will pray for you, and you will live. Yet if you do not return her, know that you will certainly die, you and all who belong to you."
verses.20:8: Abimelech rose early in the morning, summoned all his servants, and spoke all these things in their hearing; and the men were greatly afraid.
verses.20:9: Then Abimelech summoned Abraham and said to him, "What have you done to us? And in what way have I sinned against you, that you have brought a great sin upon me and upon my kingdom? You have done to me deeds that should not be done."
verses.20:10: Abimelech also said to Abraham, "What did you see, that you have done this thing?"
verses.20:11: Abraham answered, "Because I thought, 'Surely there is no fear of God in this place, and they will kill me on account of my wife.'
verses.20:12: Furthermore, in truth she is my sister, my father's daughter, yet not my mother's daughter; and she became my wife.
verses.20:13: And when God caused me to wander from my father's house, I said to her, 'This is your kindness that you shall show to me: in every place we come to, say concerning me, "He is my brother."'"
verses.20:14: Then Abimelech took flocks and herds, and male servants and female servants, and gave them to Abraham, and he returned his wife Sarah to him.
verses.20:15: Abimelech said, "Look, my land is before you; settle wherever it is good in your eyes."
verses.20:16: And to Sarah he said, "Look, I have given your brother a thousand pieces of silver; see, it is a covering of the eyes for you before all who are with you, and with everyone you are vindicated."
verses.20:17: Then Abraham prayed to God, and God healed Abimelech, his wife, and his maidservants, so that they gave birth.
verses.20:18: For the LORD had completely closed every womb of the house of Abimelech on account of Sarah, Abraham's wife.
verses.21:1: Now the LORD attended to Sarah just as He had said, and the LORD did for Sarah just as He had spoken.
verses.21:2: And Sarah conceived and bore a son for Abraham in his old age, at the appointed time that God had spoken of.
verses.21:3: Abraham gave the name Isaac to his son who was born to him, whom Sarah had borne to him.
verses.21:4: And Abraham circumcised Isaac his son at eight days old, just as God had commanded him.
verses.21:5: And Abraham was a hundred years old when Isaac his son was born to him.
verses.21:6: And Sarah said, "God has brought about laughter for me; whoever hears will laugh with me."
verses.21:7: And she said, "Who would have told Abraham, 'Sarah would nurse children'? Yet I have borne a son in his old age."
verses.21:8: The child grew and was weaned, and Abraham prepared a great banquet on the day Isaac was weaned.
verses.21:9: But Sarah saw the son of Hagar the Egyptian woman, whom she had borne for Abraham, mocking.
verses.21:10: And she said to Abraham, "Drive out this slave woman and her son, for the son of this slave woman will not inherit with my son, with Isaac."
verses.21:11: And the matter was deeply troubling in the eyes of Abraham on account of his son.
verses.21:12: But God said to Abraham, "Do not let it be troubling in your eyes because of the boy and because of your slave woman. In all that Sarah says to you, listen to her voice, for in Isaac offspring will be named for you.
verses.21:13: And I will also make the son of the slave woman into a nation, for he is your offspring."
verses.21:14: Abraham got up early in the morning, took bread and a skin of water, and gave them to Hagar—placing them on her shoulder—together with the child, and sent her away. And she went and wandered in the wilderness of Beersheba.
verses.21:15: And the water from the skin ran out, and she cast the child beneath one of the shrubs.
verses.21:16: Then she went and sat down by herself across from him at a distance, about a bowshot away, for she said, "Let me not watch the death of the child." And she sat across from him, raised her voice, and wept.
verses.21:17: And God heard the boy's voice, and the angel of God called out to Hagar from heaven and said to her, "What is wrong with you, Hagar? Do not be afraid, for God has listened to the voice of the boy where he is.
verses.21:18: Rise up, lift the boy, and keep a firm hand on him, for I will make a great nation out of him."
verses.21:19: And God opened her eyes, and she saw a well of water; she went and filled the skin with water and gave a drink to the boy.
verses.21:20: And God was with the boy, and he grew up; he settled in the wilderness and became a bowman.
verses.21:21: He settled in the wilderness of Paran, and his mother took for him a wife from the land of Egypt.
verses.21:22: Now at that time, Abimelech and Phicol, the commander of his army, spoke to Abraham and said, "God is with you in everything that you do.
verses.21:23: So now, swear to me by God here that you will not break faith with me, nor with my offspring, nor with my posterity; according to the loyal kindness that I have shown to you, you will show to me and to the land in which you have lived as a foreigner."
verses.21:25: Now Abraham reproved Abimelech on account of the well of water that Abimelech's servants had seized by force.
verses.21:26: And Abimelech said, "I do not know who did this thing; you yourself did not inform me, and I myself have not heard of it until today."
verses.21:27: Then Abraham took flocks and herds and gave them to Abimelech, and both of them made a covenant.
verses.21:28: And Abraham placed seven ewe lambs of the flock by themselves.
verses.21:29: Then Abimelech said to Abraham, "What are these seven ewe lambs that you have placed by themselves?"
verses.21:30: And he said, "You are to take the seven ewe lambs from my hand, in order that it may be a witness for me that I dug this well."
verses.21:31: For this reason he called that place Beersheba, because both of them swore an oath there.
verses.21:32: And they made a covenant at Beersheba; then Abimelech and Phicol, commander of his army, got up and returned to the land of the Philistines.
verses.21:33: Abraham planted a tamarisk tree in Beersheba, and there he called on the name of the LORD, the Eternal God.
verses.21:34: And Abraham lived as a foreigner in the land of the Philistines for many days.
verses.22:1: Now it happened after these events that God tested Abraham, and He said to him, "Abraham." And he said, "Here I am."
verses.22:2: And He said, "Please take your son, your only one, whom you love—Isaac—and go to the land of Moriah, and offer him up there as a burnt offering on one of the mountains that I will tell you about."
verses.22:3: So Abraham got up early in the morning, saddled his donkey, and took with him two of his young men and Isaac his son. He split wood for a burnt offering, then rose and went to the place that God had told him about.
verses.22:4: On the third day, Abraham lifted his eyes and saw the place from far off.
verses.22:5: And Abraham said to his young men, "Remain here with the donkey; the boy and I will go over there, and we will bow down in worship and return to you."
verses.22:6: Then Abraham took the wood for the burnt offering and placed it on Isaac his son; he took the fire and the knife in his hand, and the two of them walked together.
verses.22:7: Then Isaac spoke to Abraham his father and said, "My father!" And he replied, "Here I am, my son." And he said, "Here are the fire and the wood, yet where is the lamb for a burnt offering?"
verses.22:8: Abraham said, "God will see to the lamb for Himself as a burnt offering, my son." And the two of them walked together.
verses.22:9: And they arrived at the place that God had told him about; there Abraham built the altar, set the wood in order, bound Isaac his son, and placed him on the altar, atop the wood.
verses.22:10: And Abraham extended his hand and took the knife to slaughter his son.
verses.22:11: But the angel of the LORD called out to him from heaven and said, "Abraham! Abraham!" And he answered, "Here I am."
verses.22:12: He said, "Do not extend your hand against the boy, nor do anything to him; for now I know that you are one who fears God, and you have not held back your son, your only one, from Me."
verses.22:13: Then Abraham lifted his eyes and looked, and there, behind him, was a ram caught by its horns in the thicket. So Abraham went, took the ram, and offered it up as a burnt offering in place of his son.
verses.22:14: And Abraham called the name of that place The LORD Will See to It, as it is said today, "On the mountain of the LORD it will be seen to."
verses.22:15: And the angel of the LORD called out to Abraham a second time from heaven.
verses.22:16: He said, "By Myself I have sworn—declares the LORD—because you have done this thing and have not held back your son, your only one,
verses.22:17: I will most certainly bless you, and I will abundantly multiply your offspring like the stars of the heavens and like the sand that is on the shore of the sea; and your offspring will take possession of the gate of their enemies.
verses.22:18: And all the nations of the earth will bless themselves by your offspring, because you have listened to My voice."
verses.22:19: Then Abraham returned to his young men; they got up and went together to Beersheba, and Abraham settled in Beersheba.
verses.22:20: Now it happened after these events that it was reported to Abraham, saying, "Look, Milcah too has borne sons to Nahor your brother:
verses.22:21: Uz his firstborn, and Buz his brother, and Kemuel the father of Aram,
verses.22:22: and Chesed, Hazo, Pildash, Jidlaph, and Bethuel."
verses.22:23: And Bethuel fathered Rebekah. Milcah bore these eight to Nahor, the brother of Abraham.
verses.22:24: And his concubine—her name was Reumah—she also bore Tebah, Gaham, Tahash, and Maacah.
verses.23:1: Now Sarah's life was one hundred twenty-seven years, the years of Sarah's life.
verses.23:2: And Sarah died in Kiriath-arba, that is, Hebron, in the land of Canaan; and Abraham came to mourn for Sarah and to weep over her.
verses.23:3: Then Abraham stood up from beside his dead and spoke to the sons of Heth, saying,
verses.23:4: "I am a foreigner and a settler among you. Give me a holding for a burial place among you, so that I may bury my dead out of my presence."
verses.23:5: And the sons of Heth replied to Abraham, saying to him,
verses.23:6: "Listen to us, my lord: you are a prince of God in our midst. In the finest of our burial places, bury your dead. No man among us will withhold his burial place from you to keep you from burying your dead."
verses.23:7: Then Abraham stood up and bowed low to the people of the land, to the sons of Heth.
verses.23:8: And he spoke with them, saying, "If it is your desire that I bury my dead out of my presence, listen to me and appeal to Ephron the son of Zohar for me,
verses.23:9: so that he may give me the cave of Machpelah that belongs to him, which is at the edge of his field. For its full price let him give it to me in your midst as a holding for a burial place."
