verses.23:10: Now Ephron was sitting in the midst of the sons of Heth; and Ephron the Hittite replied to Abraham in the hearing of the sons of Heth, before all who entered the gate of his city, saying,
verses.23:11: "No, my lord, listen to me: the field I give to you, and the cave that is in it, to you I give it. In the sight of the sons of my people I give it to you; bury your dead."
verses.23:12: Then Abraham bowed low before the people of the land.
verses.23:13: And he spoke to Ephron in the hearing of the people of the land, saying, "Only, if you will, please listen to me: I give the silver for the field; take it from me, so that I may bury my dead there."
verses.23:14: And Ephron replied to Abraham, saying to him,
verses.23:15: "My lord, listen to me: land valued at four hundred shekels of silver, between me and you, what is it? Now bury your dead."
verses.23:16: So Abraham listened to Ephron, and Abraham weighed out to Ephron the silver that he had spoken of in the hearing of the sons of Heth, four hundred shekels of silver, current with the merchant.
verses.23:17: So the field of Ephron that was in Machpelah, which was facing Mamre, the field and the cave that was in it, and all the trees that were in the field, which were within its entire boundary all around, stood confirmed
verses.23:18: to Abraham as a purchased property in the sight of the sons of Heth, among all who entered the gate of his city.
verses.23:19: And after this, Abraham buried his wife Sarah in the cave of the field of Machpelah facing Mamre, that is, Hebron, in the land of Canaan.
verses.23:20: Thus the field and the cave that was in it stood confirmed to Abraham as a holding for a burial place from the sons of Heth.
verses.24:1: Now Abraham was old, far along in years, and the LORD had blessed Abraham in everything.
verses.24:2: Abraham said to his servant, the eldest of his household, who ruled over everything that belonged to him, "Please lay your hand under my thigh,
verses.24:3: so that I may make you swear by the LORD, the God of the heavens and the God of the earth, that you will not take a wife for my son from the daughters of the Canaanites, in whose midst I am living;
verses.24:4: instead, you will go to my land and to my relatives, and take a wife for my son, for Isaac."
verses.24:5: The servant said to him, "What if the woman is unwilling to come after me to this land? Should I really bring your son back to the land from which you came out?"
verses.24:6: Abraham said to him, "Be on your guard that you do not bring my son back there.
verses.24:7: The LORD, the God of the heavens, who took me from my father's house and from the land of my birth, and who spoke to me, and who swore to me, saying, 'I will give this land to your offspring,' He will send His angel ahead of you, and you will take a wife for my son from there.
verses.24:8: And if the woman is unwilling to come after you, then you will be clear of this oath of mine; only do not bring my son back there."
verses.24:9: So the servant laid his hand under the thigh of his master Abraham and swore to him regarding this matter.
verses.24:10: Then the servant took ten camels from his master's camels and set out, with all the choicest goods of his master in his hand; so he rose and went to Aram-naharaim, to the city of Nahor.
verses.24:11: He had the camels kneel down outside the city beside the well of water at the time of evening, at the time the women who draw water go out.
verses.24:12: He said, "LORD, God of my master Abraham, please bring about success before me today, and show loyal love to my master Abraham.
verses.24:13: Look, I am stationed beside the spring of water, while the daughters of the men of the city are coming out to draw water.
verses.24:14: Let it be that the young woman to whom I say, 'Please tilt your jar so that I may drink,' and who says, 'Drink, and I will also give your camels a drink,' may she be the one You have designated for Your servant, for Isaac; and through this I will know that You have shown loyal love to my master."
verses.24:15: Now before he had finished speaking, there was Rebekah coming out, who had been born to Bethuel, son of Milcah, the wife of Nahor, Abraham's brother, with her jar on her shoulder.
verses.24:16: Now the young woman was very lovely in appearance, a virgin, and no man had known her. She went down to the spring, filled her jar, and came up.
verses.24:17: Then the servant ran to meet her and said, "Please let me sip a little water from your jar."
verses.24:18: She said, "Drink, my lord." She hurried and lowered her jar onto her hand and gave him a drink.
verses.24:19: Once she had finished giving him a drink, she said, "I will draw water for your camels too, until they have finished drinking."
verses.24:20: She hurried and poured out her jar into the watering trough, then ran again to the well to draw water, and drew for all his camels.
verses.24:21: Meanwhile, the man was watching her in wonder, keeping silent to learn whether the LORD had made his way successful or not.
verses.24:22: When the camels had finished drinking, the man took a gold ring, half a shekel in weight, and two bracelets for her wrists, ten shekels of gold in weight.
verses.24:23: He said, "Whose daughter are you? Please tell me: is there a place in your father's house for us to spend the night?"
verses.24:24: She answered him, "I am the daughter of Bethuel, son of Milcah, whom she bore for Nahor."
verses.24:25: And she said to him, "We have an abundance of both straw and fodder, and a place to spend the night as well."
verses.24:26: Then the man bowed his head and prostrated himself before the LORD.
verses.24:27: He said, "Blessed be the LORD, the God of my master Abraham, who has not abandoned His loyal love and His faithfulness toward my master. As for me, the LORD has guided me along the way to the house of my master's brothers."
verses.24:28: Then the young woman ran and reported to her mother's household about these things.
verses.24:29: Now Rebekah had a brother, and his name was Laban; and Laban ran outside to the man, to the spring.
verses.24:30: As soon as he saw the ring and the bracelets on his sister's wrists, and heard the words of his sister Rebekah, saying, "This is what the man spoke to me," he came to the man, and there he was, standing beside the camels by the spring.
verses.24:31: He said, "Come in, you who are blessed by the LORD! Why are you standing outside, when I have made the house ready, along with a place for the camels?"
verses.24:32: So the man went into the house. He unharnessed the camels and gave straw and fodder to the camels, along with water to wash his feet and the feet of the men who were with him.
verses.24:33: Then something to eat was set before him, but he said, "I will not eat until I have spoken my words." He said, "Speak."
verses.24:35: The LORD has blessed my master exceedingly, and he has become great; He has given him flocks and herds, silver and gold, male and female servants, and camels and donkeys.
verses.24:36: And Sarah, my master's wife, bore a son for my master after she had grown old, and he has given him everything that belongs to him.
verses.24:37: My master made me swear, saying, 'You must not take a wife for my son from the daughters of the Canaanites, in whose land I am living;
verses.24:38: rather, you must go to my father's house and to my clan, and take a wife for my son.'
verses.24:39: I said to my master, 'What if the woman will not come after me?'
verses.24:40: And he said to me, 'The LORD, in whose presence I have walked, will send His angel with you and make your way successful, and you will take a wife for my son from my clan and from my father's house.
verses.24:41: Then you will be clear of my oath once you come to my clan; and if they do not give her to you, you will be clear of my oath.'
verses.24:42: So I came today to the spring and said, 'LORD, God of my master Abraham, if You are indeed making my way successful, on which I am going;
verses.24:43: look, I am stationed beside the spring of water. Let it be that the maiden who comes out to draw water, and to whom I say, "Please give me a little water to drink from your jar,"
verses.24:44: and who says to me, "Drink yourself, and I will also draw water for your camels," may she be the woman whom the LORD has designated for my master's son.'
verses.24:45: Before I had finished speaking in my heart, there was Rebekah coming out with her jar on her shoulder, and she went down to the spring and drew water. I said to her, 'Please give me a drink.'
verses.24:46: She hurried and lowered her jar off her shoulder and said, 'Drink, and I will also give your camels a drink.' So I drank, and she gave the camels a drink as well.
verses.24:47: Then I asked her and said, 'Whose daughter are you?' And she said, 'The daughter of Bethuel, son of Nahor, whom Milcah bore for him.' So I put the ring on her nose and the bracelets on her wrists.
verses.24:48: Then I bowed my head and prostrated myself before the LORD, and blessed the LORD, the God of my master Abraham, who had guided me along the true way to take the daughter of my master's brother for his son.
verses.24:49: And now, if you intend to show loyal love and faithfulness toward my master, tell me; and if not, tell me, so that I may turn to the right or to the left."
verses.24:50: Then Laban and Bethuel answered and said, "From the LORD this matter has come out; we cannot speak either bad or good to you.
verses.24:51: Look, Rebekah is before you; take her and go, and may she become a wife for your master's son, just as the LORD has spoken."
verses.24:52: When Abraham's servant heard their words, he prostrated himself to the ground before the LORD.
verses.24:53: Then the servant brought out silver articles and gold articles, along with garments, and gave them to Rebekah; and choice gifts he gave to her brother and to her mother.
verses.24:54: Then they ate and drank, he and the men who were with him, and spent the night. When they rose in the morning, he said, "Send me off to my master."
verses.24:55: Her brother and her mother said, "Let the young woman stay with us a few days, or ten; afterward she may go."
verses.24:56: He said to them, "Do not detain me, now that the LORD has made my way successful. Send me off so that I may go to my master."
verses.24:57: They said, "Let us call the young woman and ask her directly."
verses.24:58: So they called for Rebekah and said to her, "Will you go with this man?" She replied, "I will go."
verses.24:59: So they sent off their sister Rebekah and her nurse, along with Abraham's servant and his men.
verses.24:60: They blessed Rebekah and said to her, "Our sister, become thousands of ten thousands, and may your offspring take possession of the gate of those who hate them!"
verses.24:61: Then Rebekah rose, along with her female attendants, and they rode on the camels and went after the man. So the servant took Rebekah and set out.
verses.24:62: Now Isaac had come from the approach to Beer-lahai-roi, for he was living in the land of the Negev.
verses.24:63: Isaac went out to meditate in the field as evening approached; he raised his eyes and looked, and there were camels coming.
verses.24:64: Rebekah raised her eyes and saw Isaac, and she slipped down from the camel.
verses.24:65: She said to the servant, "Who is that man over there walking in the field to meet us?" The servant replied, "That is my master." Then she took the veil and covered herself.
verses.24:66: Then the servant recounted to Isaac all the things he had done.
verses.24:67: Isaac brought her into the tent of his mother Sarah; he took Rebekah, and she became his wife, and he loved her. So Isaac found comfort after the death of his mother.
verses.25:1: Then Abraham again took a wife, and her name was Keturah.
verses.25:2: She bore to him Zimran, Jokshan, Medan, Midian, Ishbak, and Shuah.
verses.25:3: Jokshan fathered Sheba and Dedan. The sons of Dedan were Asshurim, Letushim, and Leummim.
verses.25:4: The sons of Midian were Ephah, Epher, Hanoch, Abida, and Eldaah. All of these were the sons of Keturah.
verses.25:5: Abraham gave everything that belonged to him to Isaac.
verses.25:6: But to the sons of the concubines who belonged to Abraham, Abraham gave gifts; and while he was still alive, he sent them away from his son Isaac eastward, to the land of the east.
verses.25:7: Now these are the days of the years of Abraham's life that he lived: one hundred and seventy-five years.
verses.25:8: Then Abraham breathed his last and died at a good old age, old and satisfied, and he was gathered to his people.
verses.25:9: His sons Isaac and Ishmael buried him in the cave of Machpelah, in the field of Ephron son of Zohar the Hittite, which faces Mamre.
verses.25:10: The field that Abraham bought from the sons of Heth—there Abraham was buried, and Sarah his wife.
verses.25:11: After Abraham's death, God blessed his son Isaac; and Isaac settled near Beer-lahai-roi.
verses.25:12: Now these are the generations of Ishmael, Abraham's son, whom Hagar the Egyptian, Sarah's maidservant, bore to Abraham.
verses.25:13: These are the names of the sons of Ishmael, by their names according to their generations: the firstborn of Ishmael, Nebaioth, and Kedar, Adbeel, Mibsam,
verses.25:15: Hadad, Tema, Jetur, Naphish, and Kedemah.
verses.25:16: These are the sons of Ishmael, and these are their names, by their villages and their encampments: twelve princes according to their tribes.
verses.25:17: These are the years of Ishmael's life: one hundred and thirty-seven years. He breathed his last and died, and he was gathered to his people.
verses.25:18: They dwelt from Havilah to Shur, which faces Egypt as you go toward Assyria; he settled opposite all his brothers.
verses.25:19: Now these are the generations of Isaac, Abraham's son: Abraham fathered Isaac.
verses.25:20: Isaac was forty years old when he took Rebekah, daughter of Bethuel the Aramean from Paddan-aram, the sister of Laban the Aramean, to be his wife.
verses.25:21: Isaac pleaded with the LORD on behalf of his wife, because she was barren; and the LORD granted his plea, and Rebekah his wife conceived.
verses.25:22: The children struggled together within her, and she said, "If this is so, why then am I here?" So she went to inquire of the LORD.
verses.25:23: The LORD said to her, "Two nations are in your womb, and two peoples will be separated from inside you; one people will prove stronger than the other, and the older will serve the younger."
verses.25:24: When her days to give birth were fulfilled, look, there were twins in her womb.
verses.25:25: The first came out reddish, all over like a cloak of hair; so they called his name Esau.
verses.25:26: Afterward his brother came out, with his hand grasping Esau's heel, and his name was called Jacob. Now Isaac was sixty years old at their birth.
verses.25:27: The boys grew up, and Esau became a man skilled at hunting, a man of the field, while Jacob was a mild man, dwelling in tents.
verses.25:28: Isaac loved Esau, because game was in his mouth; but Rebekah loved Jacob.
verses.25:29: Now Jacob boiled a stew, and Esau came in from the field, and he was faint.
verses.25:30: Esau said to Jacob, "Please let me gulp down some of that red, red stuff, for I am faint." Therefore his name was called Edom.
verses.25:31: Jacob said, "Sell your birthright to me right now."
verses.25:32: Esau said, "Look, I am about to die; what then is a birthright to me?"
verses.25:33: Jacob said, "Swear to me right now." So he swore to him and sold his birthright to Jacob.
verses.25:34: Then Jacob gave Esau bread and lentil stew; and he ate and drank, and got up and went away. Thus Esau despised the birthright.
verses.26:1: Now there was a famine in the land, besides the first famine that had occurred in the days of Abraham. So Isaac went to Abimelech king of the Philistines, to Gerar.
verses.26:2: The LORD appeared to him and said, "Do not go down to Egypt; dwell in the land of which I will tell you.
verses.26:3: Sojourn in this land, and I will be with you and bless you; for to you and to your offspring I will give all these lands, and I will uphold the oath that I swore to Abraham your father.
verses.26:4: I will multiply your offspring like the stars of the heavens, and I will give to your offspring all these lands; and by your offspring all the nations of the earth will bless themselves,
verses.26:5: because Abraham listened to My voice and observed My charge, My commands, My statutes, and My instructions."
verses.26:7: When the men of the place asked about his wife, he said, "She is my sister," because he was afraid to say, "My wife," thinking, "Otherwise the men of the place might kill me on account of Rebekah," for she was lovely in appearance.
verses.26:8: When his days there had grown long, Abimelech king of the Philistines looked out through the window and saw—there was Isaac caressing Rebekah his wife.
verses.26:9: So Abimelech summoned Isaac and said, "Look, she is surely your wife! How then could you say, 'She is my sister'?" Isaac said to him, "Because I thought, 'Otherwise I might die on account of her.'"
verses.26:10: Abimelech said, "What is this that you have done to us? One of the people very nearly lay with your wife, and you would have brought guilt on us."
verses.26:11: Then Abimelech commanded all the people, saying, "Anyone who touches this man or his wife will surely be put to death."
verses.26:12: Isaac sowed in that land and obtained in that year a hundredfold; and the LORD blessed him.
verses.26:13: The man became great, and he kept growing greater and greater until he had become very great.
verses.26:14: He had possessions of flocks and possessions of herds, and a large household of servants, so the Philistines envied him.
verses.26:15: Now all the wells that his father's servants had dug in the days of his father Abraham—the Philistines had stopped them up and filled them with earth.
verses.26:16: Then Abimelech said to Isaac, "Go away from us, for you have become far mightier than we are."
verses.26:17: So Isaac departed from there, encamped in the valley of Gerar, and settled there.
verses.26:18: Isaac dug again the wells of water that had been dug in the days of Abraham his father, which the Philistines had stopped up after Abraham's death; and he called them by the same names that his father had called them.
verses.26:19: When Isaac's servants dug in the valley, they found there a well of living water.
verses.26:20: The shepherds of Gerar quarreled with Isaac's shepherds, saying, "The water belongs to us!" So he called the name of the well Esek, because they contended with him.
verses.26:21: Then they dug another well, and they quarreled over that one too; so he called its name Sitnah.
verses.26:22: He moved on from there and dug another well, and they did not quarrel over it. So he called its name Rehoboth, and he said, "For now the LORD has made room for us, and we will be fruitful in the land."
verses.26:23: From there he went up to Beersheba.
verses.26:24: The LORD appeared to him on that night and said, "I am the God of Abraham your father. Do not be afraid, for I am with you; I will bless you and multiply your offspring for the sake of My servant Abraham."
verses.26:25: He built an altar there and called on the name of the LORD; he also pitched his tent there, and Isaac's servants dug a well there.
verses.26:26: Then Abimelech went to him from Gerar, with Ahuzzath his friend and Phicol the commander of his army.
verses.26:27: Isaac said to them, "Why have you come to me, when you hate me and have sent me away from you?"
verses.26:28: They said, "We have clearly seen that the LORD has been with you; so we said, 'Let there now be a sworn oath between us, between us and you, and let us make a covenant with you,
verses.26:29: that you will do us no harm, just as we have not touched you and just as we have done only good to you and sent you away in peace.' You are now blessed by the LORD."
verses.26:30: Then he prepared a feast for them, and they ate and drank.
verses.26:31: They rose early in the morning and swore to one another; then Isaac sent them off, and they went away from him in peace.
verses.26:32: On that same day, Isaac's servants came and told him about the well that they had dug, and they said to him, "We have found water!"
verses.26:33: He named it Shibah; for that reason, the name of the city is Beersheba until this day.
verses.26:34: When Esau was forty years old, he took as wives Judith daughter of Beeri the Hittite and Basemath daughter of Elon the Hittite.
verses.26:35: They became a bitterness of spirit to Isaac and to Rebekah.
verses.27:1: And it happened when Isaac had grown old and his eyes became too dim to see, that he called Esau, his older son, and said to him, "My son." And he said to him, "Here I am."
verses.27:2: And he said, "Look now, I have grown old; I do not know the day of my death.
verses.27:3: Now then, please take your equipment, your quiver and your bow, and go out to the field and hunt game for me,
verses.27:4: and make savory dishes for me, just as I love, and bring them to me so that I may eat, in order that my soul may bless you before I die."
verses.27:5: Now Rebekah was listening as Isaac spoke to Esau his son. So Esau went to the field to hunt game to bring back.
verses.27:6: Then Rebekah said to Jacob her son, "Look, I heard your father speaking to Esau your brother, saying,
verses.27:7: 'Bring me game and make savory dishes for me so that I may eat and bless you before the LORD before my death.'
verses.27:8: So now, my son, listen to my voice in what I am commanding you.
verses.27:9: Please go to the flock and take for me from there two good young goats, and I will make them into savory dishes for your father, just as he loves.
verses.27:10: Then you will bring them to your father and he will eat, in order that he may bless you before his death."
verses.27:11: And Jacob said to Rebekah his mother, "Look, Esau my brother is a hairy man, while I am a smooth man.
verses.27:12: Perhaps my father will feel me, and I will be in his eyes like a mocker, and I will bring a curse upon myself and not a blessing."
verses.27:13: And his mother said to him, "Let your curse be upon me, my son; only listen to my voice, and go, take them for me."
verses.27:14: So he went and took them and brought them to his mother, and his mother made savory dishes, just as his father loved.
verses.27:15: Then Rebekah took the finest garments of Esau, her older son, which were with her in the house, and dressed Jacob, her younger son, in them.
verses.27:16: And she put the skins of the young goats over his hands and over the smoothness of his neck.
verses.27:17: Then she placed the savory dishes and the bread that she had made into the hand of Jacob, her son.
verses.27:18: He came to his father and said, "My father." And he said, "Here I am; who are you, my son?"
verses.27:19: Jacob said to his father, "I am Esau, your firstborn. I have done just as you spoke to me. Please rise, sit up, and eat from my game, in order that your soul may bless me."
verses.27:20: Then Isaac said to his son, "How have you been so quick to find it, my son?" And he said, "Because the LORD your God caused it to happen before me."
verses.27:21: And Isaac said to Jacob, "Come near, please, and let me feel you, my son, whether you are indeed my son Esau or not."
verses.27:22: So Jacob came near to Isaac his father, and he felt him and said, "The voice is Jacob's voice, yet the hands are Esau's hands."
verses.27:23: And he did not recognize him, for his hands were hairy like the hands of Esau his brother; so he blessed him.
verses.27:24: And he said, "Are you indeed my son Esau?" And he said, "I am."
verses.27:25: Then he said, "Bring it near to me that I may eat from my son's game, so that my soul may bless you." So he brought it near to him, and he ate; and he brought him wine, and he drank.
verses.27:26: Then Isaac his father said to him, "Come near, please, and kiss me, my son."
verses.27:27: So he came near and kissed him. And he smelled the scent of his garments and blessed him, and said, "See, the scent of my son is like the scent of a field that the LORD has blessed.
verses.27:28: May God give you from the dew of heaven and from the richness of the earth, and plenty of grain and new wine.
verses.27:29: May peoples serve you, and may nations bow down to you. Be master over your brothers, and may your mother's sons bow down to you. Let those who curse you be cursed, and let those who bless you be blessed."
verses.27:30: And it happened, right when Isaac finished blessing Jacob, and Jacob had barely gone out from the presence of Isaac his father, that Esau his brother came in from his hunt.
verses.27:31: He also made savory dishes and brought them to his father, and he said to his father, "Let my father rise and eat from his son's game, in order that your soul may bless me."
verses.27:32: Then Isaac his father said to him, "Who are you?" And he said, "I am your son, your firstborn, Esau."
verses.27:33: Then Isaac trembled with an exceedingly great trembling and said, "Who then is the one who hunted game and brought it to me, so that I ate of all of it before you came, and I blessed him? Yes, and blessed he will be!"
verses.27:34: When Esau heard the words of his father, he cried out with an exceedingly great and bitter cry, and said to his father, "Bless me, even me, my father!"
verses.27:35: And he said, "Your brother came with deceit, and he took your blessing."
verses.27:36: And he said, "Is he not rightly named Jacob, for he has tripped me up these two times? My birthright he took, and look, now he has taken my blessing!" Then he said, "Have you not set aside a blessing for me?"
verses.27:37: Isaac answered and said to Esau, "Look, I have set him as master over you, and all his brothers I have given to him as servants, and with grain and new wine I have sustained him. So for you, then, what can I do, my son?"
verses.27:38: Esau said to his father, "Do you have only one blessing, my father? Bless me, even me, my father!" And Esau lifted up his voice and wept.
verses.27:39: Then Isaac his father answered and said to him, "Look, apart from the richness of the earth your dwelling will be, and apart from the dew of heaven from above.
verses.27:40: By your sword you will live, and your brother you will serve; yet it will happen when you grow restless that you will tear his yoke off your neck."
verses.27:41: So Esau harbored animosity against Jacob because of the blessing with which his father had blessed him. And Esau said in his heart, "The days of mourning for my father are drawing near; then I will kill Jacob my brother."
verses.27:42: Now the words of Esau, her older son, were reported to Rebekah. So she sent and called for Jacob, her younger son, and said to him, "Look, Esau your brother is comforting himself regarding you, intending to kill you.
verses.27:43: So now, my son, listen to my voice: rise, flee to Laban my brother, to Haran,
verses.27:44: and stay with him a few days, until your brother's fury turns away,
verses.27:45: until your brother's anger turns away from you and he forgets what you have done to him. Then I will send and fetch you from there. Why should I be bereaved of both of you in a single day?"
verses.27:46: Then Rebekah said to Isaac, "I loathe my life because of the daughters of Heth. If Jacob takes a wife from the daughters of Heth, like these, from the daughters of the land, what is life to me?"
verses.28:1: Then Isaac called for Jacob and blessed him, and he commanded him and said to him, "You must not take a wife from the daughters of Canaan.
verses.28:2: Rise, go to Paddan-aram, to the house of Bethuel your mother's father, and take a wife for yourself from there, from the daughters of Laban your mother's brother.
verses.28:3: And may God Almighty bless you, and make you fruitful and multiply you, so that you will become an assembly of peoples.
verses.28:4: May He also give to you the blessing of Abraham, to you and to your offspring with you, for you to possess the land of your sojournings, which God gave to Abraham."
verses.28:5: So Isaac sent Jacob off, and he went to Paddan-aram, to Laban the son of Bethuel the Aramean, brother of Rebekah, mother of Jacob and Esau.
verses.28:6: Now Esau saw that Isaac had blessed Jacob and had sent him away to Paddan-aram to take a wife for himself from there, and that in blessing him he had commanded him, saying, "You must not take a wife from the daughters of Canaan."
verses.28:7: And Jacob listened to his father and to his mother, and went to Paddan-aram.
verses.28:8: So Esau saw that the daughters of Canaan were displeasing in the eyes of Isaac his father.
verses.28:9: And Esau went to Ishmael and took Mahalath, the daughter of Ishmael the son of Abraham, sister of Nebaioth, as a wife for himself in addition to his wives.
verses.28:10: Now Jacob went out from Beersheba and went toward Haran.
verses.28:11: And he came upon a certain place and stayed overnight there, because the sun had set. He took one of the stones of the place and set it at his head, and he lay down in that place.
verses.28:12: And he dreamed, and look, a stairway was set up on the earth, with its top reaching to heaven; and look, angels of God were going up and coming down on it.
verses.28:13: And look, the LORD was standing above it and said, "I am the LORD, the God of Abraham your father and the God of Isaac. The land on which you are lying, to you I will give it, and to your offspring.
verses.28:14: And your offspring will be like the dust of the earth, and you will spread out westward and eastward and northward and southward; and in you all the families of the earth will be blessed, and in your offspring.
verses.28:15: And look, I am with you, and I will guard you wherever you go, and I will bring you back to this land; for I will not abandon you until I have done what I have spoken to you."
verses.28:16: Then Jacob woke from his sleep and said, "Truly, the LORD is in this place, and I did not know it!"
verses.28:17: And he was afraid and said, "How awe-inspiring is this place! This is nothing other than the house of God, and this is the gate of heaven."
verses.28:18: Then Jacob rose early in the morning, and he took the stone that he had set at his head and set it up as a pillar, and poured oil over its top.
verses.28:19: And he called the name of that place Bethel; however, Luz was the name of the city formerly.
verses.28:20: Then Jacob vowed a vow, saying, "If God will be with me, and will guard me on this way that I am going, and will give me bread to eat and clothing to wear,
verses.28:21: and I return in peace to my father's house, then the LORD will be my God,
verses.28:22: and this stone, which I have set as a pillar, will be God's house; and of everything that You give me, I will certainly give a tenth of it to You."
verses.29:1: Then Jacob lifted his feet and went to the land of the sons of the east.
verses.29:2: He looked, and there was a well in the field, and there three flocks of sheep were lying beside it, because from that well they would water the flocks; and the stone over the mouth of the well was large.
verses.29:3: All the flocks would be gathered there, and they would roll the stone away from the mouth of the well, water the sheep, and return the stone over the mouth of the well to its place.
verses.29:4: Then Jacob said to them, "My brothers, where are you from?" They answered, "We are from Haran."
verses.29:5: He asked them, "Do you know Laban, son of Nahor?" They replied, "We know him."
verses.29:6: And he said to them, "Is it well with him?" They answered, "It is well, and look, his daughter Rachel is coming with the sheep."
verses.29:7: Then he said, "Look, the day is still high; it is not the time for the livestock to be gathered. Water the sheep, and go graze them."
verses.29:8: They replied, "We cannot until all the flocks have been gathered and they roll the stone away from the mouth of the well; then we will water the sheep."
verses.29:9: While he was still talking with them, Rachel arrived with the sheep that belonged to her father, because she was a shepherdess.
verses.29:10: Now when Jacob saw Rachel, the daughter of Laban his mother's brother, and the sheep of Laban his mother's brother, Jacob stepped forward and rolled the stone away from the mouth of the well, and he watered the sheep of Laban his mother's brother.
verses.29:11: Jacob kissed Rachel, and he lifted his voice and wept.
verses.29:12: Then Jacob told Rachel that he was her father's relative and that he was the son of Rebekah, so she ran and told her father.
verses.29:13: When Laban heard the report about Jacob, his sister's son, he ran to meet him, embraced him, kissed him, and brought him into his house. Then he recounted all these things to Laban.
verses.29:14: And Laban said to him, "Truly, you are my bone and my flesh." So he stayed with him a full month.
verses.29:15: Then Laban said to Jacob, "Just because you are my relative, should you serve me for nothing? Tell me, what should your wages be?"
verses.29:16: Now Laban had two daughters: the older one's name was Leah, and the younger one's name was Rachel.
verses.29:17: Leah's eyes were delicate, while Rachel was beautiful in figure and beautiful in appearance.
verses.29:18: Jacob loved Rachel, and he said, "I will serve you seven years for Rachel, your younger daughter."
verses.29:19: Laban replied, "It is better for me to give her to you than for me to give her to another man; stay with me."
verses.29:20: Jacob served seven years for Rachel, and in his eyes they were like a few days because he loved her.
verses.29:21: Then Jacob said to Laban, "Give me my wife, because my days are fulfilled, so that I may go in to her."
verses.29:22: So Laban gathered all the men of the place and made a banquet.
verses.29:23: When evening came, he took Leah, his daughter, and brought her to him, and he went in to her.
verses.29:24: Laban gave Zilpah, his female servant, to his daughter Leah as a female servant.
verses.29:25: When morning came, look, it was Leah! So he said to Laban, "What is this that you have done to me? Is it not for Rachel that I served with you? And why have you deceived me?"
verses.29:26: Laban answered, "It is not done this way in our place, to give the younger before the firstborn.
verses.29:27: Fulfill the week of this one, and we will give you this one as well, for the service you will serve with me—another seven years."
verses.29:28: Jacob did so and fulfilled the week of this one; then he gave him Rachel, his daughter, to be his wife.
verses.29:29: And Laban gave Bilhah, his female servant, to his daughter Rachel as her female servant.
verses.29:30: Then he went in to Rachel as well, and he also loved Rachel more than Leah; and he served with him another seven years.
verses.29:31: Now the LORD saw that Leah was hated, so He opened her womb, while Rachel was barren.
verses.29:32: Leah conceived and gave birth to a son, and she called his name Reuben, for she said, "Because the LORD has seen my affliction, now my husband will surely love me."
verses.29:33: She conceived again and gave birth to a son, and she said, "Because the LORD has heard that I am hated, He has given me this one as well." So she called his name Simeon.
verses.29:34: She conceived again and gave birth to a son, and she said, "Now this time my husband will be joined to me, because I have given birth to three sons for him." For this reason his name was called Levi.
verses.29:35: She conceived again and gave birth to a son, and she said, "This time I will give thanks to the LORD." For this reason she called his name Judah. Then she stopped giving birth.
verses.30:1: Rachel saw that she had borne no children to Jacob, and Rachel grew envious of her sister; so she said to Jacob, "Give me children, and if not, I will die."
verses.30:2: Jacob's anger blazed against Rachel, and he said, "Am I in God's place, who has held back the fruit of the womb from you?"
verses.30:3: She said, "Here is my maidservant Bilhah. Go in to her, that she may bear on my knees and I too may be built up from her."
verses.30:4: Then she gave him Bilhah, her female servant, as a wife, and Jacob went in to her.
verses.30:5: Bilhah conceived and bore a son to Jacob.
verses.30:6: Rachel said, "God has done me justice, and He has also listened to my voice and given me a son." For that reason she called his name Dan.
verses.30:7: Bilhah, Rachel's female servant, conceived again and bore a second son to Jacob.
verses.30:8: Rachel said, "With wrestlings of God I have wrestled with my sister, and I have also prevailed." So she called his name Naphtali.
verses.30:9: When Leah saw that she had stopped giving birth, she took Zilpah, her female servant, and gave her to Jacob as a wife.
verses.30:10: Zilpah, Leah's female servant, bore a son to Jacob.
verses.30:11: Leah said, "Fortune has come!" So she called his name Gad.
verses.30:12: Zilpah, Leah's female servant, bore a second son to Jacob.
verses.30:13: Leah said, "What happiness is mine! For women will call me happy." So she called his name Asher.
verses.30:14: Reuben went out during the days of the wheat harvest, found mandrakes in the field, and brought them to Leah, his mother. Rachel said to Leah, "Give me some of your son's mandrakes, please."
verses.30:15: But she said to her, "Is it too little that you have taken my husband, that you would also take my son's mandrakes?" And Rachel said, "Then he will lie with you tonight in exchange for your son's mandrakes."
verses.30:16: Jacob came from the field in the evening, and Leah went out to meet him and said, "You are to come in to me, for I have indeed hired you with my son's mandrakes." And he lay with her that night.
verses.30:17: God listened to Leah, and she conceived and bore a fifth son to Jacob.
verses.30:18: Leah said, "God has given me my wages, since I gave my female servant to my husband." So she called his name Issachar.
verses.30:19: Leah conceived again and bore a sixth son to Jacob.
verses.30:20: Leah said, "God has bestowed a good gift on me; this time my husband will honor me, for I have borne six sons to him." So she called his name Zebulun.
verses.30:21: After that she bore a daughter, and she called her name Dinah.
verses.30:22: God remembered Rachel; God listened to her and opened her womb.
verses.30:23: She conceived and bore a son, and she said, "God has removed my disgrace."
verses.30:24: She called his name Joseph, saying, "May the LORD add another son for me."
verses.30:25: Now when Rachel had given birth to Joseph, Jacob said to Laban, "Send me away, so that I may go to my place and to my land.
verses.30:26: Give me my wives and my children for whom I have served you, and let me go; for you yourself know my service with which I have served you."
verses.30:27: Laban said to him, "Please, if I have found favor in your eyes—I have learned through divination that the LORD has blessed me on account of you."
verses.30:28: And he said, "Specify your wages to me, and I will give them."
verses.30:29: He said to him, "You yourself know the way I have served you, and what your livestock has become with me.
verses.30:30: For what you had before I came was little, and it has increased into abundance, and the LORD has blessed you wherever I set foot. And now, when will I too provide for my household?"
verses.30:31: He said, "What should I give you?" And Jacob said, "Do not give me anything; if you will do this thing for me, I will again tend your flock and watch over it.
verses.30:32: Let me pass through all your flock today, removing from there every speckled and spotted animal, and every dark-colored animal among the sheep, and the spotted and speckled among the goats; and such will be my wages.
verses.30:33: And my righteousness will testify for me in time to come, when it comes before you regarding my wages: every one with me that is not speckled and spotted among the goats and dark-colored among the sheep is stolen."
verses.30:34: Laban said, "Yes, may it be according to your word."
verses.30:35: On that day he removed the striped and spotted male goats and all the speckled and spotted female goats, every one with white on it, and every dark-colored one among the sheep, and gave them into the hand of his sons.
verses.30:36: He set a three days' journey between himself and Jacob, while Jacob was tending the remaining flocks of Laban.
verses.30:37: Then Jacob took for himself fresh rods of poplar, almond, and plane, and peeled white strips on them, laying bare the white that was on the rods.
verses.30:38: He set the rods that he had peeled in the channels, in the water troughs where the flocks came to drink, directly opposite the flocks; and they bred when they came to drink.
verses.30:39: And the flocks bred before the rods, and the flocks bore striped, speckled, and spotted ones.
verses.30:40: Jacob separated the sheep, and turned the faces of the flocks toward the striped and every dark-colored one in Laban's flock; and he placed droves apart for himself, and did not place them with Laban's flock.
verses.30:41: Whenever the sturdy ones of the flocks were breeding, Jacob would put the rods before the eyes of the flocks in the channels, so that they would breed among the rods;
verses.30:42: but when the flocks were feeble, he would not put them. So the feeble ones became Laban's, and the sturdy ones became Jacob's.
verses.30:43: So the man increased exceedingly, and he came to have many flocks, and female servants and male servants, and camels and donkeys.
verses.31:1: Then he heard the words of the sons of Laban, saying, "Jacob has taken everything that belonged to our father, and out of what belonged to our father he has made all this wealth."
verses.31:2: Jacob saw Laban's face, and look, it was not toward him as yesterday and the day before.
verses.31:3: And the LORD said to Jacob, "Return to the land of your fathers and to your birthplace, and I will be with you."
verses.31:4: So Jacob sent and summoned Rachel and Leah to the field, to his flock,
verses.31:5: and said to them, "I see your father's face, that it is not toward me as yesterday and the day before, yet the God of my father has been with me.
verses.31:6: And you yourselves know that with all my strength I have served your father.
verses.31:7: Yet your father has cheated me and changed my wages ten times, but God did not allow him to do harm to me.
verses.31:8: If he spoke like this, 'The speckled will be your wages,' then all the flock bore speckled ones; and if he spoke like this, 'The striped will be your wages,' then all the flock bore striped ones.
verses.31:9: So God has taken away the livestock of your father and given it to me.
verses.31:10: And it happened at the time the flock was mating that I lifted up my eyes and saw in a dream, and look, the male goats mounting the flock were striped, speckled, and dappled.
verses.31:11: Then the angel of God said to me in the dream, 'Jacob,' and I said, 'Here I am.'
verses.31:12: And He said, 'Lift up your eyes now and see: all the male goats mounting the flock are striped, speckled, and dappled, for I have seen everything that Laban is doing to you.
verses.31:13: I am the God of Bethel, where you anointed a pillar, where you vowed a vow to Me. Now rise, go out from this land, and return to the land of your birth.'"
verses.31:14: Then Rachel and Leah replied and said to him, "Do we still have a portion and inheritance in the house of our father?
verses.31:15: Are we not counted as foreigners by him? For he has sold us, and has also utterly consumed our money.
verses.31:16: Indeed, all the riches that God has taken away from our father belong to us and to our children. Now then, do everything that God has said to you."
verses.31:17: Then Jacob rose up and lifted his children and his wives onto the camels.
verses.31:18: And he drove away all his livestock and all his property that he had amassed, the livestock of his own acquiring that he had amassed in Paddan-aram, to go to Isaac his father, to the land of Canaan.
verses.31:19: Now Laban had gone to shear his flock, and Rachel stole the household idols that belonged to her father.
verses.31:20: So Jacob deceived Laban the Aramean, in that he did not tell him that he was fleeing.
verses.31:21: So he fled, he and all that belonged to him; he arose and crossed over the River, and set his face toward the hill country of Gilead.
verses.31:22: And it was reported to Laban on the third day that Jacob had fled.
verses.31:23: So he took his kinsmen with him and pursued after him a journey of seven days, and he caught up with him in the hill country of Gilead.
verses.31:24: But God came to Laban the Aramean in a dream by night and said to him, "Guard yourself so that you do not speak with Jacob either good or bad."
verses.31:25: So Laban overtook Jacob. Now Jacob had pitched his tent in the hill country, and Laban with his kinsmen pitched camp in the hill country of Gilead.
verses.31:26: Then Laban said to Jacob, "What have you done, that you deceived me and drove off my daughters like captives of the sword?
verses.31:27: Why did you flee in secret and deceive me, and did not tell me, so that I could have sent you off with gladness and with songs, with tambourine and with lyre?
verses.31:28: And you did not permit me to kiss my sons and my daughters. Now you have acted foolishly in doing so.
verses.31:29: It is within the power of my hand to do harm to you, but the God of your father said to me last night, 'Guard yourself from speaking with Jacob either good or bad.'
verses.31:30: And now, you have indeed departed because you yearned deeply for the house of your father—why did you steal my gods?"
verses.31:31: Then Jacob answered and said to Laban, "Because I was afraid, for I thought you might forcibly take your daughters from me.
verses.31:32: The person with whom you find your gods shall not live. Before our kinsmen, identify for yourself whatever is with me and take it for yourself." Now Jacob did not know that Rachel had stolen them.
verses.31:33: So Laban went into Jacob's tent and into Leah's tent and into the tent of the two female servants, but he did not find them. Then he went out from Leah's tent and went into Rachel's tent.
verses.31:34: Now Rachel had taken the household idols, placed them in the camel's saddle, and sat on them. And Laban felt through the whole tent, but did not find them.
verses.31:35: And she said to her father, "May my lord not be angry that I am unable to stand up before you, for the way of women is upon me." So he searched, yet he did not find the household idols.
verses.31:36: Then Jacob grew angry and contended with Laban; and Jacob answered and said to Laban, "What is my transgression? What is my sin, that you have hotly pursued after me?
verses.31:37: Now that you have felt through all my belongings, what have you found from all the belongings of your house? Place it here before my kinsmen and your kinsmen, so that they may judge between the two of us.
verses.31:38: These twenty years I have been with you: your ewes and your female goats have not miscarried, and the rams of your flock I have not eaten.
verses.31:39: What was torn by wild animals I did not bring to you; I myself bore the loss of it. From my hand you demanded it, whether stolen by day or stolen by night.
verses.31:40: So I was: by day scorching heat consumed me, and frost by night, and my sleep fled from my eyes.
verses.31:41: These twenty years I have spent in your house—I served you fourteen years for your two daughters, and six years for your flock, yet you changed my wages ten times.
verses.31:42: Had the God of my father, the God of Abraham and the Fear of Isaac, not been for me, indeed by now you would have sent me off empty-handed. My affliction and the toil of my hands God saw, and He passed judgment last night."
verses.31:43: Then Laban answered and said to Jacob, "The daughters are my daughters, and the children are my children, and the flock is my flock, and everything that you see belongs to me. Yet what can I do today to these daughters of mine, or to their children whom they have borne?
verses.31:44: Now then, come, let us make a covenant, I and you, and let it serve as a witness between me and you."
verses.31:45: Then Jacob took a stone and raised it up as a pillar.
verses.31:46: And Jacob said to his kinsmen, "Gather stones." So they took stones and made a heap, and they ate there beside the heap.
verses.31:47: And Laban named it Jegar-sahadutha, while Jacob named it Galeed.
verses.31:48: Then Laban said, "This heap is a witness between me and you today." Therefore its name was called Galeed.
verses.31:49: And Mizpah, for he said, "May the LORD keep watch between me and you when we are hidden from one another.
verses.31:50: If you afflict my daughters, or if you take wives besides my daughters—no man is with us—see, God is a witness between me and you."
verses.31:52: This heap is a witness, and the pillar is a witness, that I will not pass beyond this heap to you, and that you will not pass beyond this heap and this pillar to me, for harm.
verses.31:53: May the God of Abraham and the God of Nahor judge between us, the God of their father." And Jacob swore by the Fear of his father Isaac.
verses.31:54: Then Jacob offered a sacrifice in the hill country and invited his kinsmen to eat bread; so they ate bread and lodged in the hill country.
verses.32:1: Laban got up early in the morning, kissed his sons and his daughters, and blessed them. Then Laban left and returned to his place.
verses.32:2: And Jacob went on his way, and the angels of God encountered him.
verses.32:3: When Jacob saw them, he said, "This is the camp of God." And he called the name of that place Mahanaim.
verses.32:4: Then Jacob sent messengers ahead of him to Esau his brother, to the land of Seir, the territory of Edom.
verses.32:5: He commanded them, saying, "Say this to my lord Esau: 'Your servant Jacob says this: I have sojourned with Laban and remained until now.
verses.32:6: I now have oxen and donkeys, flocks, and male and female servants, and I have sent to inform my lord, so that I may find favor in your sight.'"
verses.32:7: The messengers returned to Jacob and said, "We went to your brother Esau, and moreover he is coming to meet you, and four hundred men are with him."
verses.32:8: Jacob became very afraid and distressed, and he divided the people who were with him, along with the flocks, the herds, and the camels, into two camps.
verses.32:9: He said, "If Esau comes to the one camp and strikes it, then the remaining camp will escape."
verses.32:10: Then Jacob said, "God of my father Abraham and God of my father Isaac, LORD, who said to me, 'Return to your land and to your relatives, and I will deal well with you,'
verses.32:11: I am unworthy of all the acts of loyal love and of all the faithfulness that You have shown to Your servant, for with my staff I crossed over this Jordan, and now I have become two camps.
verses.32:12: Rescue me, please, from the hand of my brother, from the hand of Esau, for I am afraid of him, that he may come and strike me, mother along with children.
verses.32:13: Yet You Yourself said, 'I will surely deal well with you, and I will make your offspring like the sand of the sea, which cannot be counted because of its abundance.'"
verses.32:14: So he lodged there that night, and from what had come into his hand he took a gift for Esau his brother:
verses.32:15: two hundred female goats and twenty male goats; two hundred ewes and twenty rams;
verses.32:16: thirty nursing camels along with their young; forty cows and ten bulls; twenty female donkeys and ten male donkeys.
verses.32:17: He placed them in the hand of his servants, each herd by itself, and said to his servants, "Pass ahead of me, and leave a space between one herd and the next."
verses.32:18: He commanded the first one, saying, "When Esau my brother meets you and asks you, 'Whose are you, where are you going, and to whom do these ahead of you belong?'
verses.32:19: then you shall say, 'They belong to your servant Jacob; it is a gift sent to my lord Esau, and look, he also is behind us.'"
verses.32:20: He commanded the second as well, and the third, and all those walking behind the herds, saying, "You shall speak this same message to Esau when you find him,
verses.32:21: and you shall also say, 'Look, your servant Jacob is behind us.'" For he said, "Let me appease his face with the gift going ahead of me, and afterward I will see his face; perhaps he will accept me."
verses.32:22: So the gift passed ahead of him, while he himself lodged in the camp that night.
verses.32:23: During that night he got up, took his two wives, his two female servants, and his eleven children, and crossed over the ford of the Jabbok.
verses.32:24: He took them and had them cross the stream, and he sent across what belonged to him.
verses.32:25: Jacob was left alone, and a man wrestled with him until the rising of dawn.
verses.32:26: When he saw that he could not prevail over him, he touched the socket of his hip, and the socket of Jacob's hip became dislocated during his wrestling with him.
verses.32:27: Then he said, "Release me, because the dawn has risen." But he said, "I will not release you unless you bless me."
verses.32:28: He said to him, "What is your name?" And he replied, "Jacob."
verses.32:29: Then he said, "No longer will your name be called Jacob, but Israel, because you have contended with God and with men, and you have prevailed."
verses.32:30: Then Jacob asked, saying, "Tell me your name, please." And he said, "Why do you ask about my name?" Then he blessed him there.
verses.32:31: So Jacob called the name of the place Peniel: "For I have seen God face to face, yet my life has been rescued."
verses.32:32: The sun rose over him as he passed by Penuel, while he was limping on his hip.
verses.32:33: Therefore the sons of Israel do not eat the sciatic sinew that is on the socket of the hip to this day, because he touched the socket of Jacob's hip at the sciatic sinew.
verses.33:1: Jacob raised his eyes and looked, and now Esau was coming, and with him were four hundred men. So he divided the children among Leah, Rachel, and the two female servants.
verses.33:2: He placed the female servants and their children first, Leah and her children after them, and Rachel and Joseph last.
verses.33:3: He himself passed in front of them, bowing down to the ground seven times until he approached his brother.
verses.33:4: Yet Esau ran to meet him, embraced him, fell upon his neck, and kissed him; and they wept.
verses.33:5: Then he raised his eyes and saw the women and the children, and he said, "Who are these with you?" He replied, "The children with whom God has favored your servant."
verses.33:6: Then the female servants, they and their children, approached and bowed down.
verses.33:7: Leah also approached with her children, and they bowed down; and afterward Joseph and Rachel approached and bowed down.
verses.33:8: Then he asked, "What do you mean by this entire camp that I met?" And he replied, "To find favor in my lord's sight."
verses.33:9: But Esau said, "I have plenty, my brother; let what is yours remain yours."
verses.33:10: Jacob replied, "No, please! If indeed I have found favor in your sight, then take my gift from my hand, for truly I have seen your face as though seeing the face of God, and you have accepted me favorably.
verses.33:11: Please take my blessing that has been brought to you, because God has favored me and because I have everything." So he pressed him, and he took it.
verses.33:12: Then he said, "Let us set out and go on, and I will go in front of you."
verses.33:13: But he said to him, "My lord knows that the children are delicate, and the flocks and the herds are nursing under my care; if they are driven hard for a single day, all the flocks will die.
verses.33:14: May my lord please pass ahead of his servant, and I myself will move along slowly, matching the pace of the livestock in front of me and the pace of the children, until I come to my lord at Seir."
verses.33:15: Then Esau said, "Let me station with you some of the people who are with me, please." But he replied, "Why is that needed? May I find favor in my lord's sight."
verses.33:16: So on that day Esau turned back on his way to Seir.
verses.33:17: Jacob, however, traveled to Succoth; he built a house for himself, and for his livestock he made shelters. Therefore he called the name of the place Succoth.
verses.33:18: Jacob arrived safely at the city of Shechem, which is in the land of Canaan, upon arriving from Paddan-aram, and he encamped facing the city.
verses.33:19: He purchased the portion of the field on which he had pitched his tent from the hand of the sons of Hamor, the father of Shechem, for a hundred kesitahs.
verses.33:20: He set up an altar there and called it El-Elohe-Israel.
verses.34:1: Dinah, Leah's daughter whom she had borne to Jacob, went out to see the daughters of the land.
verses.34:2: Shechem, the son of Hamor the Hivite, ruler of the land, saw her, and he took her, lay with her, and violated her.
verses.34:3: His soul clung to Dinah, daughter of Jacob; he loved the young woman and spoke to the heart of the young woman.
verses.34:4: Shechem said to Hamor his father, "Get this girl for me as a wife."
verses.34:5: Jacob heard that he had defiled his daughter Dinah; his sons were with his livestock in the field, so Jacob remained silent until they came.
verses.34:6: Hamor, Shechem's father, went out to Jacob to speak with him.
verses.34:7: Jacob's sons came from the field as soon as they heard, and the men were grieved and exceedingly angry, because he had committed a disgraceful deed in Israel by lying with Jacob's daughter—and such a thing must not be done.
verses.34:8: Hamor spoke with them, saying, "My son Shechem—his soul longs for your daughter. Please give her to him as a wife.
verses.34:9: And form marriage ties with us: you will give us your daughters, and you will take our daughters for yourselves.
verses.34:10: With us you will dwell, and the land will be before you; dwell, trade through it, and take possession in it."
verses.34:11: Then Shechem said to her father and to her brothers, "May I find favor in your eyes; whatever you tell me, I will give.
verses.34:12: Make the bride-price and gift very great for me, and I will give just as you say to me; and give me the young woman as a wife."
verses.34:13: Jacob's sons answered Shechem and Hamor his father with deceit and spoke, because he had defiled Dinah their sister.
verses.34:14: And they said to them, "We are not able to do this thing—to give our sister to a man who has a foreskin—for that is a disgrace to us.
verses.34:15: Only on this basis will we consent to you: if you become like us, by having every male among you circumcised.
verses.34:16: Then we will give our daughters to you, and your daughters we will take for ourselves; we will dwell with you, and we will become one people.
verses.34:17: But if you do not listen to us so as to be circumcised, we will take our daughter and depart."
verses.34:18: Their words were good in the eyes of Hamor and in the eyes of Shechem, the son of Hamor.
verses.34:19: The young man did not delay in doing the thing, for he took delight in the daughter of Jacob; and he was more honored than all of his father's house.
verses.34:20: Hamor and Shechem his son came to the gate of their city, and they spoke to the men of their city, saying,
verses.34:21: "These men are at peace with us; let them dwell in the land and trade through it, for look, the land is broad on every side before them. Their daughters we will take for ourselves as wives, and our daughters we will give to them.
verses.34:22: Only on this basis will the men consent to us to dwell with us, to become one people: by having every male among us circumcised, just as they are circumcised.
verses.34:23: Their livestock and their property and all their animals—will they not be ours? Let us only consent to them, and they will dwell with us."
verses.34:24: So all those who went out through the gate of his city listened to Hamor and to Shechem his son, and every male was circumcised—all those who went out through the gate of his city.
verses.34:25: Now on the third day, while they were in pain, two of Jacob's sons, Simeon and Levi, Dinah's brothers, each took his sword, came against the unsuspecting city, and killed every male.
verses.34:26: Hamor and Shechem his son they killed by the edge of the sword, and they took Dinah from Shechem's house and went out.
verses.34:27: The sons of Jacob came upon those who had been killed and plundered the city, because they had defiled their sister.
verses.34:28: Their flocks, their herds, and their donkeys, and what was in the city and what was in the field, they took.
verses.34:29: And all their wealth, all their little ones, and their wives they took captive and plundered, and all that was in the house.
verses.34:30: And Jacob said to Simeon and to Levi, "You have brought trouble upon me by making me a stench among the inhabitants of the land, among the Canaanites and the Perizzites. And I am few in number; they will gather against me and strike me down, and I will be destroyed, I and my household."
verses.34:31: They replied, "Is he to treat our sister like a prostitute?"
verses.35:1: Then God said to Jacob, "Rise, go up to Bethel and settle there, and make an altar there to the God who appeared to you when you were fleeing from Esau your brother."
verses.35:2: Then Jacob said to his household and to all those with him, "Remove the foreign gods that are in your midst, and purify yourselves and change your clothes.
verses.35:3: Let us rise and go up to Bethel, that I may make an altar there to the God who answered me in the day of my distress and has been with me on the way that I have gone."
verses.35:4: So they gave Jacob all the foreign gods that were in their hands, together with the rings that were in their ears; and Jacob hid them beneath the terebinth that was by Shechem.
verses.35:5: Then they set out, and a terror from God was upon the cities around them, so they did not pursue Jacob's sons.
verses.35:6: Jacob came to Luz, which is in the land of Canaan—that is, Bethel—he and all the people who were with him.
verses.35:7: There he built an altar and called the place El-bethel, because God had revealed Himself to him there when he was fleeing from his brother.
verses.35:8: And Deborah, the nurse of Rebekah, died and was buried below Bethel, beneath the oak; and he called its name Allon-bacuth.
verses.35:9: God appeared once more to Jacob when he came from Paddan-aram, and blessed him.
verses.35:10: And God said to him, "Your name is Jacob; your name will not be called Jacob any longer; rather, Israel will be your name." So He called his name Israel.
verses.35:11: Then God said to him, "I am God Almighty; be fruitful and multiply. A nation and an assembly of nations will arise from you, and kings will come out from your loins.
verses.35:12: The land that I gave to Abraham and to Isaac, to you I will give it; and to your offspring after you I will give the land."
verses.35:13: And God ascended from him at the place where He had spoken with him.
verses.35:14: Then Jacob set up a pillar at the place where He had spoken with him, a pillar of stone; he poured a drink offering upon it and poured oil upon it.
verses.35:15: And Jacob called the place where God had spoken with him by the name Bethel.
verses.35:16: Then they set out from Bethel; while there was still some distance to reach Ephrath, Rachel went into labor, and she had severe difficulty in giving birth.
verses.35:17: As she was having severe difficulty in giving birth, the midwife said to her, "Do not be afraid, for this one also is a son for you."
verses.35:18: And as her soul was leaving—for she was dying—she called his name Ben-oni, but his father called him Benjamin.
verses.35:19: Rachel died and was buried along the way to Ephrath—that is, Bethlehem.
verses.35:20: And Jacob erected a pillar upon her burial place; it is the pillar of Rachel's burial place to this day.
verses.35:22: Now while Israel was living in that land, Reuben went and lay with his father's concubine Bilhah, and Israel heard of it. And the sons of Jacob were twelve.
verses.35:23: The sons of Leah: Jacob's firstborn Reuben, and Simeon, Levi, Judah, Issachar, and Zebulun.
verses.35:24: The sons of Rachel: Joseph and Benjamin.
verses.35:25: And the sons of Bilhah, Rachel's maidservant: Dan and Naphtali.
verses.35:26: And the sons of Zilpah, Leah's maidservant: Gad and Asher. These are Jacob's sons who were born to him in Paddan-aram.
verses.35:27: Then Jacob came to Isaac his father at Mamre, Kiriath-arba—that is, Hebron—where Abraham and Isaac had sojourned.
verses.35:28: And Isaac's days were one hundred and eighty years.
verses.35:29: Then Isaac breathed his last, died, and was gathered to his people, old and full of days; and Esau and Jacob, his sons, buried him.
verses.36:1: And these are the generations of Esau; he is Edom.
verses.36:2: Esau took his wives from among the daughters of Canaan: Adah, daughter of Elon the Hittite; and Oholibamah, daughter of Anah, daughter of Zibeon the Hivite;
verses.36:3: and Basemath, daughter of Ishmael, sister of Nebaioth.
verses.36:4: Adah gave birth to Eliphaz for Esau, and Basemath gave birth to Reuel,
verses.36:5: and Oholibamah gave birth to Jeush, Jalam, and Korah. These are Esau's sons who were born to him in the land of Canaan.
verses.36:6: Then Esau took his wives, his sons, his daughters, and all the persons of his household, and his livestock, all his animals, and all his property that he had acquired in the land of Canaan, and he went to a land away from Jacob his brother.
verses.36:7: For their possessions were too abundant for them to live together, and the land of their sojournings was unable to sustain them because of their livestock.
verses.36:8: And Esau settled in the highlands of Seir; Esau is Edom.
verses.36:9: And these are the generations of Esau, the father of Edom, in the highlands of Seir.
verses.36:10: These are the names of the sons of Esau: Eliphaz, son of Adah, wife of Esau; Reuel, son of Basemath, wife of Esau.
verses.36:11: Now the sons of Eliphaz were Teman, Omar, Zepho, Gatam, and Kenaz.
verses.36:12: And Timna was a concubine to Eliphaz, son of Esau, and she gave birth to Amalek for Eliphaz. These are the sons of Adah, wife of Esau.
verses.36:13: And these are the sons of Reuel: Nahath and Zerah, Shammah and Mizzah. These were the sons of Basemath, wife of Esau.
verses.36:14: And these were the sons of Oholibamah, daughter of Anah, daughter of Zibeon, wife of Esau: she gave birth to Jeush, Jalam, and Korah for Esau.
verses.36:15: These are the chiefs of the sons of Esau. The sons of Eliphaz, Esau's firstborn: Chief Teman, Chief Omar, Chief Zepho, Chief Kenaz,
verses.36:16: Chief Korah, Chief Gatam, Chief Amalek. These are the chiefs of Eliphaz in the land of Edom; these are the sons of Adah.
verses.36:17: And these are the sons of Reuel, son of Esau: Chief Nahath, Chief Zerah, Chief Shammah, Chief Mizzah. These are the chiefs of Reuel in the land of Edom; these are the sons of Basemath, wife of Esau.
verses.36:18: And these are the sons of Oholibamah, wife of Esau: Chief Jeush, Chief Jalam, Chief Korah. These are the chiefs of Oholibamah, daughter of Anah, wife of Esau.
verses.36:19: These are the sons of Esau, and these are their chiefs; he is Edom.
verses.36:20: These are the sons of Seir the Horite, residents of the land: Lotan, Shobal, Zibeon, Anah,
verses.36:21: Dishon, Ezer, and Dishan. These are the Horite chiefs, the sons of Seir, in the land of Edom.
verses.36:22: Now the sons of Lotan were Hori and Hemam, and the sister of Lotan was Timna.
verses.36:23: And these are the sons of Shobal: Alvan, Manahath, and Ebal; Shepho and Onam.
verses.36:24: And these are the sons of Zibeon: Aiah and Anah. This is the Anah who found the hot springs in the wilderness while he was tending the donkeys for his father Zibeon.
verses.36:25: And these are the children of Anah: Dishon, and Oholibamah, daughter of Anah.
verses.36:26: And these are the sons of Dishan: Hemdan, Eshban, Ithran, and Cheran.
verses.36:27: These are Ezer's sons: Bilhan, Zaavan, and Akan.
verses.36:28: These are Dishan's sons: Uz and Aran.
verses.36:29: These are the Horite chiefs: Chief Lotan, Chief Shobal, Chief Zibeon, Chief Anah,
verses.36:30: Chief Dishon, Chief Ezer, Chief Dishan. These are the Horite chiefs, according to their chiefdoms, in the land of Seir.
verses.36:31: And these are the kings who reigned in the land of Edom before a king reigned over the sons of Israel:
verses.36:32: Now Bela, son of Beor, reigned in Edom, and the name of his city was Dinhabah.
verses.36:33: And Bela died, and Jobab, son of Zerah, from Bozrah, reigned in his place.
verses.36:34: And Jobab died, and Husham, from the land of the Temanites, reigned in his place.
verses.36:35: And Husham died, and Hadad, son of Bedad, who struck down Midian in the field of Moab, reigned in his place; and the name of his city was Avith.
verses.36:36: And Hadad died, and Samlah, from Masrekah, reigned in his place.
verses.36:37: And Samlah died, and Shaul, from Rehoboth by the river, reigned in his place.
verses.36:38: And Shaul died, and Baal-hanan, son of Achbor, reigned in his place.
verses.36:39: And Baal-hanan, son of Achbor, died, and Hadar reigned in his place; and the name of his city was Pau, and the name of his wife was Mehetabel, daughter of Matred, daughter of Mezahab.
verses.36:40: And these are the names of the chiefs of Esau, according to their families, according to their places, by their names: Chief Timna, Chief Alvah, Chief Jetheth,
verses.36:41: Chief Oholibamah, Chief Elah, Chief Pinon,
verses.36:42: Chief Kenaz, Chief Teman, Chief Mibzar,
verses.36:43: Chief Magdiel, Chief Iram. These are the chiefs of Edom, according to their settlements in the land of their possession. He is Esau, the father of Edom.
verses.37:1: Jacob settled in the land of his father's sojournings, in the land of Canaan.
verses.37:2: These are the generations of Jacob. Joseph, when he was seventeen years old, was tending the flock with his brothers; he was a youth with the sons of Bilhah and with the sons of Zilpah, his father's wives. And Joseph brought a bad report about them to their father.
verses.37:3: Now Israel loved Joseph more than all his sons, because he was the son of his old age, and he made for him a long-sleeved tunic.
verses.37:4: When his brothers saw that their father loved him above all his brothers, they hated him and were unable to speak to him in peace.
verses.37:5: Then Joseph dreamed a dream and told it to his brothers, and they hated him all the more.
verses.37:6: He said to them, "Please listen to this dream that I have dreamed.
verses.37:7: Look, we were binding sheaves in the middle of the field, and see, my sheaf rose up and stood upright too; and look, your sheaves gathered around and bowed down to my sheaf."
verses.37:8: His brothers said to him, "Will you really reign over us, or will you truly rule over us?" So they hated him all the more on account of his dreams and on account of his words.
verses.37:9: Then he dreamed yet another dream and recounted it to his brothers. He said, "Look, I have dreamed a dream again, and see, the sun and the moon and eleven stars were bowing down to me."
verses.37:10: He recounted it to his father and to his brothers, and his father rebuked him and said to him, "What is this dream that you have dreamed? Shall we truly come—I and your mother and your brothers—to bow down to you to the ground?"
verses.37:11: His brothers envied him, while his father held the matter in mind.
verses.37:12: Now his brothers went to pasture their father's flock in Shechem.
verses.37:13: Israel said to Joseph, "Are your brothers not shepherding in Shechem? Come, and I will send you to them." And he said to him, "Here I am."
verses.37:14: So he said to him, "Please go, see to the welfare of your brothers and the welfare of the flock, and bring word back to me." He sent him from the valley of Hebron, and he came to Shechem.
verses.37:15: A man found him, and look, he was wandering in the field; and the man asked him, saying, "What are you seeking?"
verses.37:16: He said, "It is my brothers I am seeking. Please tell me where they are shepherding."
verses.37:17: The man said, "They have moved on from here, for I heard them saying, 'Let us go to Dothan.'" So Joseph went after his brothers and found them in Dothan.
verses.37:18: They saw him from a distance, and before he approached them, they schemed craftily against him to put him to death.
verses.37:19: They said to one another, "Look, that master of dreams is coming!
verses.37:20: Now then, come, let us kill him and throw him into one of the cisterns, and we will say, 'A fierce beast has devoured him.' Then we will see what becomes of his dreams."
verses.37:21: Reuben heard this and rescued him from their hand, and he said, "Let us not strike him fatally."
verses.37:22: And Reuben said to them, "Do not shed blood. Throw him into this cistern that is in the wilderness, and do not stretch out a hand against him"—in order to rescue him from their hand, to restore him to his father.
verses.37:23: So it happened, as soon as Joseph came to his brothers, that they stripped Joseph of his tunic, the long-sleeved tunic that was on him.
verses.37:24: They took him and threw him into the cistern. Now the cistern was empty; there was no water in it.
verses.37:25: Then they sat down to eat bread. And they lifted up their eyes and looked, and see, a caravan of Ishmaelites was coming from Gilead, with their camels carrying gum, balm, and ladanum, going to bring them down to Egypt.
verses.37:26: Judah said to his brothers, "What gain is there if we kill our brother and cover up his blood?
verses.37:27: Come, let us sell him to the Ishmaelites, and let not our hand be against him, for he is our brother, our own flesh." And his brothers listened.
verses.37:28: Then Midianite traders passed by; and they pulled and brought Joseph up out of the cistern, and sold Joseph to the Ishmaelites for twenty pieces of silver. And they brought Joseph to Egypt.
verses.37:29: When Reuben returned to the cistern, look, Joseph was not in the cistern! So he tore his garments.
verses.37:30: He returned to his brothers and said, "The boy is gone! And I—where can I go?"
verses.37:31: Then they took Joseph's tunic, slaughtered a male goat, and dipped the tunic in the blood.
verses.37:32: They sent the long-sleeved tunic and brought it to their father, and said, "This is what we found. Please identify it: is it your son's tunic or not?"
verses.37:33: He recognized it and said, "My son's tunic! A fierce beast has devoured him! Surely Joseph has been torn to pieces!"
verses.37:34: Then Jacob tore his clothes, put sackcloth around his waist, and mourned over his son for many days.
verses.37:35: All his sons and all his daughters rose up to comfort him, yet he refused to be comforted and said, "Indeed, I will go down to my son, mourning, to Sheol." Thus his father wept for him.
verses.37:36: Meanwhile, the Medanites sold him into Egypt to Potiphar, an official of Pharaoh, commander of the guard.
verses.38:1: Now it happened at that time that Judah went down away from his brothers and turned aside to an Adullamite man whose name was Hirah.
verses.38:2: There Judah saw the daughter of a Canaanite man whose name was Shua; he took her and went in to her.
verses.38:3: She conceived and bore a son, and he called his name Er.
verses.38:4: Then she conceived again and bore a son, and she called his name Onan.
verses.38:5: Once more she bore a son, and she called his name Shelah; and he was in Chezib when she bore him.
verses.38:6: Now Judah took a wife for Er his firstborn, and her name was Tamar.
verses.38:7: But Er, Judah's firstborn, was evil in the eyes of the LORD, so the LORD put him to death.
verses.38:8: Then Judah said to Onan, "Go in to your brother's wife, fulfill the duty of a brother-in-law to her, and raise up offspring for your brother."
verses.38:9: But Onan knew that the offspring would not belong to him; so whenever he went in to his brother's wife, he would waste it on the ground, so as not to give offspring to his brother.
verses.38:10: What he did was evil in the eyes of the LORD, so He put him to death as well.
verses.38:11: Then Judah said to Tamar his daughter-in-law, "Live as a widow in your father's house until Shelah my son grows up"—for he thought, "He might die too, like his brothers." So Tamar went and lived in her father's house.
verses.38:12: After many days had passed, Shua's daughter, Judah's wife, died. When Judah was comforted, he went up to the shearers of his flock at Timnah, he and his friend Hirah the Adullamite.
verses.38:13: It was reported to Tamar, saying, "Look, your father-in-law is going up to Timnah to shear his flock."
verses.38:14: So she removed her widow's garments, covered herself with a veil, wrapped herself up, and sat at the entrance of Enaim, which is on the road to Timnah; for she saw that Shelah had grown up, yet she had not been given to him as a wife.
verses.38:15: When Judah saw her, he thought her to be a prostitute, because she had covered her face.
verses.38:16: He turned aside to her by the road and said, "Come, please, let me come in to you"—for he did not know that she was his daughter-in-law. And she said, "What will you give me so that you may come in to me?"
verses.38:17: He said, "I myself will send a young goat from the flock." And she said, "If you will give a pledge until you send it."
verses.38:18: He said, "What is the pledge that I should give you?" And she said, "Your signet, your cord, and your staff that is in your hand." So he gave them to her and went in to her, and she conceived by him.
verses.38:19: Then she rose and went away, removed her veil, and put on her widow's garments.
verses.38:20: Judah sent the young goat by the hand of his friend the Adullamite to retrieve the pledge from the woman's hand, yet he did not find her.
verses.38:21: He asked the men of her place, saying, "Where is the shrine prostitute who was at Enaim by the road?" And they said, "There has been no shrine prostitute here."
verses.38:22: So he returned to Judah and said, "I did not find her; and what is more, the men of the place said, 'There has been no shrine prostitute here.'"
verses.38:23: Judah said, "Let her keep them for herself, or we will become an object of contempt. Look, I sent this young goat, and you did not find her."
verses.38:24: Now about three months later, it was reported to Judah, saying, "Tamar your daughter-in-law has acted as a prostitute, and look, she is also pregnant by prostitution!" And Judah said, "Bring her out and let her be burned!"
verses.38:25: As she was being brought out, she sent word to her father-in-law, saying, "By the man to whom these belong, I am pregnant." And she said, "Please identify whose signet, cords, and staff these are."
verses.38:26: Judah recognized them and said, "She is more righteous than I am, because I did not give her to Shelah my son." And he never again knew her.
verses.38:27: Now when the time came for her to give birth, look, there were twins in her womb.
