verses.38:28: And while she was giving birth, one put out a hand; and the midwife took a scarlet thread and tied it on his hand, saying, "This one came out first."
verses.38:29: Yet just as he drew back his hand, look, his brother came out! And she said, "What a breach you have broken through for yourself!" So his name was called Perez.
verses.38:30: Afterward his brother came out, on whose hand was the scarlet thread, and his name was called Zerah.
verses.39:1: Now Joseph had been brought down to Egypt, and Potiphar, an official of Pharaoh, commander of the guard, an Egyptian man, bought him from the hand of the Ishmaelites who had brought him down there.
verses.39:2: And the LORD was with Joseph, so he became a prosperous man; and he was in the house of his Egyptian master.
verses.39:3: His master saw that the LORD was with him, and that everything he did, the LORD caused to prosper in his hand.
verses.39:4: So Joseph found favor in his eyes and attended him; he appointed him over his house, and all that belonged to him he placed in his hand.
verses.39:5: From the time he appointed him in his house and over all that belonged to him, the LORD blessed the house of the Egyptian because of Joseph, and the blessing of the LORD was on all that belonged to him, in the house and in the field.
verses.39:6: So he left all that belonged to him in Joseph's hand, and with him there he took no notice of anything except the food he ate. Now Joseph was handsome in build and handsome in appearance.
verses.39:7: Now after these things, his master's wife lifted her eyes to Joseph and said, "Lie with me."
verses.39:8: But he refused and said to his master's wife, "Look, with me here, my master takes no notice of what is in the house, and all that belongs to him he has placed in my hand.
verses.39:9: He is no greater than I in this house, and he has not held back anything from me except you, since you are his wife. And how could I commit this great evil and sin against God?"
verses.39:10: And day by day, as she spoke to Joseph, he did not listen to her to lie beside her or to be with her.
verses.39:11: Now on a certain day, he came into the house to do his work, and not one of the men of the house was there in the house.
verses.39:12: Then she seized him by his garment, saying, "Lie with me!" Yet he left his garment in her hand, fled, and went outside.
verses.39:13: And when she saw that he had left his garment in her hand and fled outside,
verses.39:14: she called to the men of her house and spoke to them, saying, "See, he has brought a Hebrew man to us to mock us! He came in to me to lie with me, and I cried out in a loud voice.
verses.39:15: And when he heard that I lifted my voice and cried out, he left his garment beside me, fled, and went outside."
verses.39:16: Then she laid his garment beside her until his master came to his house.
verses.39:17: And she spoke to him with words like these, saying, "The Hebrew servant whom you brought to us came in to me to mock me.
verses.39:18: And when I lifted my voice and cried out, he left his garment beside me and fled outside."
verses.39:19: Now when his master heard his wife's words that she spoke to him, saying, "Things like these your servant did to me," his anger burned.
verses.39:20: Then Joseph's master took him and placed him in the prison, the place where the prisoners of the king were confined; and he was there in the prison.
verses.39:21: But the LORD was with Joseph and extended steadfast kindness to him, and granted him favor in the eyes of the chief of the prison.
verses.39:22: And the chief of the prison placed into Joseph's hand all the prisoners who were in the prison, and everything that was being done there, he himself was the one doing it.
verses.39:23: The chief of the prison did not look into anything at all in his hand, because the LORD was with him; and whatever he did, the LORD caused to prosper.
verses.40:1: Now after these things, the cupbearer of the king of Egypt and the baker offended their master, the king of Egypt.
verses.40:2: And Pharaoh grew furious with his two officials, with the chief cupbearer and with the chief baker.
verses.40:3: So he placed them in custody at the house of the commander of the guard, in the prison, the place where Joseph was confined.
verses.40:4: And the commander of the guard assigned Joseph to be with them, and he attended them; and they remained in custody for some days.
verses.40:5: And the two of them dreamed a dream, each man his own dream in one night, each according to the interpretation of his dream—the cupbearer and the baker of the king of Egypt, who were confined in the prison.
verses.40:6: When Joseph came to them in the morning, he saw them, and look, they were downcast.
verses.40:7: So he asked the officials of Pharaoh who were with him in custody at his master's house, saying, "Why are your faces sad today?"
verses.40:8: And they said to him, "We have dreamed a dream, and there is no interpreter for it." Then Joseph said to them, "Do interpretations not belong to God? Please recount it to me."
verses.40:9: So the chief cupbearer recounted his dream to Joseph and said to him, "In my dream, look, a vine was before me,
verses.40:10: and on the vine were three branches. As it budded, its blossoms sprang up; its clusters ripened into grapes.
verses.40:11: And Pharaoh's cup was in my hand, so I took the grapes, squeezed them into Pharaoh's cup, and set the cup on Pharaoh's palm."
verses.40:12: And Joseph said to him, "This is its interpretation: the three branches are three days.
verses.40:13: Within three days Pharaoh will lift up your head and restore you to your post; and you will place Pharaoh's cup in his hand according to the former custom, when you were his cupbearer.
verses.40:14: Only remember me when it goes well for you, and please show me kindness; make mention of me to Pharaoh, and bring me out of this house.
verses.40:15: For I was truly stolen from the land of the Hebrews, and even here I have not done anything for which they should place me in the pit."
verses.40:16: When the chief baker saw that he had interpreted well, he said to Joseph, "I also, in my dream—look, three baskets of white bread were on my head.
verses.40:17: And in the top basket were all kinds of food for Pharaoh, the work of a baker, and the birds were eating them out of the basket from off my head."
verses.40:18: Joseph answered and said, "This is its interpretation: the three baskets are three days.
verses.40:19: Within three days Pharaoh will lift up your head from off you and hang you on a tree, and the birds will eat your flesh from off you."
verses.40:20: Now it happened on the third day, Pharaoh's birthday, that he held a feast for all his servants, and he lifted up the head of the chief cupbearer and the head of the chief baker in the midst of his servants.
verses.40:21: And he restored the chief cupbearer to his post as cupbearer, and he set the cup on Pharaoh's palm.
verses.40:22: But the chief baker he hanged, just as Joseph had interpreted for them.
verses.40:23: And yet the chief cupbearer did not remember Joseph; he forgot him.
verses.41:1: It came about at the close of two full years that Pharaoh was dreaming, and look, he was standing beside the Nile.
verses.41:2: And look, coming up from the Nile were seven cows, fine in appearance and plump in flesh, and they grazed in the marsh reeds.
verses.41:3: And look, seven other cows were coming up after them from the Nile, ugly in appearance and thin in flesh, and they stood beside the cows along the bank of the Nile.
verses.41:4: Then the cows that were ugly in appearance and thin in flesh ate the seven cows that were fine in appearance and plump. And Pharaoh woke up.
verses.41:5: He fell asleep and dreamed a second time: look, seven heads of grain were coming up on a single stalk, plump and good.
verses.41:6: And look, seven heads of grain, thin and seared by the east wind, were sprouting after them.
verses.41:7: And the thin heads of grain swallowed up the seven plump and full heads of grain. Then Pharaoh woke up, and look, it was a dream.
verses.41:8: In the morning his spirit was disturbed, so he sent and summoned all the magicians of Egypt and all its wise men. Pharaoh recounted his dream to them, yet there was no one to interpret them for Pharaoh.
verses.41:9: Then the chief cupbearer spoke to Pharaoh, saying, "I mention my offenses today.
verses.41:10: Pharaoh grew angry with his servants and placed me in custody in the house of the chief of the guard, me and the chief baker.
verses.41:11: We dreamed a dream on one night, both he and I; each man dreamed according to the interpretation of his dream.
verses.41:12: Now a Hebrew youth was there with us, a servant of the chief of the guard. We told him, and he interpreted our dreams for us; to each man he interpreted according to his dream.
verses.41:13: And just as he interpreted for us, so it came about: me he restored to my post, and him he hanged."
verses.41:14: Then Pharaoh sent and summoned Joseph, and they rushed him out of the dungeon. He shaved and changed his garments, and came to Pharaoh.
verses.41:15: Pharaoh said to Joseph, "I have dreamed a dream, and there is no one to interpret it. Yet I have heard it said concerning you, 'When you hear a dream, you are able to interpret it.'"
verses.41:16: Joseph answered Pharaoh, saying, "It is not from me; God will answer for the welfare of Pharaoh."
verses.41:17: Then Pharaoh spoke to Joseph, "In my dream, there I was, standing along the bank of the Nile.
verses.41:18: And look, coming up from the Nile were seven cows, plump in flesh and fine in form, and they grazed in the marsh reeds.
verses.41:19: And look, seven other cows were coming up after them, scrawny and very ugly in form and gaunt in flesh; I have never seen any like them in all the land of Egypt for ugliness.
verses.41:20: And the gaunt and ugly cows ate the first seven plump cows.
verses.41:21: Yet when they had gone inside them, it could not be known that they had gone inside them, and their appearance was ugly as at the beginning. Then I woke up.
verses.41:22: Then I saw in my dream, and look, seven heads of grain were coming up on a single stalk, full and good.
verses.41:23: And look, seven heads of grain, shriveled, thin, seared by the east wind, were sprouting after them.
verses.41:24: And the thin heads of grain swallowed up the seven good heads of grain. Then I told the magicians, yet there was no one to declare it to me."
verses.41:25: Joseph said to Pharaoh, "The dream of Pharaoh is one; what God is about to do, He has declared to Pharaoh.
verses.41:26: The seven good cows are seven years, and the seven good heads of grain are seven years; it is one dream.
verses.41:27: And the seven gaunt and ugly cows coming up after them are seven years, and the seven empty heads of grain, seared by the east wind, will be seven years of famine.
verses.41:28: This is the matter that I spoke to Pharaoh: what God is about to do, He has shown to Pharaoh.
verses.41:29: Look, seven years are coming—great abundance in all the land of Egypt.
verses.41:30: Then seven years of famine will arise after them, and all the abundance will be forgotten in the land of Egypt, and the famine will consume the land.
verses.41:31: And the abundance will not be known in the land because of that famine afterward, for it will be exceedingly severe.
verses.41:32: And as for the dream being repeated to Pharaoh twice, it is because the matter is established by God, and God is hastening to do it.
verses.41:33: Now then, let Pharaoh look out for a man who is discerning and wise, and place him over the land of Egypt.
verses.41:34: Let Pharaoh act and appoint overseers over the land, and let him levy a fifth on the land of Egypt during the seven years of abundance.
verses.41:35: Let them gather all the food of these coming good years, and heap up grain under the hand of Pharaoh as food in the cities, and keep it.
verses.41:36: The food will be a reserve for the land for the seven years of famine that will take place in the land of Egypt, so that the land will not be cut off by the famine."
verses.41:37: And the matter was good in the eyes of Pharaoh and in the eyes of all his servants.
verses.41:38: Then Pharaoh said to his servants, "Can we find anyone like this, a man who has the Spirit of God in him?"
verses.41:39: Then Pharaoh said to Joseph, "Since God has made all this known to you, there is no one discerning and wise like you.
verses.41:40: You shall be over my house, and at your word all my people shall submit; only with respect to the throne will I be greater than you."
verses.41:41: Then Pharaoh said to Joseph, "Look, I have placed you over all the land of Egypt."
verses.41:42: Pharaoh removed his signet ring from his hand and set it on Joseph's hand; he dressed him in fine linen garments and placed the gold chain around his neck.
verses.41:43: And he had him ride in his second chariot, and they called out before him, "Bow the knee!" Thus he placed him over all the land of Egypt.
verses.41:44: And Pharaoh said to Joseph, "I am Pharaoh, yet without you no one shall lift his hand or his foot in all the land of Egypt."
verses.41:45: Pharaoh called Joseph's name Zaphenath-paneah, and he gave him Asenath, daughter of Potiphera priest of On, as his wife. So Joseph went out over the land of Egypt.
verses.41:46: Joseph was thirty years old when he stood before Pharaoh, king of Egypt. Then Joseph went out from before Pharaoh and passed through all the land of Egypt.
verses.41:47: During the seven years of abundance, the land produced bountifully.
verses.41:48: He gathered all the food of the seven years that occurred in the land of Egypt and placed food in the cities; the food from the surrounding field of each city he placed inside it.
verses.41:49: So Joseph heaped up grain like the sand of the sea, in very great quantity, until he stopped counting, for it was beyond number.
verses.41:50: Now two sons were born to Joseph before the year of famine arrived, whom Asenath, daughter of Potiphera priest of On, bore for him.
verses.41:51: Joseph named the firstborn Manasseh, "For God has caused me to forget all my toil and all my father's house."
verses.41:52: And he named the second Ephraim, "For God has caused me to be fruitful in the land of my suffering."
verses.41:53: Then the seven years of abundance that had been in the land of Egypt came to a close.
verses.41:54: And the seven years of famine began to arrive, just as Joseph had said. There was famine in all the lands, yet throughout all the land of Egypt there was bread.
verses.41:55: When the entire land of Egypt grew famished, the people cried out to Pharaoh for bread; and Pharaoh said to all Egypt, "Go to Joseph; do whatever he tells you."
verses.41:56: Now the famine was over all the face of the earth; so Joseph opened all that held reserves and sold grain to Egypt, and the famine grew severe in the land of Egypt.
verses.41:57: And all the earth came into Egypt to Joseph to buy grain, for the famine had grown severe throughout all the earth.
verses.42:1: And Jacob saw that there was grain in Egypt, and Jacob said to his sons, "Why are you looking at one another?"
verses.42:2: He said, "Look, I have heard that there is grain in Egypt. Go down there and buy grain for us from there, so that we may live and not die."
verses.42:3: And ten of Joseph's brothers went down to buy grain from Egypt.
verses.42:4: But Jacob did not send Benjamin, Joseph's brother, along with his brothers, for he said, "Harm might happen to him."
verses.42:5: And the sons of Israel came to buy grain in the midst of those who came, because the famine was in the land of Canaan.
verses.42:6: Now Joseph was the ruler over the land; it was he who sold grain to all the people of the land. And Joseph's brothers came and bowed low to him, faces to the ground.
verses.42:7: Joseph saw his brothers and recognized them, yet he acted as a stranger toward them and spoke harshly with them. He said to them, "Where have you come from?" They said, "From the land of Canaan, to buy food."
verses.42:8: Thus Joseph recognized his brothers, yet they did not recognize him.
verses.42:9: Joseph remembered the dreams that he had dreamed concerning them, and he said to them, "You are spies! To see the nakedness of the land you have come."
verses.42:10: They said to him, "No, my lord; rather, your servants have come to buy food.
verses.42:11: All of us are sons of one man; we are honest men, and your servants have not been spies."
verses.42:12: But he said to them, "No! Rather, you have come to see the nakedness of the land."
verses.42:13: And they said, "Your servants are twelve brothers, the sons of one man in the land of Canaan. Look, the youngest is with our father today, and one is no more."
verses.42:14: Joseph said to them, "This is what I spoke to you, saying, 'You are spies!'
verses.42:15: By this you will be tested: by the life of Pharaoh, you will certainly not go out from here unless your youngest brother comes here.
verses.42:16: Send one from among you and let him fetch your brother, while you remain bound, so that your words may be tested, whether truth is with you. And if not, by the life of Pharaoh, you are certainly spies."
verses.42:17: Then he gathered them into custody for three days.
verses.42:18: And Joseph said to them on the third day, "Do this and live; I fear God.
verses.42:19: If you are honest men, let one of your brothers remain bound in your house of custody, while you go and bring grain for the famine of your households.
verses.42:20: And bring your youngest brother to me, that your words may be proven true and you will not die." And they did so.
verses.42:21: And they said, each to his brother, "Indeed, we are guilty regarding our brother, in that we saw the distress of his soul when he pleaded with us for mercy, and we did not listen. For this reason this distress has come upon us."
verses.42:22: And Reuben answered them, saying, "Did I not say to you, 'Do not sin against the boy'? Yet you did not listen. And look, his blood also is being required."
verses.42:23: Now they did not know that Joseph understood, because the interpreter was between them.
verses.42:24: He turned aside from them and wept. Then he came back to them and spoke to them; and he took Simeon from them and bound him before their eyes.
verses.42:25: And Joseph gave orders to fill their containers with grain, to return each man's silver to his sack, and to give them provisions for the journey. And he did so for them.
verses.42:26: Then they loaded their grain onto their donkeys and went from there.
verses.42:27: When one of them opened his sack to give fodder to his donkey at the lodging place, he saw his silver; and look, it was in the mouth of his bag.
verses.42:28: So he said to his brothers, "My silver has been returned, and indeed, here it is in my bag!" Then their hearts failed them, and trembling they turned to one another, saying, "What is this God has done to us?"
verses.42:29: And they came to Jacob their father, to the land of Canaan, and reported to him all the things that had happened to them, saying,
verses.42:30: "The man, the lord of the land, spoke harshly with us and treated us as those spying out the land.
verses.42:31: And we said to him, 'We are honest men; we have not been spies.
verses.42:32: We are twelve brothers, the sons of our father; one is no more, and the youngest is with our father today in the land of Canaan.'
verses.42:33: Then the man, the lord of the land, said to us, 'By this I will know that you are honest men: leave one of your brothers with me, take grain for the famine of your households, and go.
verses.42:34: And bring your youngest brother to me, so that I may know that you are not spies, but rather that you are honest men. Then I will give your brother to you, and you may trade in the land.'"
verses.42:35: Now it happened, as they were emptying their sacks, that look, each man's bundle of silver was in his sack! And they and their father saw their bundles of silver, and they were afraid.
verses.42:36: Then Jacob their father said to them, "You have left me bereaved! Joseph is no more, and Simeon is no more, and Benjamin you would take. All of these things have come upon me."
verses.42:37: Then Reuben said to his father, "You may put my two sons to death if I do not bring him to you. Place him in my hand, and I myself will return him to you."
verses.42:38: But he said, "My son will not go down with you, because his brother is dead, and he alone remains. If harm befalls him along the way you are going, then you will bring down my gray hair in sorrow to Sheol."
verses.43:1: And the famine was heavy in the land.
verses.43:2: And it happened, when they had finished eating the grain they had brought from Egypt, that their father said to them, "Return, buy a little food for us."
verses.43:3: Then Judah said to him, "The man strictly warned us, saying, 'You will not see my face unless your brother is with you.'
verses.43:4: If you are going to send our brother with us, we will go down and buy food for you.
verses.43:5: But if you are not going to send him, we will not go down; because the man said to us, 'You will not see my face unless your brother is with you.'"
verses.43:6: Then Israel said, "Why did you deal badly with me by telling the man whether you still had a brother?"
verses.43:7: And they said, "The man inquired closely about us and our relatives, saying, 'Is your father still alive? Do you have a brother?' So we told him in accordance with these words. Could we possibly have known that he would say, 'Bring down your brother'?"
verses.43:8: Then Judah said to his father Israel, "Send the boy with me, and we will rise and go, so that we may live and not die, both we and you and our little ones too.
verses.43:9: I myself will be surety for him; from my hand you may require him. If I do not bring him to you and place him before you, then let me bear the guilt before you for all time.
verses.43:10: For had we not lingered, surely by now we would have returned two times."
verses.43:11: Then Israel their father said to them, "If so, then do this: take some of the prized produce of the land in your containers, and bring down a gift to the man, a little balm and a little honey, gum and myrrh, pistachio nuts and almonds.
verses.43:12: Take twice the silver in your hand, and return in your hand the silver that was returned in the mouth of your bags; perhaps it was an oversight.
verses.43:13: Take your brother too; rise and return to the man.
verses.43:14: And may God Almighty give you compassion before the man, so that he will release to you your other brother and Benjamin. As for me, if I am bereaved, I am bereaved."
verses.43:15: So the men took this gift, and they took twice the silver in their hand, along with Benjamin; and they rose up, went down to Egypt, and stood before Joseph.
verses.43:16: When Joseph saw Benjamin with them, he said to the one who was over his house, "Bring the men into the house; slaughter an animal and make preparations, because the men will eat with me at noon."
verses.43:17: So the man did as Joseph had said, and the man brought the men into Joseph's house.
verses.43:18: And the men were afraid because they had been brought into Joseph's house, and they said, "Because of the silver that returned in our bags the first time, we are being brought in, so that he may rush upon us and fall upon us, and take us as slaves, along with our donkeys."
verses.43:19: So they approached the man who was over Joseph's house and spoke to him at the entrance of the house.
verses.43:20: They said, "Please, my lord, we indeed came down the first time to buy food.
verses.43:21: And it happened, when we came to the lodging place and opened our bags, look, each man's silver was in the mouth of his bag, our silver in its full weight; so we have returned it in our hand.
verses.43:22: And we have brought down other silver in our hand to buy food; we do not know who placed our silver in our bags."
verses.43:23: And he said, "Peace be to you; do not be afraid. Your God and the God of your father has given you hidden treasure in your bags; your silver came to me." Then he brought Simeon out to them.
verses.43:24: So the man brought the men into Joseph's house; he gave water and they washed their feet, and he gave fodder to their donkeys.
verses.43:25: And they prepared the gift for the coming of Joseph at noon, because they had heard that they would eat bread there.
verses.43:26: When Joseph came into the house, they brought the gift that was in their hand into the house to him, and they bowed down to him to the ground.
verses.43:27: Then he inquired about their well-being and said, "Is it well with your aged father of whom you spoke? Is he still alive?"
verses.43:28: And they said, "It is well with your servant, our father; he is still alive." Then they bowed low and prostrated themselves.
verses.43:29: He lifted his eyes and saw Benjamin his brother, the son of his mother, and said, "Is this your youngest brother, the one you spoke to me about?" And he said, "God be gracious to you, my son."
verses.43:30: And Joseph hurried off, because his compassion was deeply stirred toward his brother, and he sought a place to weep; so he went into the inner chamber and wept there.
verses.43:31: Then he washed his face and came out; restraining himself, he said, "Set out the food."
verses.43:32: And they set food for him by himself, for them by themselves, and for the Egyptians who were eating with him by themselves, because the Egyptians could not eat bread with the Hebrews, since that is an abomination to the Egyptians.
verses.43:33: So they sat down before him, the firstborn according to his birthright and the youngest according to his youth; and the men marveled, looking at one another.
verses.43:34: He had portions carried to them from before him, and Benjamin's portion was five times greater than the portions of all of them. And they drank and drank freely with him.
verses.44:1: Then he commanded the one who was over his house, saying, "Fill the men's sacks with food, as much as they are able to carry, and place each man's silver in the mouth of his sack.
verses.44:2: And my cup, the silver cup, you shall place in the mouth of the youngest one's sack, together with the silver for his grain." And he did according to the word of Joseph that he had spoken.
verses.44:3: The morning grew light, and the men were sent off, they and their donkeys.
verses.44:4: They had gone out of the city and had not gone far when Joseph said to the one who was over his house, "Get up, pursue after the men, and when you overtake them, say to them, 'Why have you repaid evil in return for good?
verses.44:5: Is this not the one from which my lord drinks, and with which he indeed practices divination? You have done evil in what you have done.'"
verses.44:6: So he overtook them and spoke these words to them.
verses.44:7: And they said to him, "Why does my lord speak words like these? Far be it from your servants to do a thing like this!
verses.44:8: Look, the silver that we found in the mouths of our sacks we brought back to you from the land of Canaan. How then could we steal silver or gold from your lord's house?
verses.44:9: Whichever of your servants it is found with shall die, and we too will become slaves to my lord."
verses.44:10: And he said, "Even now, according to your words, so be it: the one with whom it is found shall become my slave, and you shall be innocent."
verses.44:11: Then they hurried, and each man lowered his sack to the ground, and each man opened his sack.
verses.44:12: And he searched; he began with the oldest and finished with the youngest, and the cup was found in Benjamin's sack.
verses.44:13: Then they tore their garments, and each man loaded his donkey, and they returned to the city.
verses.44:14: So Judah and his brothers came to Joseph's house while he was still there, and they fell before him to the ground.
verses.44:15: And Joseph said to them, "What is this deed that you have done? Did you not know that a man like me can indeed practice divination?"
verses.44:16: Then Judah said, "What shall we say to my lord? What shall we speak, and how can we justify ourselves? God has found the iniquity of your servants. Here we are, slaves to my lord, both we and the one in whose hand the cup was found."
verses.44:17: But he said, "Far be it from me to do this! The man in whose hand the cup was found, he shall become my slave; as for you, go up in peace to your father."
verses.44:18: Then Judah drew near to him and said, "Please, my lord, let your servant speak a word in the ears of my lord, and do not let your anger burn against your servant, for you are just like Pharaoh.
verses.44:19: My lord asked his servants, saying, 'Do you have a father or a brother?'
verses.44:20: And we said to my lord, 'We have an aged father and a young child of his old age; his brother is dead, so he alone is left of his mother, and his father loves him.'
verses.44:21: Then you said to your servants, 'Bring him down to me so that I may set my eye on him.'
verses.44:22: And we said to my lord, 'The boy cannot leave his father, for if he leaves his father, he will die.'
verses.44:23: But you said to your servants, 'If your youngest brother does not come down with you, you will not see my face again.'
verses.44:24: So it happened, when we went up to your servant my father, that we told him the words of my lord.
verses.44:25: And our father said, 'Go back, buy a little food for us.'
verses.44:26: But we said, 'We cannot go down. If our youngest brother is with us, then we will go down; for we cannot see the man's face while our youngest brother is not with us.'
verses.44:27: Then your servant my father said to us, 'You yourselves know that my wife bore two sons to me;
verses.44:28: and the one went out from me, and I said, "Surely he has been torn to pieces!" and I have not seen him until now.
verses.44:29: If you take this one also from my presence and harm befalls him, then you will bring my gray hair down in misery to Sheol.'
verses.44:30: So now, when I come to your servant my father and the boy is not with us, since his soul is bound to the boy's soul,
verses.44:31: it will happen, when he sees that the boy is not there, that he will die; and your servants will bring the gray hair of your servant our father down in grief to Sheol.
verses.44:32: For your servant pledged himself for the boy to my father, saying, 'If I do not bring him to you, then I shall be guilty before my father for all time.'
verses.44:33: Now therefore, please let your servant remain in place of the boy as a slave to my lord, and let the boy go up with his brothers.
verses.44:34: For how can I go up to my father while the boy is not with me? Let me not look upon the calamity that would find my father!"
verses.45:1: Then Joseph could not restrain himself before all those standing beside him, and he called out, "Send every man out from beside me!" So no man stood with him when Joseph made himself known to his brothers.
verses.45:2: And he let out his voice in weeping, and the Egyptians heard it, and the house of Pharaoh heard it.
verses.45:3: Then Joseph said to his brothers, "I am Joseph! Is my father still alive?" But his brothers were unable to answer him, for they were terrified in his presence.
verses.45:4: Then Joseph said to his brothers, "Please draw near to me." And they drew near. And he said, "I am Joseph your brother, whom you sold into Egypt.
verses.45:5: And now, do not be grieved and do not be angry with yourselves that you sold me to this place, for God sent me ahead of you for the preservation of life.
verses.45:6: For these two years the famine has been in the midst of the land, and there are still five years in which there will be neither plowing nor harvest.
verses.45:7: So God sent me ahead of you to establish for you a remnant on the earth and to keep you alive for a great deliverance.
verses.45:8: So now, it was not you who sent me here, but God; and He has appointed me as a father to Pharaoh, and as lord over all his house, and as ruler over all the land of Egypt.
verses.45:9: Hurry and go up to my father, and say to him, 'This is what your son Joseph says: God has appointed me lord over all Egypt; come down to me, do not delay.
verses.45:10: And you shall live in the land of Goshen, and you shall be near to me, you and your sons and your sons' sons, and your flocks and your herds and all that belongs to you.
verses.45:11: And I will sustain you there, for there are still five years of famine, so that you do not come to poverty, you and your household and all that belongs to you.'
verses.45:12: And look, your eyes see, and the eyes of my brother Benjamin, that it is my own mouth that is speaking to you.
verses.45:13: And you shall tell my father of all my glory in Egypt and of all that you have seen, and you must hurry and bring my father down here."
verses.45:14: Then he fell upon the neck of Benjamin his brother and wept, and Benjamin wept on his neck.
verses.45:15: And he kissed all his brothers and wept over them, and after that his brothers spoke with him.
verses.45:16: Now the report was heard in the house of Pharaoh, saying, "Joseph's brothers have come." And it was good in the eyes of Pharaoh and in the eyes of his servants.
verses.45:17: Then Pharaoh said to Joseph, "Say to your brothers, 'Do this: load your beasts and go, enter the land of Canaan,
verses.45:18: and take your father and your households and come to me, and I will give you the best of the land of Egypt, and you will eat the fat of the land.'
verses.45:19: Now as for you, you are commanded: 'Do this: take wagons for yourselves from the land of Egypt for your little ones and for your wives, and carry your father and come.
verses.45:20: And let your eye have no regret for your belongings, for the best of all the land of Egypt is yours.'"
verses.45:21: And the sons of Israel did so; and Joseph gave them wagons according to Pharaoh's command, and he gave them provisions for the journey.
verses.45:22: To all of them, to each man, he gave changes of garments, but to Benjamin he gave three hundred pieces of silver and five changes of garments.
verses.45:23: And to his father he sent as follows: ten male donkeys carrying some of the best things of Egypt, and ten female donkeys carrying grain and bread and food for his father on the journey.
verses.45:24: So he sent his brothers off, and they departed; and he said to them, "Do not become agitated on the way."
verses.45:25: Then they went up from Egypt and came to the land of Canaan, to Jacob their father.
verses.45:26: And they told him, saying, "Joseph is still alive, and indeed he is ruler over all the land of Egypt!" And his heart grew faint, for he did not believe them.
verses.45:27: But when they spoke to him all the words of Joseph that he had spoken to them, and he saw the wagons that Joseph had sent to carry him, the spirit of Jacob their father revived.
verses.45:28: Then Israel said, "It is enough! Joseph my son is still alive. Let me go and see him before I die."
verses.46:1: Then Israel set out with all that belonged to him, and he came to Beersheba and offered sacrifices to the God of his father Isaac.
verses.46:2: God spoke to Israel in night visions, saying, "Jacob, Jacob." He replied, "Here I am."
verses.46:3: He said, "I am God, the God of your father. Do not fear going down to Egypt, because there I will make you into a great nation.
verses.46:4: I Myself will go down with you to Egypt, and I Myself will also surely bring you up, and Joseph will place his hand on your eyes."
verses.46:5: Jacob then rose from Beersheba, and Israel's sons carried their father Jacob, their little ones, and their wives in the wagons Pharaoh had sent to carry him.
verses.46:6: They took their livestock and the possessions they had acquired in the land of Canaan, and they came to Egypt, Jacob and all his offspring with him.
verses.46:7: His sons and his sons' sons with him, his daughters and his sons' daughters, and all his offspring he brought with him into Egypt.
verses.46:8: These are the names of the sons of Israel who came to Egypt, Jacob and his sons: Jacob's firstborn, Reuben.
verses.46:9: The sons of Reuben were Hanoch, Pallu, Hezron, and Carmi.
verses.46:10: The sons of Simeon were Jemuel, Jamin, Ohad, Jachin, Zohar, and Shaul, the son of the Canaanite woman.
verses.46:11: The sons of Levi were Gershon, Kohath, and Merari.
verses.46:12: The sons of Judah were Er, Onan, Shelah, Perez, and Zerah—though Er and Onan died in the land of Canaan—and the sons of Perez were Hezron and Hamul.
verses.46:13: The sons of Issachar were Tola, Puvah, Job, and Shimron.
verses.46:14: The sons of Zebulun were Sered, Elon, and Jahleel.
verses.46:15: These are the sons of Leah, whom she bore to Jacob in Paddan-aram, together with his daughter Dinah; all the persons of his sons and his daughters were thirty-three.
verses.46:16: The sons of Gad were Ziphion, Haggi, Shuni, Ezbon, Eri, Arodi, and Areli.
verses.46:17: The sons of Asher were Imnah, Ishvah, Ishvi, Beriah, and their sister Serah; and the sons of Beriah were Heber and Malchiel.
verses.46:18: These are the sons of Zilpah, whom Laban had given to his daughter Leah; she bore these to Jacob—sixteen persons.
verses.46:19: The sons of Rachel, Jacob's wife, were Joseph and Benjamin.
verses.46:20: Manasseh and Ephraim were born to Joseph in the land of Egypt, whom Asenath the daughter of Potiphera, priest of On, bore to him.
verses.46:21: The sons of Benjamin were Bela, Becher, Ashbel, Gera, Naaman, Ehi, Rosh, Muppim, Huppim, and Ard.
verses.46:22: These are the sons of Rachel who were born to Jacob—fourteen persons in all.
verses.46:23: And the sons of Dan: Hushim.
verses.46:24: The sons of Naphtali were Jahzeel, Guni, Jezer, and Shillem.
verses.46:25: These are the sons of Bilhah, whom Laban had given to his daughter Rachel; she bore these to Jacob—seven persons in all.
verses.46:26: All the persons belonging to Jacob who came to Egypt—those coming from his loins, apart from the wives of Jacob's sons—were sixty-six persons in all.
verses.46:27: And Joseph's sons who were born to him in Egypt were two persons; all the persons of Jacob's household who came to Egypt were seventy.
verses.46:28: Now he sent Judah ahead of him to Joseph to direct the way before him to Goshen, and they came to the land of Goshen.
verses.46:29: So Joseph harnessed his chariot and went up to Goshen to meet his father Israel; he appeared to him, fell on his neck, and wept on his neck for a long while.
verses.46:30: Israel said to Joseph, "Now I can die, after seeing your face, for you are still alive."
verses.46:31: Joseph said to his brothers and to his father's household, "I will go up and report to Pharaoh, and say to him, 'My brothers and my father's household, who were in the land of Canaan, have come to me.
verses.46:32: And the men are shepherds, for they have been livestock keepers, and they have brought their flocks, their herds, and everything that belongs to them.'
verses.46:33: So it will be that when Pharaoh summons you and says, 'What is your work?'
verses.46:34: you must say, 'Your servants have been livestock keepers from our youth until now, both we and our fathers,' so that you may settle in the land of Goshen, because every shepherd is an abomination to the Egyptians."
verses.47:1: Then Joseph came and reported to Pharaoh, saying, "My father and my brothers, with their flocks, their herds, and everything that belongs to them, have come from the land of Canaan, and here they are in the land of Goshen."
verses.47:2: And he took five men from among his brothers and set them before Pharaoh.
verses.47:3: Pharaoh said to his brothers, "What is your work?" They replied to Pharaoh, "Your servants are shepherds, both we and our fathers."
verses.47:4: And they said to Pharaoh, "We have come to sojourn in the land, because there is no pasture for the flocks belonging to your servants, since the famine is severe in the land of Canaan. Now please let your servants settle in the land of Goshen."
verses.47:5: Then Pharaoh spoke to Joseph, saying, "Your father and your brothers have come to you.
verses.47:6: The land of Egypt lies before you. Settle your father and your brothers in the best part of the land; let them settle in the land of Goshen. And if you know that there are capable men among them, appoint them as overseers of livestock over what belongs to me."
verses.47:7: Joseph then brought in his father Jacob and had him stand before Pharaoh, and Jacob blessed Pharaoh.
verses.47:8: Pharaoh asked Jacob, "How many are the days of the years of your life?"
verses.47:9: Jacob answered Pharaoh, "The days of the years of my sojourning are one hundred thirty years. Few and difficult have been the days of the years of my life, and they have not reached the days of the years of my fathers' lives during the days of their sojourning."
verses.47:10: Then Jacob blessed Pharaoh and went out from before Pharaoh.
verses.47:11: Joseph settled his father and his brothers and gave them property in the land of Egypt, in the best part of the land, in the land of Rameses, just as Pharaoh had commanded.
verses.47:12: Joseph also sustained his father, his brothers, and his father's entire household with bread in proportion to their little ones.
verses.47:13: Now there was no bread in all the land, because the famine was very severe, and the land of Egypt and the land of Canaan grew faint on account of the famine.
verses.47:14: Joseph collected all the silver found in the land of Egypt and in the land of Canaan for the grain they were buying, and Joseph brought the silver into Pharaoh's house.
verses.47:15: When the silver was exhausted from the land of Egypt and from the land of Canaan, all the Egyptians came to Joseph and said, "Give us bread! Why should we die in front of you? For silver has run out."
verses.47:16: Then Joseph said, "Give over your livestock, and I will give to you in exchange for your livestock, if silver has run out."
verses.47:17: So they brought their livestock to Joseph, and Joseph gave them bread in exchange for the horses, the flocks, the cattle, and the donkeys; he provided them with bread in exchange for all their livestock during that year.
verses.47:18: When that year came to an end, they came to him in the second year and said to him, "We will not conceal from my lord that the silver is spent and the herds of livestock belong to my lord; nothing remains before my lord except our bodies and our land.
verses.47:19: Why should we die before your eyes, both we and our land? Buy us and our land in exchange for bread, and we along with our land will become servants to Pharaoh. And give seed so that we may live and not die, and the land will not become desolate."
verses.47:20: Then Joseph bought all the land of Egypt for Pharaoh, because the Egyptians sold each one his field, since the famine prevailed over them; and the land became Pharaoh's.
verses.47:21: As for the people, he relocated them to the cities, from one end of the border of Egypt to the other.
verses.47:22: Only the priests' land he did not buy, because the priests had a set allowance from Pharaoh, and they ate their allowance that Pharaoh gave them; for that reason they did not sell their land.
verses.47:23: Joseph then said to the people, "Look, I have bought you and your land for Pharaoh today. Here is seed for you, and you shall sow the land.
verses.47:24: And it shall be at the harvests that you must give a fifth to Pharaoh, while the four parts will be yours—for seed of the field, for your food and for those in your households, and for your little ones to eat."
verses.47:25: They replied, "You have kept us alive! May we find favor in the eyes of my lord, and we will be servants to Pharaoh."
verses.47:26: So Joseph established it as a statute over the land of Egypt to this day, that the fifth belongs to Pharaoh; only the land of the priests alone did not become Pharaoh's.
verses.47:27: Now Israel settled in the land of Egypt, in the land of Goshen; they acquired property in it, and they became fruitful and increased greatly.
verses.47:28: And Jacob lived seventeen years in the land of Egypt, so the days of Jacob, the years of his life, were one hundred forty-seven years.
verses.47:29: When the days drew near for Israel to die, he summoned his son Joseph and said to him, "If now I have found favor in your eyes, please place your hand under my thigh and deal with me in loyal love and faithfulness: please do not bury me in Egypt.
verses.47:30: But when I lie down with my fathers, carry me out of Egypt and bury me in their burial site." He answered, "I myself will do according to your word."
verses.47:31: And he said, "Swear to me," so he swore to him. Then Israel bowed down at the head of the bed.
verses.48:1: Now it happened after these things that someone said to Joseph, "Look, your father is sick." So he took his two sons with him, Manasseh and Ephraim.
verses.48:2: Then someone informed Jacob and said, "Look, your son Joseph is coming to you." So Israel strengthened himself and sat up on the bed.
verses.48:3: Jacob said to Joseph, "God Almighty appeared to me at Luz in the land of Canaan and blessed me.
verses.48:4: And He said to me, 'See, I am going to make you fruitful and multiply you, and I will make you into an assembly of peoples, and I will give this land to your offspring after you as a perpetual possession.'
verses.48:5: So now, your two sons born to you in the land of Egypt before my coming to you into Egypt belong to me; Ephraim and Manasseh shall be mine, like Reuben and Simeon.
verses.48:6: But the children whom you father after them shall belong to you; they shall be called under the name of their brothers in their inheritance.
verses.48:7: As for me, when I was coming from Paddan, Rachel died, to my grief, in the land of Canaan along the road, while there was still a stretch of land before reaching Ephrath, and I buried her there on the road to Ephrath, that is, Bethlehem."
verses.48:8: Then Israel saw the sons of Joseph, and he said, "Who are these?"
verses.48:9: Joseph replied to his father, "They are my sons, whom God has given me in this place." So he said, "Bring them over to me, please, so that I may bless them."
verses.48:10: Now the eyes of Israel had grown heavy from old age; he was unable to see. So he brought them near to him, and he kissed them and embraced them.
verses.48:11: Then Israel said to Joseph, "I did not suppose I would see your face, yet look, God has let me see your offspring too."
verses.48:12: Then Joseph brought them out from beside his knees and bowed low with his face to the ground.
verses.48:13: Joseph took both of them, Ephraim in his right hand on Israel's left, and Manasseh in his left hand on Israel's right, and brought them near to him.
verses.48:14: Israel stretched out his right hand and set it on the head of Ephraim, though he was the younger, and his left hand on the head of Manasseh, crossing his hands, for Manasseh was the firstborn.
verses.48:15: Then he blessed Joseph and said, "The God in whose presence my fathers Abraham and Isaac walked, the God who has shepherded me throughout my life until this day,
verses.48:16: the Angel who has redeemed me from all harm—may He bless the boys, and may my name be called in them, and the name of my fathers Abraham and Isaac, and may they teem into a multitude in the midst of the earth."
verses.48:17: When Joseph saw that his father was setting his right hand on Ephraim's head, it was displeasing in his sight; so he took hold of his father's hand to move it from Ephraim's head onto Manasseh's head.
verses.48:18: Then Joseph said to his father, "Not like this, my father, because this one is the firstborn; lay your right hand on his head."
verses.48:19: Yet his father refused and said, "I know, my son, I know; he too will become a people, and he too will grow great. Nevertheless, his younger brother will grow greater than he, and his offspring will become a fullness of nations."
verses.48:20: So he blessed them on that day, saying, "By you Israel will pronounce blessing, saying, 'May God make you like Ephraim and like Manasseh.'" Thus he set Ephraim ahead of Manasseh.
verses.48:21: Then Israel said to Joseph, "Look, I am about to die, yet God will be with you and bring you back to the land of your fathers.
verses.48:22: And as for me, I have given you one ridge above your brothers, which I took from the hand of the Amorites with my sword and with my bow."
verses.49:1: Then Jacob called for his sons and said, "Assemble yourselves, so that I may declare to you what will happen to you in the latter days.
verses.49:2: Gather together and listen, sons of Jacob, and listen to Israel your father.
verses.49:3: Reuben, you are my firstborn, my strength and the beginning of my vigor, excelling in dignity and excelling in might.
verses.49:4: Turbulent as water, you shall not excel, because you went up onto your father's bed; then you defiled it—he went up onto my couch!
verses.49:5: Simeon and Levi are brothers; instruments of violence are their blades.
verses.49:6: Into their council let my soul not enter; with their assembly let my honor not be joined, for in their anger they killed men, and at their whim they hamstrung oxen.
verses.49:7: Cursed is their anger, for it is ferocious, and their fury, for it is harsh; I will divide them among Jacob and scatter them throughout Israel.
verses.49:8: Judah, you are the one your brothers will praise; your hand will be on the nape of your enemies' necks; the sons of your father will bow down to you.
verses.49:9: A lion's cub is Judah; from the prey, my son, you have come up. He crouched, he lay down like a lion, and like a lioness—who will rouse him?
verses.49:10: A scepter will not depart from Judah, nor a commander's staff from between his feet, until Shiloh comes, and to him will belong the obedience of peoples.
verses.49:11: He tethers his young donkey to the vine, and the colt of his donkey to the choice vine; he washes his garment in wine, and his cloak in the blood of grapes.
verses.49:12: Darker are his eyes than wine, and whiter are his teeth than milk.
verses.49:13: Zebulun will settle by the shore of the seas; he himself will serve as a haven for ships, and his border will be toward Sidon.
verses.49:14: Issachar is a strong-boned donkey, lying between the sheepfolds.
verses.49:15: He saw that rest was good and that the land was delightful; so he bent his shoulder to bear burdens and became subject to forced labor.
verses.49:16: Dan will judge his people, as one of Israel's tribes.
verses.49:17: May Dan be a serpent along the road, a horned viper beside the path, biting the heels of a horse so that its rider falls backward.
verses.49:18: For Your deliverance I wait, LORD.
verses.49:19: Gad—a raiding band will raid him, yet he himself will raid at their heel.
verses.49:20: From Asher, his food will be rich, and he himself will furnish the delicacies of a king.
verses.49:21: Naphtali is a doe set free, one who gives words of beauty.
verses.49:22: A fruitful branch is Joseph, a fruitful branch beside a spring; its offshoots climb over a wall.
verses.49:23: Archers dealt bitterly with him, shot at him, and harried him;
verses.49:24: yet his bow remained steadfast, and the arms of his hands stayed nimble by the hands of the Mighty One of Jacob—from there comes the Shepherd, the Stone of Israel—
verses.49:25: by the God of your father, may He help you, and by the Almighty, may He bless you with blessings of the heavens above, blessings of the deep lying below, blessings of breasts and womb.
verses.49:26: The blessings of your father have surpassed the blessings of my progenitors, as far as the farthest limit of the eternal hills; may they be on Joseph's head, and on the crown of the head of the one set apart among his brothers.
verses.49:27: Benjamin is a wolf that tears; in the morning he devours prey, and at evening he apportions plunder."
verses.49:28: All these are the twelve tribes of Israel, and this is what their father spoke to them when he blessed them; he blessed them, each one according to his own blessing.
verses.49:29: Then he commanded them and said to them, "I am about to be gathered to my people; bury me with my fathers in the cave that is in the field of Ephron the Hittite,
verses.49:30: in the cave that is in the field of Machpelah, facing Mamre in the land of Canaan, which Abraham bought together with the field from Ephron the Hittite as a burial possession.
verses.49:31: There they buried Abraham and Sarah, his wife; there they buried Isaac and Rebekah, his wife; and there I buried Leah.
verses.49:32: The purchase of the field and the cave that is in it was from the sons of Heth."
verses.49:33: After Jacob finished commanding his sons, he gathered his feet onto the bed, breathed his last, and was gathered to his people.
verses.50:1: Joseph fell onto his father's face; he wept over him and kissed him.
verses.50:2: Then Joseph ordered his servants, the physicians, to embalm his father, and the physicians embalmed Israel.
verses.50:3: Forty days were completed for him, for thus the days of embalming are completed, and Egypt wept for him seventy days.
verses.50:4: The days of weeping for him passed, and Joseph spoke to Pharaoh's household, saying, "Please, if I have found favor in your eyes, do speak in Pharaoh's ears, saying,
verses.50:5: 'My father made me swear, saying, "Look, I am dying. In my grave that I dug for myself in the land of Canaan, there you are to bury me." And now, let me go up, please, and bury my father, and I will return.'"
verses.50:6: Pharaoh replied, "Go up and bury your father, just as he made you swear."
verses.50:7: Joseph went up to bury his father, and all of Pharaoh's servants went up with him, the elders of his household, and all the elders of the land of Egypt,
verses.50:8: and all of Joseph's household, his brothers, and his father's household. Only their little ones, their flocks, and their herds did they leave in the land of Goshen.
verses.50:9: Both chariots and horsemen went up with him, and the company was very massive.
verses.50:10: They came as far as the threshing floor of Atad, which is beyond the Jordan, and there they lamented with a great and very heavy lamentation; and he observed mourning for his father for seven days.
verses.50:11: When the Canaanite inhabitants of the land saw the mourning at the threshing floor of Atad, they said, "This is a heavy mourning for Egypt." Therefore its name was called Abel-mizraim, which is beyond the Jordan.
verses.50:12: And his sons did for him in this way, just as he had ordered them.
verses.50:13: His sons carried him to the land of Canaan and buried him in the cave of the field of Machpelah, the field that Abraham had purchased as a burial possession from Ephron the Hittite, facing Mamre.
verses.50:14: Then Joseph returned to Egypt, he and his brothers and all who had gone up with him to bury his father, after he buried his father.
verses.50:15: Now Joseph's brothers saw that their father had died, and they said, "What if Joseph harbors a grudge against us and surely repays us for all the evil that we dealt to him?"
verses.50:16: So they sent word to Joseph, saying, "Your father gave orders before his death, saying,
verses.50:17: 'This is what you are to say to Joseph, "Please, do pardon the transgression of your brothers and their sin, for they dealt evil to you."' Now then, please pardon the transgression of the servants of your father's God." Joseph wept as they spoke to him.
verses.50:18: Then his brothers also went and fell before him, and they said, "Here we are as servants to you."
verses.50:19: Joseph replied to them, "Do not fear, for am I in God's place?
verses.50:20: You yourselves planned evil against me, yet God planned it for good, in order to act as on this day, to keep a numerous people alive.
verses.50:21: So now, do not fear; I myself will sustain you and your little ones." And he comforted them and spoke to their hearts.
verses.50:22: Joseph resided in Egypt, he and his father's household, and Joseph lived a hundred and ten years.
verses.50:23: Joseph saw Ephraim's sons of the third generation, and the sons of Machir, the son of Manasseh, were born upon Joseph's knees as well.
verses.50:24: Then Joseph said to his brothers, "I am dying, but God will surely attend to you and bring you up from this land to the land that He swore to Abraham, to Isaac, and to Jacob."
verses.50:25: And Joseph made the sons of Israel swear, saying, "Surely God will attend to you, and you must bring up my bones from here."
verses.50:26: Joseph died at a hundred and ten years of age; they embalmed him, and he was placed in a coffin in Egypt.

notes.1:1: The Hebrew has the plural hashamayim, so "the heavens" (contrast the Greek and Latin singular); the wording follows the locked style policy example.
notes.1:2: Tohu wavohu is a rhyming pair meaning unformed and unfilled, rendered "formless and empty." Ruach can mean wind, breath or spirit; with "of God" and the participle "hovering" (as of a bird over its young, Deut 32:11) it is rendered "the Spirit of God."
notes.1:5: The Hebrew says yom echad, literally "day one" or "one day," with a cardinal number; the following days use ordinals ("a second day"), and only the sixth has the article.
notes.1:6: Raqia (from a verb meaning to beat out or spread) is rendered "expanse" throughout.
notes.1:8: Shamayim is rendered "heavens" here to stay consistent with 1:1.
notes.1:16: Hebrew lememsheleth, literally "for the dominion of," is rendered "to govern" here (matching the related verbal infinitive limshol in 1:18).
notes.1:21: Tanninim can mean large sea creatures or sea monsters; "great sea creatures" keeps the plain sense.
notes.1:26: Adam without the article is the collective "humanity"; the plural "Us/Our" is kept as in the Hebrew.
notes.1:27: Ha-adam is followed by the singular pronoun "him" and then the plural "them"; both are kept as in the Hebrew.
notes.1:30: Nefesh chayyah, rendered "living creature" elsewhere, appears here in a relative clause, so it is rendered "a living soul." The verb "I have given" is carried over from 1:29, as the Hebrew implies.
notes.2:2: The Hebrew reads "on the seventh day" in both clauses (contrast the Greek "sixth day" in the first clause). Shabath means to stop or cease, the root of "Sabbath"; "ceased" keeps that sense rather than suggesting tiredness.
notes.2:3: The Hebrew has "which God created to make," which is rendered "had created and made" so that it reads naturally.
notes.2:4: Toledoth ("generations") introduces a new section, as at 5:1 and elsewhere in Genesis. The divine name YHWH first appears here, joined to Elohim, so it is rendered "the LORD God."
notes.2:6: The meaning of ed is uncertain (a mist, or an underground spring or stream); "mist" is the traditional sense.
notes.2:7: There is a wordplay between adam (man) and adamah (ground). Nefesh chayyah is the same phrase used for animals in 1:20, 24, so it is rendered "living creature" to keep the term consistent. Wayyippach means "blew" or "breathed."
notes.2:10: Rashim, literally "heads," is rendered "headstreams," meaning the sources of four rivers.
notes.2:12: Bdellium is an aromatic resin; the identity of the shoham stone is uncertain (onyx or carnelian).
notes.2:14: The Hebrew name is Hiddeqel, which is the Tigris (compare Dan 10:4); Perath is the Euphrates. Ashur is rendered "Assyria."
notes.2:15: Wayyannichehu, from the verb "to rest," means to set down or settle. Leshomrah means "to keep, guard."
notes.2:17: Moth tamuth is an emphatic infinitive construction ("dying you will die"), rendered "you will certainly die."
notes.2:18: Ezer kenegdo is literally "a helper as opposite him," that is, matching or corresponding to him. Ezer implies no lower rank; it is used of God in Ps 33:20.
notes.2:20: Here the Masoretic pointing has le-adam without the definite article (unlike ha-adam earlier in the chapter), marking the first personal-name use "Adam."
notes.2:21: Tsela usually means "side"; the traditional "rib" is kept.
notes.2:23: There is a wordplay between ishah (woman) and ish (man). The Hebrew repeats zoth, "this one," three times, and the repetition is kept.
notes.3:1: Arum ("shrewd") echoes arummim ("naked") in 2:25. The serpent's opening, af ki, expresses surprise or doubt, so it is rendered "Is it really so that."
notes.3:4: The serpent negates God's emphatic phrase from 2:17 (lo moth temuthun), rendered "You certainly will not die."
notes.3:5: Kelohim can mean "like God" or "like gods"; the singular sense fits the reference to God earlier in the verse.
notes.3:6: Lehaskil means to make wise or to give insight.
notes.3:7: Chagoroth are belts or loin coverings.
notes.3:8: Leruach hayyom is literally "at the wind/breeze of the day," probably the cooler evening breeze; the literal phrase is kept.
notes.3:15: Zera ("offspring," literally "seed") is a collective singular, and hu ("he") agrees with it in the masculine. The same verb shuf is used for both actions, so "strike" is used for both; its exact sense (crush, bruise, strike) is debated.
notes.3:16: Itsavon ("pain") is the same word used for the man in 3:17; etsev ("pain") in the next line is from the same root. Harbah arbeh is emphatic: "I will greatly multiply." "Your pain and your conception" may be a hendiadys meaning "your pain in pregnancy."
notes.3:17: Le-adam is pointed without the article, as in 2:20, so it is rendered "Adam." Itsavon ("pain") echoes the woman's sentence in 3:16.
notes.3:20: Chawwah (Eve) sounds like chai, "living"; the Hebrew gives the name itself, not a translation of it.
notes.3:22: The sentence breaks off after pen ("lest"), and the action follows in 3:23; the dash marks this unfinished sentence.
notes.4:1: Hebrew plays on the name Cain (qayin) and the Qal verb qaniti ("I have acquired"). The phrase et-YHWH literally reads "with the LORD," often understood as "with the help of the LORD."
notes.4:7: Hebrew se'et is the Qal infinitive construct of nasa ("lift up"), likely denoting the lifting of a fallen face or acceptance. Although chatta't ("sin") is grammatically feminine, the Qal participle rovets ("crouching") and the following pronouns are masculine, personifying sin as a lurking predator.
notes.4:8: The Masoretic Hebrew uses wayyomer ("said/spoke") without recording any spoken words; ancient versions such as the Septuagint and Samaritan Pentateuch supply "Let us go out to the field."
notes.4:13: Hebrew awon encompasses both guilt/iniquity and its resulting punishment, and minneso (preposition min plus Qal infinitive construct of nasa) can mean either "too great to bear" or "too great to forgive."
notes.4:22: The phrase lotesh kol-choresh (two Qal participles, literally "forging/sharpening every cutting-implement/craftsman") is difficult and is understood either as "forger of every cutting tool" or "sharpener/instructor of every craftsman."
notes.5:1: Hebrew adam serves both as the proper name "Adam" and as the generic noun "man/humankind," creating a wordplay across 5:1-3 where God names male and female together "Man" (adam).
notes.5:3: Literally "and he fathered in his likeness, according to his image"; "a son" is implied by the naming clause that follows. The prepositions be- ("in") and ke- ("according to") appear here in the reverse order of Genesis 1:26.
notes.5:22: In place of the chapter's repeated formula wayehi ("and he lived"), the narrator uses the Hithpael verb wayyithallek ("walked" continually or intimately) for Enoch's life with God here and in 5:24.
notes.5:29: Hebrew yenachamenu is the Piel imperfect of nacham ("comfort"), forming a sound play with the name Noah (noach, linked to nuach, "rest"); the Septuagint instead renders "will give us rest."
notes.6:3: The rare verb yadon, occurring only here in the Masoretic Text, has an uncertain meaning, rendered either 'remain/abide' or, if linked to din, 'contend/strive.' The Masoretic pointing beshaggam parses as 'in that also' ('since he too'), rather than 'in their straying.'
notes.6:13: Hebrew repeats the same root shachat across verses 11-13 and 17—Niphal 'became corrupt' (vv. 11-12), Hiphil 'corrupted' (v. 12) and 'destroy' (v. 13), and Piel 'destroy' (v. 17)—highlighting measure-for-measure judgment.
notes.6:14: Gopher wood is a hapax legomenon naming an unidentified timber species, often conjectured to be cypress or another resinous wood; qinnim literally means 'nests,' here denoting compartments.
notes.6:16: Tsohar occurs in the singular only here and is connected with the root for midday brightness ('opening for light' or skylight), though some interpret it via an Arabic cognate as a 'roof.'
notes.7:2: The distributive expression shivah shivah (lit. 'seven, seven') means 'by sevens,' often understood as seven pairs in light of the following idiom ish we'ishto (lit. 'a man and his wife,' used here for animal mates).
notes.7:4: Hayequm (from qum, 'to stand/exist') denotes 'every existing thing' or living substance; the same term recurs in 7:23.
notes.7:23: The opening verb wayyimach is vocalized as active Qal ('He wiped out,' governing the direct object marker et) with God as implicit subject, followed by the passive Niphal wayyimmachu ('and they were wiped out').
notes.8:13: Verse 13 uses charav ('dried off,' free of standing water), whereas verse 14 uses yavesh ('become dry,' thoroughly desiccated), distinguishing two stages of drying.
notes.8:17: Ketiv reads hotse' (standard contracted Hiphil imperative of yatsa'); Qere reads haytse' (retaining the initial radical yod in the Hiphil imperative). Both forms mean 'bring out.'
notes.8:21: 'Soothing aroma' (reach hannichoach) derives from the root nuach ('to rest'), echoing Noah's name (Noach), the ark coming to rest (wattanach, 8:4), and the dove's 'resting place' (manoach, 8:9).
notes.9:5: Hebrew "et-dimkhem lenafshoteikhem" literally means "your blood belonging to your lives" (that is, lifeblood). The idiom "miyyad ish achiv" (literally "from the hand of a man, his brother") denotes accountability required from any fellow human being.
notes.9:14: Hebrew "be'aneni anan" uses a Piel infinitive construct of the denominative verb "anan" with its cognate noun ("when I cloud a cloud"), meaning "when I gather a cloud."
notes.9:20: The Hebrew wording "vayyachel Noach ish ha'adamah vayyitta karem" (using the Hiphil of "chalal," "begin") is literally "Noah began, a man of the soil, and planted a vineyard." It can be understood either as "began as a man of the soil" or, taking the two verbs together, as "Noah, a man of the soil, was the first to plant a vineyard."
notes.9:21: The verb "vayyitgal" is a Hithpael reflexive form of "galah" ("uncover"), hence "uncovered himself." The final word "oholo" ("his tent") displays the archaic Masoretic spelling with final he ("-oh") rather than vav ("-o").
notes.9:27: The Hiphil jussive "yaft" (from "patah," "be wide" or "spacious") creates a wordplay on the name "Yefet" (Japheth). The subject of "veyishkon" ("may he dwell") is grammatically ambiguous and could refer either to Japheth or to God; likewise the poetic suffix in "lamo" (here and in v. 26) can mean either "to him" or "to them."
notes.10:4: The Masoretic Hebrew reads "Dodanim," whereas the Samaritan Pentateuch, the Septuagint, and most manuscripts of 1 Chronicles 1:7 read "Rodanim" due to the visual similarity of dalet and resh.
notes.10:11: The Hebrew clause "min-ha'arets hahi yatsa Ashur" is grammatically ambiguous: taking "Ashur" as an unmarked accusative of destination yields "he [Nimrod] went into Assyria," whereas taking "Ashur" as the subject yields "Asshur went out from that land."
notes.10:19: Hebrew "bo'akhah" (repeated here and in v. 30) is a Qal infinitive construct of "bo" ("go" or "enter") with an archaic second-person suffix ("your going"), used idiomatically as a directional marker meaning "going toward."
notes.10:21: The construct phrase "achi Yefet haggadol" is syntactically ambiguous in Hebrew and can be read either as "the brother of Japheth the elder" or as "the elder brother of Japheth."
notes.10:25: The name "Peleg" (meaning "division" or "water channel") is linked by wordplay to the Niphal verb "niflegah" ("was divided").
notes.11:1: Hebrew literally reads "one lip" (saphah, idiomatically "language") and "single/unified words" (devarim achadim, plural of echad indicating a uniform set of words).
notes.11:7: The verb "confuse" is a rare Qal cohortative form (navelah, from balal, "to mix/confuse") that prepares the wordplay on "Babel" in v. 9; "understand" translates shama', literally "hear."
notes.11:28: "During the lifetime of Terah his father" renders the Hebrew idiom 'al-peney ("upon the face of"), meaning while his father was still alive (cf. Num 3:4).
notes.11:31: The Masoretic Hebrew reads literally "and they went out with them" (wayyetse'u ittam), rendered idiomatically as "they went out together."
notes.12:2: "And be a blessing" renders a Qal imperative (weheyeh), which following the preceding cohortative and imperfect verbs carries both an exhortative and a consequential force ("so that you will be a blessing").
notes.12:3: Hebrew contrasts plural "those who bless you" with singular "the one who reviles you" (Piel participle of qalal, "treat lightly/disdain/revile"), answered by the stronger verb arar ("curse"). The Niphal verb "will be blessed" (wenivreku) can be read as passive ("be blessed") or middle/reflexive ("find blessing / bless themselves").
notes.12:5: "The persons whom they had acquired" translates literally "the soul that they had made" (hannephesh asher-'asu), using collective singular nephesh for household members or servants and 'asah in the sense of acquiring (cf. Gen 31:1; Deut 8:17).
notes.12:8: The word for "his tent" (here and in 13:3) is written with an archaic final -h spelling for the masculine singular suffix -o; "west" translates Hebrew yam, literally "sea."
notes.13:2: The adjective "wealthy" (kaved) literally means "heavy," creating a verbal echo with the "severe" (kaved) famine in 12:10.
notes.13:10: "As one goes toward Zoar" translates the Hebrew geographic idiom bo'akah ("your coming [to]"), a Qal infinitive construct of bo' with a second-person masculine singular suffix used impersonally.
notes.13:11: Hebrew miqqedem literally means "from the east" or "on the east" (cf. 11:2), and here idiomatically denotes traveling eastward from the hills of Bethel toward the Jordan plain.
notes.13:17: "Walk about" translates the Hithpael imperative of halak (hithhallek), conveying iterative roaming throughout the land as a formal gesture of taking possession.
notes.14:6: Hebrew behareram literally reads "in their mountain/hill country," with a third-person plural possessive suffix, standing in apposition to Seir.
notes.14:14: Hebrew wayyareq (Hiphil of riq, literally "poured out" or "unsheathed," used elsewhere for drawing a sword) is used here idiomatically for mobilizing troops. Hebrew achiv (literally "his brother") denotes a close relative, here Abram's nephew Lot (v. 12).
notes.14:19: Hebrew qoneh (Qal active participle of qanah) carries the dual sense of "Creator" and "Possessor/Owner" (similarly in v. 22).
notes.14:23: The Hebrew conditional particle im ("if") following an oath gesture ("raised my hand," v. 22) introduces an emphatic negative vow ("I will certainly not...").
notes.15:1: Following the Masoretic disjunctive accent on "for you," the final nominal clause ("your reward will be exceedingly great") stands independently; some translations construe it in apposition to "a shield."
notes.15:2: Hebrew ben-mesheq beti contains the hapax legomenon mesheq (likely "acquisition" or "stewardship," hence "heir"), forming a wordplay with Dammeseq ("Damascus") at the end of the verse.
notes.15:6: Hebrew he'emin (Hiphil perfect of aman with simple waw) expresses active trust or belief, and wayyachsheveha carries a feminine singular object suffix referring to that act of trust.
notes.15:9: Hebrew meshulleshet / meshullash (Pual participle of shalash, literally "threefold") is generally understood to mean "three-year-old," though some ancient interpreters took it to mean "three of each."
notes.15:13: Hebrew shifts the subject across two active verbs: va'avadum ("they [the offspring] will serve them") and ve'innu otam ("they [the inhabitants] will afflict them"), rendered passively here for clarity in English.
notes.16:2: Hebrew ibbaneh (Niphal imperfect of banah, "build") literally means "be built up," playing on ben ("son") to express building a family by obtaining children through Hagar.
notes.16:5: In the Masoretic Text, uveynekha ("and you") bears an extraordinary dot (punctum extraordinarium) over the second yod, marking an unusual spelling with an extra yod.
notes.16:9: Hebrew hit'anni (Hithpael imperative of anah, "humble/submit oneself") uses the reflexive stem of the same verb translated "afflicted" in v. 6 and the noun "affliction" in v. 11.
notes.16:12: Hebrew al-peney (literally "upon the face of" or "opposite") carries both a geographical sense ("to the east of") and a relational sense ("in opposition to").
notes.16:13: The Masoretic pointing distinguishes El Ro'i (noun ro'i, "seeing") from ro'i at the end of the verse (Qal active participle with first-person suffix, "Him who sees me"); "seen after Him who sees me" conveys either gazing after God's departing presence or remaining alive to see after encountering Him. In v. 14, Beer-lahai-roi means "Well of the Living One who sees me."
notes.17:1: "God Almighty" translates Hebrew El Shaddai, whose etymology is uncertain (possibly "God of the mountain" or "God of sufficiency"). The verb "walk continually" renders the Hithpael imperative of halakh, expressing habitual conduct.
notes.17:11: The form unemaltem ("you shall circumcise") is analyzed either as a Qal perfect from a by-form namal taking a direct object ("the flesh of your foreskin") or as an unusual Niphal of mul (compare the Niphal with the direct-object marker in 17:14 and 17:25).
notes.17:14: The Masoretic Text has no "on the eighth day" here (found in the Samaritan Pentateuch and Septuagint). The feminine demonstrative pronoun is written h-w-a by Pentateuchal convention and read hi ("that").
notes.17:16: The Masoretic Text consistently uses feminine singular forms ("I will bless her... she will become... from her"), whereas the Septuagint, Syriac, and Vulgate shift to masculine pronouns referring to the promised son.
notes.18:3: The Masoretic Text vocalizes the address as Adonai ("Lord," with qamets, the divine title), whereas verses 4-5 switch to plural verbs and pronouns addressing all three visitors collectively.
notes.18:10: "When the season returns" translates the Hebrew idiom ka'et hayyah (literally "at the living/reviving time," indicating about this time next year; compare 17:21 and 18:14).
notes.18:19: "I have known him" renders the Qal of yada, which in covenantal contexts conveys intimate recognition and election (compare Amos 3:2).
notes.18:21: The Hebrew phrase asu khalah is syntactically difficult; taking kalah adverbially yields "acted altogether" according to the outcry, though elsewhere the phrase means "make a complete end" and a Masoretic paseq divides the two words.
notes.18:22: Traditional rabbinic lists include this clause ("Abraham remained standing before the LORD") among the scribal emendations (tiqqune soferim) for an original wording in which the LORD stood before Abraham; this translation follows the Masoretic Text verbatim.
notes.19:9: The post-positive Qal infinitive absolute in 'keeps acting as judge' (wayyishpot shafot) emphasizes continual or persistent action. The verse also plays on the root ngsh ('step back' ... 'stepped forward').
notes.19:11: The rare plural noun sanwerim ('blindness', occurring only here and 2 Kings 6:18) appears to denote a sudden, disorienting blindness rather than permanent physical loss of sight.
notes.19:18: Although Lot addresses both angels ('to them'), the pausal form Adonai is followed by singular verbs and pronouns in v. 19; it may be understood as honorific singular 'my lord' (addressing the spokesman of v. 17), pausal plural 'my lords', or the divine title 'Lord'.
notes.19:21: Literally 'I have lifted your face', a Hebrew idiom for showing favor or granting a request. In v. 22, the name Zoar (Tsoar) echoes Lot's repeated word 'a small one' (mitsar) in v. 20.
notes.19:33: The Masoretic Text places a scribal dot (punctum extraordinarium) above the letter vav in 'when she got up' (uvequmah), traditionally marking a textual or interpretive question on the form (contrast the shorter spelling without vav in v. 35).
notes.20:6: The form 'from sinning' (mechato) is an unusual Qal infinitive construct of chata ('to sin') spelled without its final silent aleph.
notes.20:13: The Hiphil verb 'caused to wander' (hitu) is grammatically plural in agreement with the plural form of Elohim ('God'), an occasional Hebrew construction (cf. Genesis 35:7) that here also fits Abraham addressing a foreign king.
notes.20:16: The idiom 'a covering of the eyes' (kesut einayim) denotes compensation that removes reproach and prevents suspicion. The final clause (we-et kol wenokachat) pairs the preposition et ('with/before') with a Niphal feminine singular participle of ykach ('vindicated' or 'cleared').
notes.21:2: Hebrew 'oto' is pointed as the direct-object pronoun resuming 'the appointed time' ("which God had spoken of"), though some take it as an alternative form of 'itto' ("with him").
notes.21:9: Hebrew 'metsacheq' is the Piel participle of 'tsachaq' (the same root as Isaac's name and the Qal verb "laugh" in v. 6), with a semantic range covering "laughing," "playing," or "mocking." The Masoretic Text ends with this participle and does not include the Septuagint addition "with Isaac her son."
notes.21:14: Hebrew 'sam al-shikhmah' ("placing on her shoulder") is an asyndetic circumstantial clause interrupting the objects of "gave," so "together with the child" resumes what Abraham handed over to Hagar rather than placing the child on her shoulder.
notes.21:31: The place name Beersheba ('be'er sheva') carries a double wordplay, meaning both "well of seven" (linking to the seven ewe lambs in vv. 28-30) and "well of the oath" (linking to the Niphal verb 'nishbe'u', "swore an oath").
notes.22:8: The idiom 'ra'ah lo' literally means "see for oneself," conveying "see to" or "provide," and introduces the repeated 'ra'ah' ("see") wordplay that culminates in the naming of the site in v. 14.
notes.22:13: The Masoretic Text reads 'achar' ("behind"), rather than the variant 'echad' ("a" or "one") found in the Samaritan Pentateuch, Septuagint, and some Hebrew manuscripts.
notes.22:14: The place name pairs the divine name with 'yir'eh' (Qal imperfect of 'ra'ah', "see," echoing v. 8's idiom "see to/provide"), playing on 'yera'eh' (Niphal imperfect of the same verb), which can mean either "it will be seen to/provided" or "He will be seen/appear."
notes.22:18: Hebrew 'vehithbarekhu' is the Hithpael of 'barakh' (in contrast to the Niphal used in Gen 12:3 and 18:18), which may be understood reflexively ("bless themselves") or as a middle/passive ("obtain blessing / be blessed").
notes.23:6: The phrase "prince of God" (nesi' 'elohim) is translated literally, though in Hebrew it can also serve as a superlative idiom meaning "a mighty prince."
